Once upon a time there was a girl called Mary. Mary was three years old and loved to play. One day Mary was playing in her garden when she heard something. It was a strange noise; Mary had never heard anything like it before. She was a bit scared. 

Mary looked around to see where the noise was coming from and noticed a big hole in the ground. She decided to take a look to see what was inside. When she looked in the hole, it was so quiet; there was only silence.

Cautiously, Mary stepped into the hole and it got darker and darker until she saw a big light. She followed it and as she got closer, she realized it was an old house. Mary was scared but brave! She slowly walked inside.

Once inside, everything seemed so normal. There were toys and furniture that looked like the kind Mary had at home. She explored the house for a long time and eventually felt the courage to come back outside. As she stepped back into the sunshine, the birds sang and the world felt alive again. 

Mary was so happy that she had come. It was an amazing adventure, and she was so glad it had all turned out ok!

Suddenly a policeman appeared from behind a tree. He wore a big helmet and he had a loud voice. He said, "Don't be scared. Come with me and I'll lead you to safety."

Lucy took a deep breath to calm herself and followed the policeman. He led her away from the dog and across a busy street. Finally they made it to a safe place and the policeman gave Lucy a hug.

The policeman gave Lucy a special helmet for when she was playing outside. He said, "This will help you stay safe. From now on, no more being frightened!"

Lucy thanked the policeman and went home with her new helmet. She was so happy and proud of herself for not letting the big dog scare her. Lucy always remembers to wear her helmet when she goes outside now, so she can stay safe.

The baby grew bigger and bigger, just like the kind penguin, and soon both the kind penguin and baby could swim together, play together and waddle around in the snow. The two were very happy. The kind penguin always looked after the baby and would make sure it stayed safe. 

The kind penguin was so loving and kind and soon the two were the best of friends. They would always be together, eating, swimming and playing in the cold but happy place.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Goldilocks. She was so excited. She was told that she could pick whichever dessert she wanted. 

Goldilocks looked over the desserts that were available; there was ice cream, cake, and pudding. She couldn't decide! She wanted it all! 

Goldilocks asked the baker, "Can I have a scoop of each? I want all of them."

The baker laughed, "There is not enough for everyone. You must choose one." 

Goldilocks was so upset. She stamped her feet and cried, "No, I want it all!" 

The baker thought for a minute and then said, "I know! How about I melt the ice cream, cake, and pudding together and you can have just one teaspoon?"

Goldilocks was thrilled! She smiled and said, "Yes, please!"

The baker took the three desserts and melted them together in a bowl. When it was done, Goldilocks tasted it with her teaspoon and found it was the best dessert ever! 

Goldilocks was so happy she had the best dessert that was available!

"Maybe it is sleeping," Sara said.

"Maybe it is sick," Tom said.

They decided to take the bird to their house. They put it in a shoe box with some grass and water. They hoped the bird would wake up and fly away.

But the bird did not wake up. The next day, it was still not moving. Sara and Tom knew the bird was dead. They cried and hugged each other.

"We have to bury the bird," Sara said. "That is what people do when someone dies. They bury them in the ground and say goodbye."

"OK," Tom said. "But where do we bury it?"

They thought for a while. Then they remembered their favorite spot in the garden. It was under a big tree with a swing. They loved to swing and watch the sky.

They took the shoe box and a shovel. They dug a hole under the tree. They put the bird in the hole and covered it with dirt. They said a prayer and thanked the bird for its life.

They made a cross with two sticks and put it on the grave. They picked some flowers and put them on the cross.

"Goodbye, bird," Sara said. "We will miss you."

"Goodbye, bird," Tom said. "We will remember you."

They held hands and walked back to their house. They felt sad, but they also felt happy. They had each other. They were best friends. They were dependable. They knew they would always be there for each other.

Sara and Ben were twins who loved to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a magic wand that could make things shrink or grow. They liked to shrink their dolls and cars and put them in their pockets, or grow their blocks and books and make big forts.

One day, their mom made a beautiful dessert for them. It was a cake with pink frosting and sprinkles. She put it on the table and told them to wait until after dinner. Sara and Ben looked at the cake and their eyes grew big. They wanted to eat it right away.

"Let's use the magic wand to shrink the cake and eat it now," Sara whispered to Ben. "Mom won't notice."

Ben nodded and they sneaked the wand from their room. They pointed it at the cake and said the magic word. The cake became very small, like a cookie. They smiled and picked it up.

But before they could take a bite, they heard their mom coming back. They quickly hid the cake and the wand under a napkin. Mom set the plates and forks on the table and looked at the cake.

"Where is the cake?" she asked, surprised. "I left it right here."

Sara and Ben felt guilty. They knew they had done something bad. They looked at each other and decided to tell the truth.

"Mom, we're sorry," Sara said. "We used the magic wand to shrink the cake and we wanted to eat it."

Mom lifted the napkin and saw the tiny cake. She was not happy. She took the wand and the cake and put them away.

"Sara and Ben, you know you should not use the magic wand without permission. And you should not take the dessert before dinner. That is not nice. You have to wait and share with everyone. Now you have no cake and no wand. How do you feel?"

Sara and Ben felt sad and ashamed. They realized they had been selfish and greedy. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry.

"We feel bad, Mom. We're sorry we took the cake and the wand. We won't do it again. We love you and we love the cake. Can we have some after dinner?"

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She forgave them and said they could have some cake after dinner, but only a small piece. She also said they could have the wand back tomorrow, but only if they promised to use it wisely and kindly.

Sara and Ben agreed and thanked their mom. They learned their lesson and never tried to shrink the dessert again. They also learned to be patient and grateful for what they had. They enjoyed their dinner and their cake, and played with their toys happily. They knew that the magic wand was fun, but not as important as their mom and their love.

On the way to Lily's friend's house, they met a big, mean train named Max who blocked the tracks. Max said, "You can't go this way, Tom!" Tom was sad, but he was also smart. He said, "If we work together, we can both go on the tracks and help people." Max thought about it and agreed.

Tom and Max became friends and worked together to help people. Lily was happy to reach her friend's house, and everyone loved the smart train Tom and his new friend Max.

The rabbit had an idea. He told the bear to follow him. They walked together and soon found bear's home. The scared bear was happy to be home. He thanked the rabbit and they became good friends. From that day on, they played together in the forest and the bear was never scared again.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play near the river. They knew they had to be careful and not go too close to the water, because their mom and dad told them so. But one day, they saw a big, shiny rock on the other side of the river. They wanted to touch it and see if it was smooth or rough.

"Let's go get the rock!" Ben said.

"No, we can't. It's too far and the river is too fast. We have to remain here," Lily said.

"But it's so pretty! Maybe it's a magic rock. Come on, it will be fun!" Ben said.

He did not listen to Lily and ran towards the river. He tried to jump over it, but he slipped and fell into the water. He screamed and splashed, but the river was too strong and carried him away.

Lily was very scared and sad. She ran to get help from their mom and dad, who were nearby. They heard her cry and followed her to the river. They saw Ben floating away and quickly got a long stick. They reached out to Ben and pulled him out of the river. He was wet and cold and crying.

"Ben, you were very naughty! You could have drowned in the river! Why did you not listen to Lily and remain here?" their mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted the rock. I thought it was magic," Ben said.

"It's not magic, it's just a rock. And it's not worth risking your life for. You have to be more careful and obey us. We love you and we don't want you to get hurt," their dad said.

They hugged Ben and Lily and took them home. They gave them warm clothes and soup and cuddled them on the couch. Ben and Lily learned their lesson and never went near the river again without their parents. They also said sorry to each other and promised to be good twins.

"Maybe, if the water is not too cold," Dad said.

"Maybe, if we are quiet and lucky," Mom said.

Sara and Ben hoped to see some animals. They liked animals, especially hairy ones. They had a dog at home, but he was too old to come with them. They missed him a lot.

"I want this one!" Sara said, pointing to a bed with a pink quilt.

"I want this one!" Ben said, pointing to a bed with a blue quilt.

Benny was a big dog who liked to run and play. He had a lot of fur that was soft and brown. He had a friend named Fifi, who was a small dog who liked to bark and jump. She had a lot of fur that was white and curly.

One day, Benny and Fifi went to the park with their owners. They saw a lot of other dogs and people. They had fun chasing balls and sticks and each other. But then, Benny felt something itchy on his back. He scratched and scratched, but it did not go away. He looked and saw a tiny bug on his fur. It was a flea.

"Hey, Fifi, look at this!" Benny said. "I have a flea on me. It is making me itch. How do I get rid of it?"

Fifi came closer and looked at the flea. She said, "That is a bad flea. It is biting you and making you hurt. You need to close your mouth and snap at it. That will make it go away."

Benny did what Fifi said. He closed his mouth and snapped at the flea. But he missed. The flea was too fast and too small. It jumped to another spot on his fur. Benny tried again and again, but he could not catch the flea. He got more and more itchy and more and more grumpy.

"Stop it, Benny!" Fifi said. "You are making too much noise and too much fuss. You are scaring the other dogs and people. You are being silly. The flea is not that bad. Just ignore it. It will go away by itself."

Benny did not like what Fifi said. He thought she was being mean and rude. He said, "No, Fifi, you are wrong. The flea is very bad. It is making me miserable. You do not understand. You do not have a flea on you. You are lucky. You are not my friend. Go away."

Fifi was hurt by what Benny said. She thought he was being unfair and unkind. She said, "Fine, Benny, if that is how you feel. I was only trying to help you. You are not my friend either. Go away."

And so, Benny and Fifi went their separate ways. They did not play or talk to each other for the rest of the day. They were both sad and lonely. They wished they had not fought over a flea. They wished they had been nicer to each other. They wished they were friends again.

Tommy likes to watch the birds in the park. He likes their colors and their songs. He wants to have a bird as a friend. One day, he finds a birdcage in the trash. He thinks it is a good home for a bird. He takes it to his room and cleans it.

The next day, he goes to the park with the birdcage. He sees a friendly bird on a tree. He calls to the bird and offers some seeds. The bird flies down and eats the seeds. Tommy is happy. He opens the birdcage and puts the bird inside. He closes the door and carries the birdcage home.

He puts the birdcage on his window sill. He talks to the bird and gives it more seeds and water. He names the bird Sunny. Sunny chirps back and flaps its wings. Tommy thinks Sunny is happy too.

But after a few days, Tommy notices that Sunny is not so cheerful. Sunny does not eat much or sing much. Sunny looks sad and lonely. Tommy wonders why.

One morning, Tommy hears a knock on his window. He sees another bird outside. The bird looks like Sunny. It pecks at the glass and calls to Sunny. Sunny perks up and answers. Tommy realizes that the bird is Sunny's friend. He feels sorry for Sunny.

He opens the window and the birdcage. He says to Sunny, "You can go with your friend. You belong in the sky, not in a cage. I will miss you, but I want you to be happy." Sunny hops out of the cage and joins the other bird. They fly away together. Tommy waves goodbye and smiles. He still likes birds, but he knows they are not his pets. He decides to make friends with other children instead.

One day, Tom and Lily wanted to play a game. They looked for something fun in their room. They saw their mom's bathrobe. It was big and soft and pink.

"Let's pretend we are superheroes!" Tom said. He put the bathrobe on and tied it around his neck. He felt strong and brave.

"I want to be a superhero too!" Lily said. She grabbed the other end of the bathrobe and pulled it. Tom did not want to share. He pulled back. They both fell on the floor.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Lily on the floor with her bathrobe. She was not happy.

"What are you doing with my bathrobe?" she asked. "You could have ripped it or stained it!"

Tom and Lily felt sorry. They did not mean to hurt the bathrobe. They just wanted to have fun.

"We were playing superheroes, mom," Tom said. "The bathrobe was our cape. It was harmless."

Mom sighed. She knew they were not bad kids. They were just curious and creative. She smiled and hugged them.

"I'm glad you have a big imagination, but you need to ask before you use my things," she said. "Now, why don't you get your own capes and play outside? It's a sunny day."

Tom and Lily nodded. They said sorry to mom and thanked her. They got their own capes from their closet. They were old towels with stickers on them. They ran outside and played superheroes. They had a lot of fun. Mom watched them from the window and smiled. She loved her kids.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to walk in the park and look at the sky. The sky is blue and has white clouds. Sometimes they see birds and planes.

One day, they walk to the pond. They see ducks and fish. Lily wants to feed the ducks. She has some bread in her bag. She takes out a piece and throws it to the ducks.

But Ben is hungry. He sees the bread and wants some too. He grabs the bag from Lily and opens it. He takes out another piece and eats it.

Lily is angry. She says, "Ben, that is not nice! That is my bread! Give it back!"

Ben says, "No, I want it! It is yummy!"

They start to pull the bag. The bag rips. The bread falls out. The ducks come and eat the bread.

Lily and Ben are sad. They have no bread left. They look at the ducks. The ducks are happy.

Lily says, "Ben, I am sorry. I should have shared my bread with you."

Ben says, "Lily, I am sorry too. I should not have taken your bread. You are my friend."

They hug. They say, "We are sorry, ducks. We hope you enjoy the bread."

The ducks quack. They say, "Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are kind."

Lily and Ben smile. They walk back to the park. They look at the sky. The sky is still blue and has white clouds. They are happy.

One day, Jen has an idea. She asks Tom, "Can we race to the big tree today?" Tom says, "Yes, that is easy. I will win again." Jen smiles. She knows something that Tom does not know.

They start the race. Tom runs very fast. Jen runs slowly. Tom is far ahead of Jen. He thinks he will win. He does not see the big hill before the big tree. He gets tired and slows down. Jen is patient. She keeps running slowly. She sees the big hill. She runs up the hill. She passes Tom. She reaches the big tree first. She wins the race. She is happy.

Tom is surprised. He says, "How did you do that? You are slow." Jen says, "I am slow, but I am smart. I knew there was a big hill. I saved my energy. You ran too fast. You got tired. I succeeded. I won the race." Tom says, "You are right. You are smart. You are a good friend. Can we race again tomorrow?" Jen says, "Yes, we can race again tomorrow. But you have to be patient. Maybe you will win next time." They hug and laugh. They are still friends.

One day, she found a new marble in her box. It was very big and shiny. It had swirls of blue and green and yellow. It looked like a rainbow. Anna wondered where it came from. She had never seen it before. It was mysterious.

She picked it up and held it in her hand. It felt smooth and cool. She brought it close to her face and looked at it. It sparkled in the light. She wondered what it would taste like. She opened her mouth and put it in.

It tasted very bad. It was hard and bitter and sour. Anna spat it out and made a face. She did not like the taste of the marble. She decided it was not candy. She put it back in the box and looked for another marble. She hoped it would taste better.

Lily and Ben were playing in the big house. They liked to run and jump and hide. But they did not like the dark and scary basement. Mommy and Daddy told them to never go down the stairs to the basement. They said there were terrible things there that could hurt them.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Ben. She looked in the kitchen, the living room, the bedroom, but she could not find him. She heard a noise from the basement door. She ran to the door and opened it. She saw Ben on the stairs. He was holding a flashlight and a toy sword. He looked at Lily and smiled.

"Ben, what are you doing?" Lily asked. "You know we are not allowed to go to the basement. Mommy and Daddy warned us. It is dangerous and terrible."

Ben shook his head. "No, it is not. It is fun and exciting. I want to see what is down there. Maybe there are dragons or pirates or treasures. Come with me, Lily. Don't be scared."

Lily felt scared. She did not want to go to the basement. She wanted to go back to the big house. She grabbed Ben's hand and tried to pull him up. "No, Ben, no. We have to go back. Mommy and Daddy will be angry. And we could get hurt. Please, Ben, please."

But Ben did not listen. He pulled his hand away and ran down the stairs. He shouted, "Come on, Lily. Don't be a baby. It will be fun."

Lily did not follow him. She stayed on the top of the stairs. She cried and called for Mommy and Daddy. She hoped they would come soon and save Ben from the terrible things in the basement. She hoped Ben would be okay. She wished he had listened to her warning.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and building towers. But soon, they started to feel tired. They yawned and rubbed their eyes.

"Are you sleepy, Ben?" Lily asked.

"A little bit," Ben said. "But I don't want to stop playing."

"Me too," Lily said. "But maybe we should take a nap. Mommy said naps are good for us."

They looked at each other and nodded. They put their toys away and went to their bedroom. They climbed into their beds and pulled the blankets over them.

But they did not fall asleep right away. They whispered and giggled and told each other stories. They did not hear Mommy coming upstairs.

Mommy opened the door and saw them awake. She frowned and said, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? You should be sleeping. It's nap time."

Lily and Ben felt guilty. They knew they were not supposed to be talking. They looked at Mommy with big eyes and said, "Sorry, Mommy."

Mommy smiled and said, "It's okay. I know you were having fun. But now it's time to rest. You need to be fresh and happy for the afternoon."

She kissed them on their foreheads and said, "I love you, sweeties. Sleep well."

She turned off the light and closed the door. Lily and Ben snuggled in their beds and closed their eyes. They yawned and said, "I love you, too, Mommy."

They fell asleep and dreamed of more toys and games.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the garden and look for bugs and flowers. One day, they found a big bean plant with many green beans. They picked some beans and put them in a basket.

"Look, Lily, these beans are new and shiny. We can eat them for lunch," Tom said.

"Or we can make a necklace with them. See, they have holes in them. We can use a string and tie them together," Lily said.

"Lily, you are my best friend. Do you want to marry me?" Tom asked.

"Yes, Tom, I do. You are my best friend too. Let's marry," Lily said.

They hugged and kissed. Then they ran to the house to show their parents their bean necklaces and tell them their news.

"Really? That's very sweet. But you are very young. You have to wait until you are older to marry," Mom said.

"But we love each other. And we have bean necklaces. See?" Tom said.

"Okay. But we still want to marry. Maybe when we are four," Lily said.

"Maybe. We'll see. Now go and have fun," Mom said.

Lily and Tom ran back to the garden. They played with their bean necklaces and pretended to be married. They were happy and had a lot of fun.

Poppy was a small dog who liked to sleep a lot. He slept on the sofa, on the bed, on the rug, and sometimes even in the garden. He had a big family who loved him and gave him food and toys and hugs.

One day, Poppy was sleeping on the sofa when he heard a loud noise outside. He opened his eyes and saw a big truck in front of the house. The truck had a long arm that grabbed the sofa and lifted it up. Poppy was scared and barked.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "I don't want to go with the truck!"

His family heard him and ran outside. They saw Poppy on the sofa in the air and shouted.

"Stop! Stop!" they yelled. "That's our sofa and our dog!"

The truck driver heard them and stopped the arm. He looked at the sofa and saw Poppy. He was surprised and sorry.

"Oh, I'm sorry!" he said. "I didn't see the dog. I thought this was an old sofa that you wanted to throw away."

He lowered the arm and put the sofa back on the ground. Poppy jumped off the sofa and ran to his family. They hugged him and kissed him and told him he was safe.

"Thank you for saving me!" Poppy said. "That was very dangerous!"

The truck driver apologized again and drove away. Poppy and his family went back inside the house. Poppy was tired and shaken from his adventure. He decided to sleep on the bed instead of the sofa. He curled up and closed his eyes. He dreamed of happy things and forgot about the truck. He was a lucky dog.

Tom and Anna are twins. They like to go out with Mom and Dad. Today, they go to a restaurant. It is a big place with many tables and chairs. They see many foods and drinks.

Tom and Anna sit next to each other. They have pizza and juice. They are happy. They talk and laugh. Mom and Dad smile.

"No, it is mine. You have your own pizza," Anna says.

"No, it is not fair. You always want my things," Anna says.

Tom is sad. He looks at his pizza. He does not want it anymore. He puts it on the edge of the table. He does not see the cat.

The cat is hungry. It smells the pizza. It jumps on the table. It grabs the pizza with its mouth. It runs away.

Tom sees the cat. He cries. He has no pizza. He is hungry.

"Mom, Dad, the cat took my pizza!" Tom says.

Mom and Dad look at the cat. They are surprised. They feel sorry for Tom.

"Can I have some of Anna's pizza?" Tom asks.

Anna looks at Tom. She sees his tears. She feels sorry for him too.

"OK, Tom. You can have some of my pizza. It is fair. We are twins. We share," Anna says.

She gives him a slice of her pizza. He smiles. He thanks her. He eats the pizza. He is happy.

They hug each other. Mom and Dad hug them too. They are a happy family. They finish their meal. They leave the restaurant. They do not see the cat. The cat is full. It sleeps under a tree.

"But I want to pet him," Ben said. He tried to climb over the fence.

"Ben, stop!" mom said. "You are not allowed to go over the fence. That is dangerous. The kangaroo might get scared and kick you. You have to stay with me and Sara."

Ben was sad. He wanted to be friends with the baby kangaroo. He looked at him with big eyes.

The baby kangaroo looked back at Ben. He saw that Ben was not mean. He was just curious. He poked his head out of his mom's pouch. He made a soft noise.

"Look, mom, he likes me!" Ben said. He smiled.

"Maybe he does," mom said. "But you still have to respect his space. You can wave to him and say hello, but you can't touch him. OK?"

"OK, mom," Ben said. He waved to the baby kangaroo and said, "Hello, little one. You are very cute. I hope you have a nice day."

The baby kangaroo waved back with his paw. He was happy. He had a new friend.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a big doll that looked like a princess. Max had a small car that he zoomed around the floor.

"Look at my princess, she is so pretty and tall!" Lily said, holding her doll up.

"My car is faster and cooler than your princess!" Max said, driving his car near Lily's doll.

They started to argue about whose toy was better. They did not hear their mom calling them for dinner.

"Kids, dinner is ready! Come to the kitchen now!" Mom said.

Lily and Max ignored her. They kept fighting over their toys.

"Your princess is too big, she takes up all the space!" Max said, pushing Lily's doll away.

"Your car is too small, I can't even see it!" Lily said, kicking Max's car.

Suddenly, something strange happened. Lily and Max felt a tickle in their bellies. They looked at each other and gasped. They were shrinking!

They became smaller and smaller, until they were the same size as their toys. Their toys looked huge and scary. They felt scared and lost.

"Mom! Mom! Help us!" they cried.

Mom heard their tiny voices. She came to the living room and saw them on the floor, next to their toys.

"Oh no, what happened to you?" she asked, picking them up gently.

"We don't know, we were playing and then we shrank!" Lily said.

"We're sorry, Mom, we didn't listen to you!" Max said.

Mom hugged them and kissed them. She said, "Don't worry, I know how to fix this. You need to eat your dinner. It will make you grow back to normal."

She carried them to the kitchen and put them on the table. She gave them each a spoon and a plate of food. The food looked big and yummy.

"Here, eat this. It's good for you." Mom said.

Lily and Max ate their dinner. They felt the tickle in their bellies again. They looked at each other and smiled. They were growing!

They became bigger and bigger, until they were the same size as before. They felt happy and relieved.

"Thank you, Mom, we love you!" they said, hugging Mom.

"You're welcome, I love you too. But next time, please listen to me when I call you for dinner. And don't fight over your toys. They are just toys. You are more important." Mom said.

Lily and Max nodded. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We won't fight anymore. We'll share our toys and play nicely."

They finished their dinner and cleaned up their toys. They gave their toys a kiss and put them away. They went to bed with a smile on their faces. They had learned a lesson. They never shrank again.

"You're welcome, sweetie," her mom said. She kissed her on the cheek and put her down. "But it's time for bed now. You can read your book tomorrow."

"But I want to read now," Lily said. She pouted and looked at her book.

"I know, honey, but reading in the dark is not good for your eyes. And you need to sleep to grow and learn. How about I read you a story instead?" her mom said.

"Okay," Lily said. She nodded and crawled back into her bed. She picked a story book from her shelf and handed it to her mom.

Her mom sat on the edge of the bed and opened the book. She read the story in a soft voice, while Lily listened and looked at the pictures. The lamp gave a warm light, not a harsh one. Lily felt cozy and happy. She closed her eyes and drifted into a dream.

Lily was playing with her dolls in the garden. She liked to make them talk and have tea parties. She saw a big dog walking on the street. He was brown and fluffy, but he looked smelly and hungry. Lily felt sorry for him. She wanted to invite him to her tea party.

She ran to the gate and called out, "Hello, doggy! Do you want to play with me and my dolls? I have cookies and juice for you." The dog stopped and looked at her. He wagged his tail and barked. He seemed friendly, but he was a stranger. Lily did not know him.

Lily's mom was watching from the window. She saw Lily talking to the dog. She felt worried. She knew that some dogs could be mean or bite. She did not want Lily to get hurt. She ran outside and said, "Lily, come here! You should not talk to strangers, even if they are dogs. You don't know if they are nice or not."

Lily looked at her mom and said, "But mom, he is so cute and lonely. He wants to join my tea party. Can I invite him, please?" She pointed at the dog, who was still waiting at the gate.

Lily's mom shook her head and said, "No, honey, you can't. He might be smelly and dirty. He might have fleas or germs. He might knock over your dolls or eat your cookies. He might not listen to you or share. He is not a good guest for your tea party. You should only invite your friends or people you know."

Lily felt sad and disappointed. She wanted to be nice to the dog. She said, "But mom, he is not a bad dog. He is just a sad dog. He needs a friend. Maybe he could be my friend." She looked at the dog with big eyes.

Lily's mom sighed and said, "Lily, I know you are a kind and sweet girl. But you have to be careful with strangers, even if they are animals. They might not be what they seem. Maybe the dog has an owner who is looking for him. Maybe he is not sad, but angry or scared. Maybe he is not a dog at all, but a wolf in disguise." She smiled and said, "Why don't you invite someone else to your tea party? How about your neighbor, Ben? He likes to play with dolls, too. And he is not smelly or hungry. He is a good friend for you."

Lily thought about it and said, "OK, mom. I will invite Ben. He is fun and nice. He will like my tea party." She waved goodbye to the dog and said, "Sorry, doggy. Maybe another time. Bye-bye." She ran inside to get the phone and call Ben.

The dog watched Lily go. He was not a dog, but a wolf in disguise. He had a plan to trick Lily and eat her and her dolls. He was angry and hungry. He did not like cookies or juice. He did not want to play or share. He wanted to bite and chew. He had a bad smile and sharp teeth. He was a bad stranger. But he was too late. Lily's mom had saved her. He had to find another prey. He howled and ran away.

Lily feels sad and angry. She does not like Ben's trumpet. She thinks it is noisy and rude. She decides to teach Ben a lesson. She waits until Ben is not looking, and then she runs to the bench and grabs his trumpet. She runs away with it, laughing.

"Hey, give it back!" Ben shouts. He chases after Lily, but she is faster. He feels scared and mad. He loves his trumpet. He does not want to lose it.

Lily runs to the other side of the park, where there is a pond. She sees some ducks swimming in the water. She thinks it would be funny to throw Ben's trumpet in the pond. She says, "Bye-bye, trumpet. Go and play with the ducks."

She tosses the trumpet in the air, but she does not aim well. The trumpet does not land in the pond. It lands on the head of a big man who is sitting on a bench. The man is startled and angry. He stands up and yells, "Who did this? Who threw this trumpet at me?"

Lily is scared. She did not mean to hit the man. She runs away, leaving the trumpet behind. Ben sees what happened. He runs to the man and says, "I'm sorry, sir. That is my trumpet. My sister took it from me. She was trying to throw it in the pond."

The man looks at Ben and sees his blue trumpet. He sees that Ben is sorry and scared. He feels sorry for him too. He says, "It's okay, kid. I'm not hurt. But you should be more careful with your trumpet. It is not a toy. It is a musical instrument. You should respect it and play it nicely."

He gives Ben his trumpet back. Ben says, "Thank you, sir. I will. I'm sorry for the trouble."

He hugs his trumpet and walks back to his mom and sister. He decides to play with his trumpet more quietly and kindly. He also decides to play with Lily on the slide sometimes. He learns that his trumpet is not the only thing that is fun. He learns to share and care.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees and grass. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a castle or a dragon!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Mom said not to go too far or get dirty."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They were happy and excited. They reached the top and looked around.

"Wow!" Ben said. "Look at that!"

He pointed to a big, wet, green place. It had a lot of water and mud and plants and animals. It looked like a different world.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I think it's a swamp," Ben said. "I read about it in a book. It's a place where frogs and snakes and bugs live. Do you want to go and see?"

Lily was not sure. She thought the swamp looked scary and dirty. She remembered what Mom said.

"I don't know, Ben," she said. "It looks too far and too messy. Maybe we should go back."

But Ben was curious and persistent. He wanted to see the swamp. He wanted to hear the frogs and touch the plants and find the bugs.

"Come on, Lily," he said. "It will be fun. We can rush and be back before Mom knows. Please, please, please!"

He pulled Lily's hand and ran down the hill. Lily tried to stop him, but he was too fast and strong. She followed him, feeling scared and worried. She hoped they would not get lost or hurt or in trouble.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

But then they saw a black and white bird walking towards them. It was a penguin. The penguin was very nosy. It wanted to see what the children were doing. It waddled closer and closer to the snowman.

"Hello, penguin!" Lily said. "Do you like our snowman?"

The penguin nodded. It liked the snowman very much. It liked the carrot nose and the buttons. It wanted to touch them. It reached out with its flipper and poked the snowman's nose.

"Hey, don't do that!" Ben said. "That's our snowman's nose. You can't take it."

The penguin did not listen. It pulled the carrot out of the snowman's face. It held it in its mouth. It looked very happy.

"Give it back, penguin!" Lily said. "That's not nice. That's not yours."

The penguin did not listen. It ran away with the carrot. It was very fast. The children chased after it. They wanted their snowman's nose back.

They ran and ran until they reached a big hill. The penguin slid down the hill on its belly. It was very fun. The children slid down the hill too. They were very brave.

They caught up with the penguin at the bottom of the hill. The penguin saw them and stopped. It looked at them with its big eyes. It felt sorry. It dropped the carrot on the ground. It made a soft sound.

"I'm sorry, children," the penguin said. "I was very nosy. I just wanted to see your snowman. He was very nice. Can we be friends?"

The children looked at the penguin. They looked at the carrot. They looked at each other. They smiled.

"OK, penguin," Lily said. "We can be friends. But you have to promise not to take our snowman's nose again."

"I promise," the penguin said. "Can I help you fix your snowman?"

"Sure," Ben said. "That would be very nice of you."

The children and the penguin went back to the snowman. They put the carrot back in his face. They gave him a hug. They settled down next to him. They were very happy. They had a new friend.

Lily liked to play with her dolls in her big room. She had many dolls and clothes and toys. She was a wealthy girl, but she was not happy. She wanted a friend to play with.

One day, a new girl moved in next door. Her name was Anna. She had only one doll and a few clothes and toys. She was not wealthy, but she was happy. She liked to play outside and make new friends.

Lily saw Anna playing in her yard. She wanted to talk to her, but she was shy. She decided to offer her a gift. She picked her favorite doll, the one with the velvet dress and the shiny hair. She put it in a box and wrapped it with a ribbon.

She walked to Anna's door and knocked. Anna opened the door and smiled. "Hi, I'm Anna. Do you want to play with me?" she asked.

Lily held out the box and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. This is for you. It's my favorite doll. I want to be your friend."

Anna looked at the box and then at Lily. She was surprised and touched. She said, "Thank you, Lily. That's very kind of you. But I can't accept your gift. It's too much. You should keep your favorite doll. I have my own doll. She's not as pretty as yours, but I love her very much. She's my friend."

Lily felt sad and confused. She thought Anna would like her gift and her friendship. She said, "But I have many dolls. I don't need them all. I want you to have this one. Please, take it."

Anna shook her head and said, "No, Lily. I don't need many dolls. I need a real friend. A friend who will play with me and share with me and have fun with me. A friend who will like me for who I am, not for what I have. Do you want to be that friend?"

Lily thought for a moment. She realized that Anna was right. She didn't need many dolls. She needed a real friend. She smiled and said, "Yes, Anna. I want to be that friend. I'm sorry for offering you my doll. I was trying to be nice, but I was also trying to impress you. Can we start over?"

Anna smiled back and said, "Of course, Lily. I'm sorry for refusing your gift. I was trying to be honest, but I was also trying to protect myself. Can we be friends?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, Anna. We can be friends."

They hugged and then went to play together. They shared their dolls and clothes and toys. They had a lot of fun. They became the best of friends.

Anna likes to write poems. She writes them on paper with her crayons. She writes about flowers, stars, and her cat. She thinks her poems are powerful. She wants to share them with her friends.

But her friends do not like her poems. They say they are silly and boring. They laugh at her and tear her paper. They tell her to stop writing poems and play with them.

Anna is sad and angry. She refuses to play with them. She says they are mean and rude. She runs away to her room. She takes her crayons and her paper. She writes more poems. She says they are her only friends.

Her mom comes to her room. She sees Anna crying and writing. She asks her what is wrong. She tries to hug her and comfort her. She tells her that her poems are beautiful and that she is proud of her.

But Anna does not listen to her mom. She pushes her away. She refuses to talk to her. She says she does not need her mom. She says she only needs her poems. She says her poems are powerful and they will protect her.

Her mom is worried and sad. She does not know what to do. She leaves Anna alone in her room. She hopes that Anna will calm down and come out soon.

But Anna does not come out. She stays in her room all day and all night. She writes more and more poems. She fills her paper with words. She says her poems are powerful and they will make her happy.

But her poems do not make her happy. They make her lonely and scared. They fill her head with strange and dark thoughts. They make her forget about her mom, her friends, and her cat. They make her forget about herself.

She writes one last poem. She says it is the most powerful poem of all. She says it will make her free. She says goodbye to her poems. She says goodbye to the world.

She tears her paper into pieces. She throws them in the air. She watches them fall like snow. She closes her eyes. She stops breathing.

"Yes, we can!" Tom and Anna said.

"Thank you, children," the man said. "You are very helpful. You can keep one toy each as a reward. Which one do you want?"

Tom chose the saw. He liked to make things. Anna chose the robot. She liked to learn new words.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. Some cars are big and some cars are small. Some cars are fast and some cars are slow.

One day, Tom and Mia go to the park with their cars. They find a big hill. They want to see which car can zoom down the hill the fastest. They take turns to put their cars on top of the hill and let them go.

"Look at my red car!" Tom says. "It is very fast and shiny. It can zoom faster than any other car."

"No, look at my yellow car!" Mia says. "It is very bright and pretty. It can zoom faster than your red car."

They put their cars on the hill and let them go. The cars zoom down the hill very fast. They make loud noises. They look like rockets.

But then, something happens. The sun is very hot and bright. It shines on the cars. The cars get very hot. The cars start to melt. The red car and the yellow car become a big puddle of orange.

"Oh no!" Tom and Mia say. "Our cars are gone! They are melted by the sun!"

They are very sad. They cry. They hug each other.

A man sees them. He is very rich. He has a lot of money. He feels sorry for them. He comes to them.

"Hello, little ones," he says. "Why are you crying?"

"Our cars are melted by the sun!" Tom and Mia say.

"That is very sad," the man says. "But don't worry. I have a gift for you. I have a new car for you. It is very big and very fast. It can zoom faster than any other car. And it will not melt by the sun. Do you want it?"

Tom and Mia look at the man. They look at the new car. It is very big and very fast. It is blue and silver. It has four doors and four wheels. It has a horn and a radio. It looks like a dream.

"Yes, please!" Tom and Mia say.

The man smiles. He gives them the keys. He helps them get in the car. He tells them to be careful and have fun.

Tom and Mia are very happy. They thank the man. They start the car. They zoom away. They laugh. They sing. They forget about their melted cars. They have a new car. A big and fast car. A blue and silver car. A car that will not melt by the sun. A car that is a dream.

One day, they see a big truck with many tires. They want to count the tires, but they are too high. They ask the truck driver if they can climb on the truck. The truck driver says yes, but be careful. The tires are rough and dirty.

Ben and Lily climb on the truck. They touch the tires and feel the rough bumps. They start to count the tires. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. They count ten tires on one side of the truck. They are happy and clap their hands.

They want to count the tires on the other side of the truck, but they are tired. They climb down from the truck and say thank you to the truck driver. They go back to the swing and the slide. They have fun in the park. They like to count, but they also like to rest.

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks. Ben and Lily liked the ducks. They wanted to feed them bread.

"Can we feed the ducks, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Some ducks are not nice. They might bite you," Mom said.

Ben and Lily took some bread from Mom and walked to the pond. They saw a big duck with no feathers on its head. It was a bald duck. Ben and Lily thought it was funny.

"Look at that duck, Lily. It has no hair. It is a bald duck," Ben said.

"Ha ha, it is a bald duck. It looks silly," Lily said.

They threw some bread to the bald duck. The bald duck ate the bread. It wanted more. It came closer to Ben and Lily. It opened its mouth. It had sharp teeth.

"More bread, more bread," the bald duck quacked.

Ben and Lily were scared. They had no more bread. They tried to run away. But the bald duck was faster. It caught Ben and Lily. It bit them hard.

"Help, help, Mom!" Ben and Lily cried.

Mom heard them. She ran to the pond. She saw the bald duck. It was a bad duck. It was not a duck at all. It was a goose. A mean goose.

Mom grabbed a stick. She hit the goose. She made it let go of Ben and Lily. She took them in her arms. She hugged them.

"Are you okay, Ben and Lily?" Mom asked.

"No, Mom. The bald duck hurt us. It was a bad duck. It was a goose," Ben and Lily said.

Mom looked at their wounds. They were bleeding. They needed a doctor.

"Come on, Ben and Lily. We have to go to the hospital. The goose gave you a bad bite. You need a bandage and a shot," Mom said.

Ben and Lily did not like the hospital. They did not like the bandage and the shot. They cried a lot. They wished they never fed the bald duck. They learned a lesson. They never went near the pond again. The end.

Anna and Ben felt better and thanked the lady. They learned a lesson. They should not play too far from home and they should be careful of wild animals. They also learned that the log was not a dragon log, but a unique log. They still liked it, but they did not want to see the bear again.

The fire fighters noticed her and put her free. They asked, "Can you help, little bear? See that house? We need help to put out the fire in the house."

Sue clenched her paws, and bravely nodded her head. She could manage this. The fire fighters once again asked, "Are you sure, little bear?" 

Sue replied, "Yes, I love helping! I can manage this!"

The fire fighters beamed. They gave her a big hug and said, "Thank you for your lovely help!" 

Sue smiled. She had managed to help in the emergency and it made her feel really happy. She waved goodbye to the fire fighters and happily went on her way.

Once upon a time, there were two little lions who lived in the jungle. The lions were very happy, until one day the little male lion decided to go for a walk. But as soon as he stepped outside, he started to suffer the heat. It was unbearably hot and uncomfortable. 

The little lion stumbled around the jungle, feeling miserable in the sweltering heat. All he wanted was to find some shade, but wherever he looked he only saw sunshine.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. "Do you need help?"

"Yes!" said the little lion. "I'm so hot!"

A monkey appeared from behind a tree and said, "I know a place where you can cool off. Follow me!"

The monkey took the little lion to a tall tree with a big branch hanging over a stream. There the little lion finally found relief from the heat. He sat down, put his feet in the water, and felt the coolness on his fur.

The monkey watched from the branch above. After a while he said, "Would you like a tip from me? Whenever you feel uncomfortable, just come here."

The little lion thanked the monkey and promised to take his advice. From that day on, every time he suffered from the heat, he went to the tall tree. And there he took a dip in the cool stream.

One day, Joe asked his brother "John, why do you have a brain?" John was very surprised but he explained, "the brain helps me to think and understand things." Joe replied "I want to understand things too, can I come inside and learn too?"

John was so happy to hear that Joe wanted to learn and he said "yes, of course you can come in and learn."

So Joe came to join John in the classroom every day and he worked hard to learn. Over time, Joe began to understand and his brain grew stronger.

John was so grateful for Joe's hard work and was proud of how his brother had grown. In the end, he learned that even though people may not be as smart as others, it doesn't mean they can't learn. With hard work and determination, anyone can do whatever they set their mind to.

Once upon a time, there was a patient little dog named Spot. Spot was always kind and gentle.

One day, Spot went to the park with his owner. Spot saw some other dogs playing and he wanted to join in. He asked his owner, "Can I play with them too?" 

His owner said, "Sure! But you must pay attention and be a good patient doggie." 

Spot agreed and ran off to join the other dogs in their fun. But what Spot hadn't noticed was that the other dogs were eating a smelly old bowl of sour milk. Spot took a bite, and it was so sour that he yelped!

The other dogs just laughed and said, "You have to pay for breakfast, doggie!"

Spot ran back to his owner and his owner said, "See, Patience is a virtue! Next time, don't take a bite before you pay attention!" 

Spot nodded and learned his lesson. From then on, he was more patient and paid closer attention to his surroundings.

Once upon a time, there lived a duck called Daisy. One day, Daisy took a step out of her home to find a pond. As Daisy stepped on the grass, she could feel a little water leaking through her feet. 

She looked around and saw a pond in the distance. Excitedly, she started to run towards the pond, but her happy smile turned into a frown when she got closer. The pond was quiet, not full of water like Daisy had hoped. 

Daisy was disappointed and asked, "Where is the water?". Just then, a little frog hopped up and said, "The water is gone, but be careful. If you keep taking steps to places without water, you will eventually run out of places to go."

Daisy thanked the frog for the advice and decided to be more careful. Taking large steps could be dangerous, so from then on, Daisy chose to take smaller, quieter steps and make sure she always had enough water. 

The moral of the story is that it is always good to be careful and think before taking a step.

Finally, he found one of his brave knights, Sir Owen, and asked him what had happened to the crown.

"Well," Sir Owen said, "it looks like a mouse snuck into the castle and stole the crown. He wanted a special hat for himself."

King Henry was very sad, and so he decided to replace his crown with a new one. He searched high and low throughout the kingdom, until he finally found a special crown for himself. It shone brightly and was full of sparkles.

When King Henry returned to the castle wearing his new crown, all his subjects cheered for him. He smiled, for he knew his crown would bring him luck once again.

One sunny day, a little boy named Jack was playing in his garden. He saw a spider spinning a web. It twirled and whirled around very quickly. "Wow, that spider is speeding around!" Jack shouted out in amazement.

He decided to follow the spider and quickly ran along the path. The spider was too fast for him though and he soon lost sight of it. Suddenly, he heard a very loud buzzing noise and saw a clear plane flying up in the sky.

Jack stopped and looked up at the plane with awe. "It's speeding away so fast!" he exclaimed. He kept watching the plane for a few moments before running back home.

He knew he had to tell his family about the plane, which he thought was the same speed as the spider! Even though he couldn't catch the spider, Jack knew that the plane would remember him forever.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf little girl named Jane. Jane was always so curious about the world and the things around her, but she could never quite hear them. One day, she decided to peek out of the window and noticed something strange - a curtain was blowing in the wind.

Jane was so excited. She ran to the window and tried to open the curtain. It moved a little bit, but it was too hard for her to open it. Jane was frustrated, but then she thought of a plan. She gathered some chairs from around the house and used them to sort of climb up to the curtain.

When she was finally tall enough, she reached out and grabbed the curtain. She pulled and it opened a little bit more. Eventually, the curtain was wide open and Jane could see the world outside her window - birds were chirping and trees were swaying in the wind. Jane was amazed and wondered how all of the beautiful things sounded, but she knew that she would never know because she was deaf.

Once upon a time there was a big, fat frog. He loved to kick his big, green, webbed feet. One day, he was kicking by a pond when he heard something by the edge. He hopped over and saw a hook. He hopped closer, but he was too fat to jump on it.

The frog said "What are you doing here, hook?"

The hook replied "I'm here to catch juicy fish!"

The frog said "That sounds like fun! Can I join you?"

So the hook and the frog spent the day together. They tried to catch fish, but they still hadn't been successful. But then the frog had an idea. He said "Let me kick the water and make a splash. The fish might come out to see what's happening."

The hook agreed and the frog began to kick the water in the pond. Sure enough, the fish came out and the hook quickly grabbed one. The frog cheered and they happily enjoyed the fish together.

Luckily, with some quick thinking, he managed to avoid the danger and get back home safe. As soon as he walked through the door, his Mom gave him another cautionary look. She said, "Fine is not always safe. Remember that!"

Jake nodded, understanding now what she had meant before. He promised to always be more careful and never again shrug off the importance of staying safe.

But when they turned on the TV, the picture was fuzzy. Lily's daddy tried to fix it, but it didn't work. Then, Lily remembered something. She rubbed the TV screen with a soft cloth. And just like that, the picture became clear again! Lily was very proud of herself for helping fix the TV.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, Lily's friend Emma hid in a chamber and Lily couldn't find her. 

"Emma, where are you?" Lily called out.

"I'm in the chamber!" Emma replied.

Lily tried to open the chamber, but it was too hard. She needed something flexible to help her open it. 

Just then, Lily's big brother came along. "What's wrong, Lily?" he asked.

"Emma is in the chamber and I can't open it," Lily said.

Her brother found a flexible stick and used it to open the chamber. Emma was very happy to be found and Lily was happy to have her friend back. From that day on, Lily always followed her big brother's advice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she was playing with her friend Jack. They were having fun running around and chasing each other. 

Suddenly, Lily saw her shadow on the ground. She pointed at it and said, "Look, Jack! My shadow is following me!" Jack looked at his own shadow and smiled. "I have a shadow too!" he said. 

After a while, Lily's mom called them inside for a snack. She opened the door and said, "Come on in, kids! I have some yummy cookies for you to enjoy." Lily and Jack ran inside and sat down at the table. They took a bite of the cookies and smiled. "These are delicious!" they said. 

As they finished their snack, Lily's mom asked, "Did you have fun playing outside?" Lily and Jack nodded their heads and said, "Yes, we had so much fun! We loved playing with our shadows."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was always hungry and his mom would make him delicious meals every day. One day, Timmy saw his dad chopping wood with an axe. Timmy asked his dad if he could try to chop wood with the axe too.

His dad said, "No, Timmy, you're too little and the axe is too heavy. You might hurt yourself."

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play cops and robbers. Ben has a toy gun. Sam has a hat. Ben says, "I am the cop. You are the robber. I will catch you." Sam says, "No, you will not. I will run away." They run around the house.

Sam runs into the kitchen. He sees a cake on the table. He thinks, "I want some cake." He stops and takes a bite. Ben sees him and says, "Stop, robber. I have a gun." Sam says, "No, I have cake." He throws some cake at Ben. Ben ducks and shoots his toy gun. Sam laughs and runs away.

Ben follows Sam. He says, "You are a bad robber. You stole the cake." Sam says, "You are a slow cop. You cannot catch me." They run into the living room. They see Mom on the couch. She is reading a book. She says, "What are you doing, boys?" Ben says, "We are playing cops and robbers. I have a gun. He has cake." Mom says, "That sounds fun. But be careful. Do not make a mess."

Sam runs behind the couch. He says, "I have a good hiding place. You cannot find me." Ben says, "Yes, I can. I will look everywhere." He looks under the table, behind the curtains, and in the closet. He cannot find Sam. He says, "Where are you, robber?" Sam says, "I am here." He jumps out from behind the couch and hits Ben with a pillow. Ben falls down and says, "Ow, that hurt."

Sam says, "I win. I am the best robber." Ben says, "No, you are not. You are a cheater. You used a pillow." Sam says, "No, I am not. You used a gun." They start to argue. Mom says, "Boys, boys, calm down. It is just a game. Why don't you share the cake and the gun and the pillow?" Ben and Sam look at each other. They say, "OK, Mom. We are sorry. We love you." They hug Mom and each other. They share the cake and the gun and the pillow. They are happy. They are brothers.

Lily liked to play with her bow. It was pink and shiny and had a ribbon on it. She put it in her hair every day and felt very pretty. But one day, she could not find her bow. She looked in her room, in the bathroom, in the kitchen, but it was not there. She felt sad and restless. She wanted her bow back.

She asked her mom and dad if they had seen her bow, but they said no. They were busy making dinner and told her to keep looking. Lily thought maybe her brother Max had taken her bow. He liked to tease her and hide her things. She went to his room and knocked on the door. He opened it and smiled.

"Hi, Lily. What do you want?" he asked.

"I want my bow. Did you take it?" she asked.

He shook his head. "No, I did not take your bow. Why would I want your silly bow?"

He showed her his room. It was messy and full of toys, but there was no bow. Lily felt more sad and restless. She wanted her bow back.

She left his room and walked down the hall. She saw a flash of pink in the corner of her eye. She turned and saw her bow. It was on the floor, under a table. She ran to it and picked it up. She felt happy and relieved. She had found her bow.

She put it in her hair and smiled. She wondered how it got there. She looked up and saw a picture on the wall. It was of her and Max when they were babies. They were both wearing bows. She remembered that Max used to like bows too, when he was little. She thought maybe he had taken her bow as a joke, but then felt sorry and put it back. She decided to forgive him and share her bow with him. She went to his room and knocked on the door. He opened it and looked surprised.

"Hi, Lily. What do you want?" he asked.

"I want to say sorry for being mad at you. And I want to give you something." she said.

She took off her bow and handed it to him. He looked confused and curious.

"What is this?" he asked.

"It's my bow. You can have it. I know you used to like bows too." she said.

He took the bow and looked at it. He felt a little embarrassed and a little happy. He remembered that he used to like bows too, when he was little. He decided to thank her and share his toys with her. He smiled and hugged her.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. And I'm sorry for teasing you. Do you want to play with me?" he asked.

She nodded and hugged him back. She felt happy and peaceful. She had found her bow and her brother. They went to his room and played together. They both wore bows and had fun.

"Look at our castle, Mommy!" Lily said. "It is the best castle ever!"

"Can we make another one?" Ben asked. "Maybe a bigger one?"

"Sure, you can make another one. But first, you have to pay the sand man." Mommy said.

"Pay the sand man?" Lily and Ben asked. "Who is the sand man?"

"He is the sand man. He makes sand art for everyone to see. He is very kind and talented. But he also needs money to buy more sand and tools. So, if you want to use his sand, you have to pay him a little bit." Mommy explained.

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They wanted to be kind and fair too. They ran to the sand man and said hello.

"Hello, little ones. Do you like my sand art?" The sand man asked.

"Yes, we do. They are very pretty and cool." Lily and Ben said.

"Thank you. Do you want to use some of my sand to make your own sand art?" The sand man asked.

"Yes, please. But we have to pay you first." Lily and Ben said.

They gave the sand man some coins from their pockets. The sand man smiled and thanked them. He gave them some sand from his bag.

"Here you go. Have fun and be creative. And don't forget to show me your sand art when you are done." The sand man said.

Lily and Ben thanked him and ran back to their spot. They used the sand man's sand to make another castle, bigger and better than the first one. They were very happy and proud. They showed their castle to the sand man and Mommy. They all clapped and cheered. Lily and Ben hugged the sand man and Mommy. They had a wonderful day at the beach.

Lily and Tom give the parrot another cracker. The parrot eats it too.

"Thank you, thank you!" the parrot says. "You are nice!"

Lily and Tom are happy. They like the parrot. They want to play more with the parrot.

But then, a man comes. He is the owner of the parrot. He is angry.

"Hey, you!" he shouts. "Stop feeding my parrot! He is not your pet! He is mine!"

Lily and Tom are scared. They run away from the cage. The parrot is sad.

"Bye, bye!" the parrot says. "Come back soon!"

The man grabs the cage and leaves. He is bad. He does not let the parrot have fun. Lily and Tom wish they could free the parrot and be his friends.

Tom and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the snow and make snowmen. One day, they saw a big hill with lots of snow. They wanted to slide down the hill on their sleds.

"Let's go, Lily! It will be fun!" Tom said.

"OK, Tom. But promise me we will be careful. The hill is very steep and fast." Lily said.

"I promise, Lily. Don't worry. We will be safe." Tom said.

They took their sleds and climbed up the hill. They were very excited. They looked at the view. It was brilliant. They could see the whole town and the sun shining.

"Ready, Lily?" Tom asked.

"Ready, Tom!" Lily answered.

They pushed their sleds and started to slide down the hill. They laughed and screamed. They felt the wind and the snow on their faces. They were having so much fun.

But then, something bad happened. Tom's sled hit a rock and flipped over. Tom fell off his sled and rolled down the hill. He hit a tree and hurt his head. He cried and cried.

Lily saw what happened and stopped her sled. She ran to Tom and hugged him.

"Tom, Tom, are you OK? I'm so sorry. I'm here for you." Lily said.

Tom looked at Lily with tears in his eyes.

"Lily, you promised me we would be careful. You lied to me. You made me crash. You are not my friend anymore." Tom said.

Lily felt very sad and sorry. She tried to say something, but Tom did not listen. He pushed her away and ran to his home.

Lily was left alone on the hill. She wished she could take back her promise. She wished she could make Tom happy again. She wished they could have cocoa and cookies together. But it was too late.

The moral of the story is: Don't make promises you can't keep. They can hurt your friends and yourself. Be honest and responsible.

Anna did not like broccoli. She thought it was green and yucky. She always tried to hide it under her plate or give it to her dog. But her mom knew her tricks and always made her eat some.

One day, it was very gloomy outside. The sky was gray and it rained a lot. Anna could not go out and play with her friends. She was bored and sad. She hoped that dinner would be something nice, like pizza or macaroni.

But when she came to the table, she saw a big bowl of broccoli. Her mom smiled and said, "Anna, today we have broccoli. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy. You have to eat some, okay?"

Anna frowned and shook her head. She did not want to eat broccoli. She said, "No, mom, I don't like broccoli. It is gross. Can I have something else, please?"

Her mom sighed and said, "No, Anna, you have to eat what I made. Broccoli is not gross. It is tasty. You just have to try it. Look, I put some cheese on it. Cheese is yummy, right?"

Anna looked at the broccoli with cheese. She did not think it looked yummy. She thought it looked worse. She said, "No, mom, cheese does not make broccoli better. It makes it worse. I don't want it. I want pizza or macaroni."

Her mom said, "Anna, stop being so picky. You have to eat some broccoli. It is not fair to waste food. There are many children who don't have enough food. You should be grateful for what you have. Come on, just take one bite. Maybe you will like it."

Anna did not want to take a bite. She wanted to cry. She said, "No, mom, I don't want to. I don't like it. I don't care. I hate broccoli."

Her mom said, "Anna, that's enough. You are being very rude and stubborn. You have to eat some broccoli or you will not get any dessert. Do you understand?"

Anna did not like that. She loved dessert. She wanted ice cream or cake. She did not want to miss dessert. She looked at the broccoli and the cheese. She thought for a moment. She decided to try it. Maybe it was not so bad. Maybe she could get dessert.

She took a small bite of broccoli and cheese. She chewed it slowly. She waited for the taste. She was surprised. It was not so bad. It was not so yucky. It was kind of good. She liked the cheese. She took another bite. She liked it more. She smiled and said, "Mom, you were right. Broccoli is not gross. It is tasty. I like it. Can I have some more, please?"

Her mom was happy and proud. She said, "Of course, Anna. I'm glad you like it. You can have some more. And you can also have some dessert. You did a good job. You tried something new. You were brave and smart. I love you, Anna."

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples. Sara wanted to pick an apple, but Tom said no.

"Why not?" Sara asked.

"Because the tree is not ours. It belongs to someone else. We should not take what is not ours. That is bad," Tom said.

"But I am hungry. And the apples look so good. And no one is here. Who will know?" Sara said.

Tom shook his head. "That is not right. We should trust what our parents and teachers tell us. They say we should be honest and kind. If we take the apples, we are not honest and kind. We are selfish and greedy. And maybe someone will know. Maybe the owner of the tree will come and be angry. Or maybe we will feel guilty and sad. Do you want that?" Tom said.

Sara thought for a moment. She looked at the apples. They were shiny and red. But she also looked at Tom. He was her friend. He had clear eyes and a warm smile. He always helped her and shared with her. She trusted him. She did not want to make him or anyone else unhappy. She did not want to be selfish and greedy. She wanted to be honest and kind.

"You are right, Tom. I am sorry. I will not take the apples. Let's go and find something else to eat. Maybe we can ask our parents for a snack. Or maybe we can find some berries or nuts in the park. They are also good and yummy. And they are free and fair," Sara said.

Tom smiled and hugged Sara. "I am proud of you, Sara. You are a good friend. And you are smart and brave. You made a good choice. Come on, let's go and have fun. Maybe we can also find some flowers or rocks or bugs to look at. There are so many things to see and do in the park. And we can enjoy them together. Because we are friends. And we trust each other," Tom said.

They held hands and ran to the park. They had a great time. And they did not need the apples. Because they had something better. They had each other. And they had trust. And that was the best thing of all.

He looked at his toys. He had a train, a car, a doll and a puzzle. He tried to play with them, but he was bored. He missed his friends. He felt lonely. He said to himself, "I don't like this. I want to go out. Maybe it's not so cold. Maybe my friends are waiting for me."

He decided to sneak out of his house. He put on his coat, his boots and his yellow hat. He took his red ball and his blue bike. He opened the door and ran outside. He did not see his mom.

He rode his bike to the park. He hoped to find his friends there. But the park was empty. There was no one there. The swings were still, the slide was wet and the sandbox was frozen. Tom felt even more lonely. He said, "Where are my friends? Why are they not here? Don't they want to play with me?"

He heard a voice behind him. It was his mom. She had followed him. She was angry. She said, "Tom, what are you doing here? I told you to stay inside. It's too cold. You are naughty. Come back with me right now."

His mom hugged him. She said, "I'm not mad at you, Tom. I love you. I know you were lonely. But you have to listen to me. It's not safe to go out when it's cold. You could get hurt or sick. Tom nodded. He said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I love you too. Can we play a game when we get home?"

His mom smiled. She said, "Sure, Tom. We can play a game. Whatever you want. You are my sweet boy."

She decides to let him play for a few more minutes, and then she will tell him to put the scale back on the table. She hopes that he will not lie to her and say that he did not touch it. She wants him to be honest and careful. She thinks of a way to reward him for being a good boy.

She goes to the fridge and takes out a chocolate cake. She cuts a slice and puts it on a plate. She sprinkles some colorful sprinkles on top. She thinks that Ben will love it. She walks to the living room, where Ben is still playing with the scale.

She says, "Ben, what are you doing with the scale?"

Ben looks up and sees the cake. He smiles and says, "I was just weighing my train, mom. I'm sorry, I know it's not a toy. Can I have some cake, please?"

Mom smiles and says, "Yes, you can have some cake, Ben. You are a good boy for telling me the truth. But first, you have to put the scale back on the table, and clean up your toys. Okay?"

Ben nods and says, "Okay, mom. Thank you for the cake. It looks yummy."

He puts the scale back on the table, and picks up his toys. He puts them in his toy box. He runs to the kitchen and hugs his mom. He says, "I love you, mom. You are the best."

Mom hugs him back and says, "I love you too, Ben. You are the best too. Now, let's enjoy the cake together."

They sit down and eat the cake. Ben thinks it is the best cake ever. He is happy and full. He forgets about the scale and the train. He just wants to cuddle with his mom and his teddy bear. He is not restless anymore. He is sleepy. He lies down on the couch and closes his eyes. Mom covers him with a blanket and kisses his forehead. She says, "Good night, Ben. Sweet dreams."

As the game went on, Billy noticed that everyone liked Tom and wanted to play with him. Billy felt left out and realized that teasing people was not nice. He went to Tom and said sorry for teasing him. Tom forgave Billy and let him join the game. From that day on, Billy learned that being kind and playing together was more fun than teasing others. The moral of the story is that kindness is better than teasing, and everyone can have fun when they play together.

He was so lonely and began to sob. Soon all he wanted to do was sleep. So he curled up and closed his eyes. Just as he was about to drift off to sleep, one of the animals returned. She had heard the bear sobbing, thought it was sad and decided to come back to him.

The animal snuggled up to the bear and said it was ok. The bear smiled and thanked her. The two of them laid down together and soon fell asleep. From that day onward, the group of animals would never forget the bear. Even when things got tough, the group would remember the bear's kind and caring heart.

"That is not fun!" Tom said. "That is bad! You hurt us and other people. You should stop!"

"Hey, hey, hey!" the man yelled. "What are you doing? Give that back!"

The lady and the dog thanked them. They said they were brave and kind. They gave them a hug and a treat.

"No, I want to play on the slide," Ben said.

"But the flag is so pretty and bright. Please, Ben, let's go look at it," Lily begged.

"No, I don't like the flag. It's boring. The slide is more fun," Ben said.

Lily was sad. She really wanted to see the flag. She thought Ben was being mean. She decided to go by herself. She ran to the flag pole. She looked up at the flag. She smiled. She felt happy.

But then she heard a loud noise. It was a dog. A big, black dog. The dog was barking and running towards her. Lily was scared. She didn't like dogs. She wanted Ben. She screamed.

"Help, Ben, help! There's a dog!"

Ben heard Lily scream. He looked and saw the dog. He was scared too. But he also cared about Lily. He ran to her. He grabbed her hand. He pulled her away from the dog.

"Come on, Lily, let's go to the slide. It's safer there," Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben. You're a good friend," Lily said.

They ran to the slide. They played together. They forgot about the flag and the dog. They were happy.

"Let's enter the box!" Tom says. He opens the box and sees a suit. The suit is red and blue and has a big S on the chest.

Tommy wanted to draw too. He did not have a pen. He saw Lisa's red pen and he liked it. He went to Lisa and said, "Can I have your pen?"

Lisa looked at Tommy and said, "No, this is my pen. I am drawing with it. You can't have it."

Tommy felt sad and angry. He wanted to draw with the red pen. He said, "That's not fair. You have to share. Sharing is good."

Lisa said, "But I like my pen. It is my favorite pen. I don't want to share it."

Tommy tried to grab the pen from Lisa. Lisa held on to the pen. They both pulled and tugged. The pen broke in half. They both cried.

Miss Jane heard them cry. She came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken pen and the sad faces. She said, "What happened here?"

Lisa and Tommy told her what happened. They both said they were sorry. Miss Jane said, "It's okay to be sorry, but it's better to be kind. Sharing is a kind thing to do. When you share, you make friends. Friends are more fun than pens. Do you want to be friends?"

Lisa and Tommy nodded. They said, "Yes, we want to be friends."

Miss Jane smiled. She said, "That's good. I have more pens for you. You can each have a pen and draw together. You can also share your pens with other kids. They will like you and you will be popular. Popular means many kids like you. Do you want to be popular?"

Lisa and Tommy nodded. They said, "Yes, we want to be popular."

Miss Jane gave them each a pen. Lisa got a blue pen and Tommy got a green pen. They said, "Thank you, Miss Jane."

They went to a table and started to draw. They shared their pens and their paper. They drew nice pictures. They smiled and laughed. They made friends with other kids. They were happy and popular.

Tom and Anna liked to go to the park with their mom. They liked to see the ducks in the pond. They liked to feed them bread and watch them swim.

One day, they saw a duck that was different from the others. It had a big red beak and a green head. It looked very pretty. Tom and Anna wanted to pet it.

"Can we go closer, mom?" Tom asked.

"Be careful, it might bite," mom said.

Tom and Anna walked slowly to the edge of the pond. The duck saw them and came closer too. It quacked loudly and opened its beak.

"Hello, duck," Anna said. "You are very pretty. Can we be your friends?"

The duck quacked again and nodded its head. It seemed to like Anna. It swam closer and rubbed its beak on her hand. Anna giggled and stroked its feathers.

"Can I kiss it, mom?" Anna asked.

"Only if it lets you," mom said.

Anna leaned forward and gave the duck a gentle kiss on its head. The duck quacked happily and kissed her back on the cheek.

"Wow, you are very successful, Anna," Tom said. "You made a new friend."

Anna smiled and hugged the duck. The duck hugged her back with its wings.

"I love you, duck," Anna said.

"I love you, Anna," the duck said.

Mom, Tom and Anna were very surprised. They did not know that the duck could talk. They wondered what other secrets it had. They decided to visit it again and learn more about it. They had a lot of fun at the park.

Lily's daddy quickly got a towel and wiped up the juice. "Good job, Daddy!" said Lily.

After they finished looking at the paintings, they went to the gift shop. Lily saw a cute stuffed animal and said, "Mommy, can I have this?"

Her mommy replied, "Of course, it's so cute! Let's take it home with us."

Lily was so happy and hugged her new stuffed animal tightly. "Thank you, Mommy and Daddy!" she said with a big smile on her face.

Timmy was sad, but he followed his mom. They continued on the trail until they found a river. Timmy asked if he could soak his feet in the water, but his mom said no because it was too cold. Timmy was sad again, but he listened to his mom.

As they were walking back home, Timmy saw a big hill covered in snow. He wanted to slide down it, but his mom said no because it was too dangerous. Timmy was really sad now, but he listened to his mom.

When they got home, Timmy told his dad about all the things he couldn't do. His dad told him that it was important to listen to his mom because she knew what was best. Later that night, they heard on the news that a little boy had slipped on the icy puddle, fallen into the river, and was swept away by the current. Timmy realized that his mom was right and felt grateful for her keeping him safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat that lived in the harbor. The boat was so big that it couldn't fit under the bridge. One day, the boat wanted to go to the other side of the harbor, but it couldn't because of the bridge.

The boat thought and thought, and then it had an idea. It lowered its tall mast and bow, so that it could fit under the bridge. The boat was so happy that it could finally go to the other side of the harbor.

As the boat sailed to the other side of the harbor, it saw a thick fog ahead. The boat was scared because it couldn't see where it was going. But then, the boat remembered how it had lowered its mast and bow to get under the bridge. So, it lowered them again to help it navigate through the thick fog.

And just like that, the boat safely made it to the other side of the harbor. The end.
