He saw a monkey on a tree and wanted to eat it. He climbed the tree and tried to catch the monkey. But the monkey was not weak. He threw a banana at the lion and swung to another tree. The lion fell down and was more hurt and angry.

He saw a turtle on the grass and wanted to eat it. He walked slowly and bit the turtle. But the turtle was not weak. He hid in his shell and the lion could not open it. The lion was very hurt and very angry.

He saw a mouse on a rock and wanted to eat it. He crawled to the mouse and opened his mouth. But the mouse was not afraid. He said to the lion, "Why are you so mean? You are big and strong, but you are not happy. You should be kind and share with others. Then you will have friends and be happy."

The lion was surprised. He said, "But I am hungry and you are small and weak. I can eat you easily."

The mouse said, "Maybe you can, but you should not. You should accept what you have and be grateful. Look, there is a staff of honey on that bush. You can eat that and be sweet. And I can help you with your wounds and be your friend."

The lion thought for a moment. He said, "You are right. I have been greedy and rude. I am sorry. I will accept the staff of honey and be sweet. And I will be your friend and be kind."

The mouse smiled and said, "That is good. Come, I will show you the staff of honey and help you with your wounds."

The lion and the mouse walked together to the bush. They ate the staff of honey and licked each other's wounds. They became friends and were happy.

The moral of the story is: You should accept what you have and be grateful. You should be kind and share with others. Then you will have friends and be happy.

Her mom and dad heard her cry, and they ran to her. They were scared and worried. They knelt down and hugged her. They checked her knee, and they saw it was bleeding. They said they were sorry, and they loved her. They said they would take her to the doctor, and then they would buy her a toy cat.

Sara stopped crying, and she said she was sorry too. She said she loved them, and she did not want to run away. She said she learned her lesson, and she would not try to climb the wall again. She said she was happy to have a toy cat, and she would take good care of it. She said she was still independent, but she also needed her mom and dad.

"Look, Sue, this is a print of a big mountain. It has snow on top and trees at the bottom. Do you want to go there?" Tom asks.

"Yes, Tom, I want to go there. It looks very pretty and cold. Maybe we can make a snowman and slide on the snow," Sue says.

They pack their bags and tell their mom and dad. Their mom and dad say they can go, but they have to be careful and stay together. They give them a map and a phone. They say they will call them when they get there.

"Wow, Sue, look, we are almost there. The mountain is very big and white. I can see the snow shining in the sun. Are you excited?" Tom asks.

"Yes, Tom, I am very excited. I can't wait to play in the snow and see the trees. Maybe we will see some animals too. Do you think there are bears or deer or rabbits?" Sue asks.

They get off the train and walk to the cabin. They see a sign that says "Available". They knock on the door and a nice lady opens it. She says they can stay in the cabin for two nights. She gives them the key and some blankets. She says there is a fireplace and a kitchen and a bathroom. She says they can use the sleds and the skis and the snowshoes. She says they can have fun, but they have to be safe and warm.

They say they love each other and their mom and dad. They say they are ready to have fun.

Tom and Anna like to play with their cart. They put their toys and books in the cart and push it around the yard. Sometimes they pretend the cart is a car or a train or a boat.

One day, they decide to make a race with their cart. They draw a line with a stick and say, "This is the start. This is the end. The first one to reach the end wins." They put their cart behind the start line and get ready to run.

"Are you ready, Anna?" Tom asks.

"Yes, I am ready, Tom," Anna says.

"Okay, let's go!" Tom says and they both start to push their cart as fast as they can.

But the race is not easy. The cart is heavy and the yard is bumpy. Tom and Anna have to push hard and avoid the rocks and the holes. They also have to be careful not to bump into each other or the fence.

Tom is a little bit faster than Anna. He is almost at the end when he sees a big puddle. He thinks, "I can go through the puddle. It will be fun." He pushes his cart into the water and splashes.

But the puddle is deeper than he thought. The water slows down his cart and makes it muddy. He tries to push harder, but his feet slip and he falls.

Anna sees Tom fall and stops. She thinks, "I can help Tom. He is my friend." She leaves her cart and runs to Tom. She helps him get up and says, "Are you okay, Tom?"

"Yes, I am okay, Anna. Thank you," Tom says. He looks at his cart and says, "But my cart is not okay. It is wet and dirty. I can't finish the race."

Anna looks at her cart and says, "My cart is okay. It is dry and clean. I can finish the race. But I don't want to finish without you. You are my friend."

Tom smiles and says, "You are my friend too, Anna. You are very kind. How about we finish the race together?"

Anna nods and says, "Yes, let's finish the race together. That will be more fun."

They take their carts and walk to the end line. They cross it at the same time and say, "We did it! We finished the race!"

They hug and laugh. They don't care who won or lost. They are happy to play with their cart and their friend. The race was difficult, but they finished it together.

"No, Tom, we can't keep the wallet. It belongs to someone else. Maybe they are looking for it. We should give it back." Sam says. He is a good boy and knows how to share.

"But how do we find the owner? Maybe they are gone. Maybe they don't care. Maybe they have more money." Tom says. He is a greedy boy and wants to keep the wallet.

"Let's ask the lady over there. She works in the park. Maybe she knows who lost the wallet." Sam says. He points to a lady in a blue uniform. She has a badge and a walkie-talkie.

"We are playing and having fun. We like the park. It is big and green and has many slides and swings." Sam says.

"Sure, what is it?" The lady says.

"Do you know who lost this wallet?" Sam says. He takes the wallet out of Tom's pocket and shows it to the lady.

One day, they find a big paper book on a bench. The book has many pictures of animals and colors and shapes. Tim and Jen want to look at the book.

"Can we share the book?" Jen asks Tim.

"Yes, we can share the book," Tim says. "You can have the first page and I can have the second page."

They open the book and see a picture of a white dove. The dove has a long neck and a small beak and two wings. The dove looks nice and regular.

"I like the dove," Jen says. "It is pretty and soft."

"I like the dove too," Tim says. "It can fly and sing."

They turn the page and see a picture of a lion. The lion has a big mane and a long tail and sharp teeth. The lion looks scary and strong.

"I don't like the lion," Jen says. "It is mean and loud."

"I don't like the lion either," Tim says. "It can bite and roar."

They want to see more pictures of the dove, but they forget how to turn the page back. They pull the book from both sides, but the book does not move.

"Let go of the book!" Jen says.

"No, you let go of the book!" Tim says.

They pull harder and harder, but the book still does not move. Then, they hear a loud rip. The book tears in half. The dove and the lion fall to the ground.

"Oh no!" Jen says.

"Oh no!" Tim says.

They look at the book and see that it is broken. They feel sad and sorry. They did not mean to tear the book.

They pick up the dove and the lion and put them back on the bench. They hope that someone can fix the book. They say goodbye to the book and the dove and the lion. They go home and tell their mom what happened.

Mom hugs them and says, "It's okay. You made a mistake, but you can learn from it. Next time, be careful with books and other things that are not yours. Books are for reading and learning, not for tearing. And doves and lions are for looking and respecting, not for fighting. Do you understand?"

Tim and Jen nod and say, "Yes, mom. We understand. We are sorry. We love you."

Mom smiles and says, "I love you too. Now, let's have some cookies and milk and read a new book together."

She took another piece of bread and held it in her hand. She stretched her arm to the swan. The swan looked at her and swam to her. Lily was happy. She thought the swan liked her.

But the swan was not friendly. It was stubborn and greedy. It wanted all the bread for itself. It snapped at Lily's hand and bit her finger. Lily screamed and dropped the bread. She felt a sharp pain in her finger. She ran back to Mom, crying.

Luckily, a kind duck saw her and swam to her. He lifted her up with his beak and brought her to the shore. He shook his head and said, "You are a bird, not a fish. You should not fly so low over the water. You could have drowned. You should be more careful and listen to your elders."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was playing in the park with her friend, Jack. They were having a lot of fun on the swings and the slide. Suddenly, Lily saw something shiny on the ground. It was a gold coin! She picked it up and showed it to Jack.

"Look what I found!" she said excitedly.

"That's great!" Jack said. "But I'm sorry, we have to give it to the park ranger. It's not ours."

Lily didn't want to give the gold coin away, but Jack was right. They went to find the park ranger, but on the way, Lily tripped and the gold coin fell out of her hand. It sprang into the air and landed in a nearby pond. They tried to fish it out, but it was too deep.

Lily felt very sad. She wished she had listened to Jack and given the gold coin to the park ranger. She was sorry for not doing the right thing. Jack tried to cheer her up, but it was no use. They went home feeling disappointed.

"I want the dolls to be happy," Lucy said. 

But her dad didn't understand. "Hanging the toys won't make them happy," he said. 

Lucy disagreed and said. "It will! I want them to fly."

Her dad explained that the toys would not fly, no matter how much she wanted them to. He said, "You need to be more successful at making your dolls happy. Try something new!"

So, Lucy came up with a new way. She took the plastic dolls and hung them on a string between two trees, so it looked like they were flying. Her dad smiled and said, "That's much better! Now your dolls are really happy." 

The end.

Soon, a big angry bear came to the park. The bear saw Max playing with his ball and was very upset. The bear said, "Max, you took my ball without asking. That was foolish of you." Max felt bad and gave the ball back to the bear. He learned that it is important to ask before taking things that don't belong to him. From that day on, Max always asked before playing with things he found in the park.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Ben and Mike. Every day they would hang out at school and play tag. One day Mike had a plan. He said to Ben: "Let's do something different today. I have a great idea!"

Ben was excited and said: "What is it?". Mike then said: "Let's hang out at the garbage dump". Ben was a bit surprised and said: "That's a bit disgusting, why do you want to do that?".

Mike smiled and said: "Sometimes it's good to try different things, you never know what might happen". Ben thought for a bit then said: "OK, let's give it a try".

So the two friends carefully made their way to the garbage dump. When they arrived they were surprised by how much junk there was. The smell was disgusting and Ben thought that he had made a mistake.

But then Mike found a treasure! It was a beautiful golden necklace! The two friends were so excited!

The moral of this story is that you should never judge a book by its cover. Just because something looks or smells disgusting doesn't mean that it's not worth exploring. You never know what treasures you may find!

One day, Sara had a new car that was very shiny and red. She said to Ben, "My car is the best. It has more speed than your car. Let us race and see who wins."

Ben agreed, but he was not happy. He liked his car, even if it was old and pale. He said, "My car may not have much speed, but it has more heart. Let us count to three and then start."

They counted, "One, two, three!" and pushed their cars on the floor. Sara's car zoomed ahead, but Ben's car followed close behind. Sara smiled and said, "I told you, my car is faster. I will win the race."

But then, something happened. Sara's car hit a bump and flipped over. It landed on its back and could not move. Ben's car passed by and reached the finish line. Ben stopped and said, "I won the race. My car may not have much speed, but it has more heart. It does not give up."

Sara felt sad and sorry. She said, "You are right, Ben. Your car has more heart. I was wrong to boast about my car. It does not matter how fast or shiny it is, if it cannot finish the race. I am sorry, Ben. Can we still be friends?"

Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. We are still friends. And we can still play with our cars. But next time, let us not race, but share. Sharing is more fun than winning."

The moral of the story is: Do not be proud of what you have, but be grateful for what you have. And do not compete with others, but cooperate with them. Sharing is more fun than winning.

The bird wished it could pause time and fly away, but it was too late. The cat had caught it and there was nothing the bird could do. The story ended sadly with the bird being eaten by the cat.

Lily played with her new toy car for hours until it was time for bed. As she was getting ready for bed, she saw a spider on the wall. Lily was scared of spiders and didn't want to sleep in her room with it. "Daddy, there's a spider on the wall! Can you please help me?" asked Lily. Her dad came to her room and used the hammer to gently remove the spider from the wall. "Don't worry, Lily. The spider won't hurt you. It's gone now," said her dad.

Lily felt relieved and hugged her dad. "Thank you, daddy. You're the best!" said Lily. She went to bed feeling happy and safe, with her new toy car by her side.

The friendly monster laughed and blew softly on the rabbit. The rabbit just laughed and hopped away.

The End.

"Maybe the bird doesn't know its name," said Lola's mom thoughtfully. So she taught Lola how to spell the bird's name.

Lola was so happy to meet her new feathered friend. She was sure they would stay friends forever!

Ben was glad to see Lily and mom. He was still scared and sticky, but he felt better. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. The slide is not fun. It's scary and jammy. I don't like it."

Lily said, "It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry too. I didn't know there was jam on the slide. It was a bad surprise. I don't like it either."

Mom said, "Let's go home and clean up. Then we can have some cookies and milk. And maybe we can find a different slide next time. One that is not so enormous and not so jammy."

Lily and Ben agreed. They held mom's hand and walked home. They were happy to be together and to leave the jammy snake slide behind.

"Tom, put it back!" Anna says. "That is not yours. You are being bad."

One day, a little girl named Mia found a small, furry animal in her backyard. It was hiding under a bush and looked scared and hurt. Mia wanted to help it, so she gently picked it up and brought it inside. She gave it some water and a soft blanket to lie on. She asked it, "What is your name? Where do you come from?"

The animal did not answer, but it made a soft noise and snuggled closer to Mia. It had big, round eyes and a long, fluffy tail. Mia thought it was very cute and mysterious. She decided to call it Mimi, because it sounded like the noise it made.

Mia's mom came home and saw Mia and Mimi on the couch. She was surprised and asked Mia, "What is that, honey? Where did you find it?"

Mia told her mom the story of how she found Mimi and how she comforted it. She said, "Can we keep it, mom? Please? It needs a home and a friend."

Mia's mom smiled and said, "Well, I don't know what kind of animal it is, but it seems very sweet and gentle. And you have been very kind and caring to it. I think we can keep it, as long as you promise to take good care of it and learn more about it."

Mia was very happy and hugged her mom and Mimi. She said, "Thank you, mom! I love you and Mimi!"

Mia's mom said, "I love you too, Mia. And I'm proud of you for being so brave and compassionate. You have a big heart, my dear."

They learned that pangolins were shy and gentle creatures that rolled into balls when they felt threatened. Mia decided to do something to help pangolins and other animals in danger. She made a poster and a speech and presented them to her class. She told them about Mimi and how she found her and comforted her. She told them about pangolins and how they needed protection and respect. She asked them to join her in raising awareness and money for animal conservation.

Mia's classmates were very impressed and moved by her story and her passion. They agreed to help her and Mimi. They made more posters and flyers and organized a bake sale and a donation drive. They also invited a wildlife expert to come and talk to them about pangolins and other animals.

Tommy had a dog named Spot. Spot was a good dog, but he liked to run away from home. He would dig under the fence and chase cats and birds. Tommy's mom gave Spot a collar with a tag that had their address and phone number. She said, "This collar will help us find you if you get lost, Spot. You have to wear it all the time."

One day, Spot saw a shiny bone in the yard next door. He wanted the bone, so he dug under the fence again and ran to get it. But the bone belonged to another dog, a big dog named Rex. Rex saw Spot and barked, "Hey, that's my bone! Go away, you selfish dog!"

Spot was scared of Rex, but he did not want to give up the bone. He tried to run away with it, but Rex was faster and stronger. He bit Spot's collar and pulled it off. Then he chased Spot away and kept the bone and the collar.

Spot ran back to his home, but he felt sad and ashamed. He had lost his collar and his bone, and he had made Rex angry. He also knew that Tommy and his mom would be worried about him. He wished he had listened to them and stayed in his yard.

When Tommy came home from school, he looked for Spot, but he could not find him. He asked his mom, "Where is Spot, mom? Did he run away again?"

His mom said, "I don't know, Tommy. I called the animal shelter, but they did not find him. Maybe someone saw his collar and called us, but we have not heard anything. I hope he is safe, Tommy. He should not be so selfish and run away from us. We love him and we want him to be happy."

Tommy felt sad and angry. He loved Spot, but he did not like that he ran away and did not care about them. He said, "I wish Spot would return, mom. I miss him, but he has to learn his lesson. He has to be a good dog and stay with us."

The next day, Tommy heard a knock on the door. He opened it and saw a man holding Spot. Spot was dirty and tired, but he wagged his tail and licked Tommy's face. The man said, "Is this your dog, son? I found him wandering on the street, without a collar. He looked lost and hungry, so I took him home and fed him. Then I saw your poster on the lamppost and I brought him back to you."

Tommy hugged Spot and thanked the man. He said, "Thank you, sir. You are very kind. This is my dog, Spot. He ran away from home and lost his collar. I'm sorry he caused you trouble."

The man said, "It's no trouble, son. I'm glad I could help. You have a nice dog, but he needs to be more careful and obedient. He could get hurt or lost if he runs away again. You should get him a new collar and keep him in your yard."

Tommy nodded and said, "I will, sir. I learned my lesson, too. I have to watch over Spot and teach him to be a good dog. He is not selfish, he is just curious. But he loves us and we love him. Right, Spot?"

Spot barked and nodded. He was happy to return to his home and his family. He realized that he had been selfish and foolish, and he decided to never run away again. He wanted to be a good dog and make Tommy and his mom proud. He also hoped that Rex would forgive him and maybe share his bone with him someday.

One day, her mom took her to see a nice man who could help her. He was a dentist. He wore a white coat and a mask. He had a big chair and a bright light. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, Lily. I am here to talk to you and make your tooth feel better. Do you want to sit on my chair?"

Lily was scared. She did not want to sit on the chair. She did not want the man to touch her tooth. She shook her head and said, "No, thank you. I want to go home."

The dentist was gentle. He said, "I understand, Lily. But if you let me look at your tooth, I can give you something to make the pain go away. It will be quick and easy. You can hold your mom's hand and I will talk to you the whole time. How does that sound?"

Lily looked at her mom. Her mom nodded and said, "It's okay, Lily. The dentist is very nice and he knows what to do. He will help you feel better. I will be right here with you. You are very brave."

Lily took a deep breath. She trusted her mom and the dentist. She said, "Okay. I will try." She climbed on the chair and opened her mouth. The dentist looked at her tooth and said, "Good job, Lily. You have a cavity. That's why your tooth hurts. But don't worry. I have a special tool that can fix it. It will make a funny noise, but it won't hurt. Do you want to hear it?"

Lily nodded. The dentist turned on the tool and it made a buzzing sound. Lily giggled. It sounded like a bee. The dentist said, "See? It's not so bad. Now I will use it on your tooth. You will feel a little tickle, but nothing more. Are you ready?"

Lily nodded again. She held her mom's hand and closed her eyes. The dentist used the tool on her tooth. It tickled a little, but it did not hurt. Lily felt the dentist put something on her tooth. He said, "All done, Lily. You did great. Now your tooth is fixed and it won't hurt anymore. You can open your eyes and see."

Lily opened her eyes and saw the dentist smiling. He gave her a mirror and said, "Look, Lily. You have a shiny new tooth. It's silver and it will protect your tooth from getting bad again. Do you like it?"

Lily looked at her tooth. It was shiny and silver. She liked it. She smiled and said, "Thank you, dentist. You are very nice. You made my tooth feel better. I am not miserable anymore."

The dentist said, "You're very welcome, Lily. I'm glad you're happy. You have a beautiful smile. Now you can eat your favorite food and play with your toys. But remember to brush your teeth every day and visit me again in six months. Can you do that?"

Lily said, "Yes, I can. I will brush my teeth every day and visit you again. Thank you, dentist. Goodbye."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best. And you are very brave."

"Look, Ben, bees!" Sara says. "They make honey. Do you like honey?"

"Yes, I like honey. It is sweet and sticky. But we should not go near the bees. They can sting us and it hurts," Ben says.

They watch the bees from a safe distance. They see one bee that is different. It is not yellow and black. It is pink. It has a pink body and pink wings. It is very pretty.

"Wow, Sara, look at that bee. It is pink. I have never seen a pink bee before. Do you think it is a special bee?" Ben says.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe it is a princess bee. Maybe it is the queen of the hive. Maybe it likes pink flowers," Sara says.

They see the pink bee zoom around the tree. It flies faster than the other bees. It looks happy and free. It sees Sara and Ben and flies towards them. It lands on Sara's nose and tickles her.

"Hi, pink bee. You are so cute. What is your name?" Sara says.

The pink bee buzzes softly. It sounds like it is saying hello. It wiggles its antennae and flaps its wings. It smiles at Sara and Ben.

"Hello, pink bee. You are so fast. Where do you come from?" Ben says.

The pink bee buzzes again. It sounds like it is saying something. It points its antennae at the tree and then at the sky. It looks like it is telling them a story.

"Are you saying you live in the hive in the tree, but you also like to fly in the sky? Do you have friends in the hive and in the sky?" Sara says.

The pink bee nods and buzzes. It sounds like it is saying yes. It looks happy and proud. It likes to live in the hive and to fly in the sky. It has friends in both places.

"That is so cool, pink bee. You are very lucky. You have the best of both worlds. You are a special bee," Ben says.

The pink bee beams and buzzes. It sounds like it is saying thank you. It likes Sara and Ben. They are nice and friendly. They are also special.

The pink bee gives Sara and Ben a kiss on the cheek. It says goodbye and zooms away. It flies back to the hive and then to the sky. It waves at Sara and Ben and smiles.

Sara and Ben wave back and smile. They are happy and amazed. They have met a pink bee. They have made a new friend. They will never forget the pink bee.

One day, she was playing with her dolls in her room, when her brother Ben came in. He saw the princess doll and grabbed it.

"Ben, that's not nice!" Lily said. "You hurt my princess. She's my friend. Give her back to me."

Ben stuck out his tongue. "No, she's mine now. You can't have her. Go away."

Lily felt like crying. She did not know what to do. She looked around and saw her mom in the kitchen. She ran to her and told her what happened.

"Mom, Ben took my princess. He's mean. He won't give her back. Can you help me?" she said.

Mom looked at Lily and smiled. She hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I have an idea. Let's go and talk to Ben. Maybe we can solve this problem together."

Mom and Lily went to the living room, where Ben was still holding the princess doll. Mom sat down next to him and said, "Ben, I see you like the princess doll. She's very pretty, isn't she?"

Ben nodded. He liked the princess doll's dress and crown.

Mom said, "But you know, Lily likes her too. She was playing with her before you came in. She was making a story with her and the other dolls. She was very happy. How do you think she felt when you took her away?"

Ben looked at Lily, who was standing behind Mom. He saw her sad face and felt a little sorry.

He said, "She felt bad."

Mom said, "That's right. She felt bad. And you don't want to make your sister feel bad, do you?"

Ben shook his head. He did not want to make Lily feel bad. He loved his sister, even when they fought.

Mom said, "So, what can you do to make her feel better?"

Ben thought for a moment. He looked at the princess doll and then at Lily. He had an idea.

He said, "I can give her back the princess. And I can play with her and the other dolls. Maybe I can be the dragon."

Lily smiled. She liked Ben's idea. She said, "Thank you, Ben. That's very nice of you. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I would love to play with you and the dolls. You can be the dragon. He's very brave and strong."

Ben smiled too. He gave Lily the princess doll and hugged her. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm sorry I took her. I love you, sis. Let's play."

Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them. They had solved their problem by talking and sharing. They were good kids. She said, "I love you both. Have fun playing. And remember, the princess is important. She has to solve a problem with the fairy and the dragon."

Lily and Ben nodded. They took their dolls and went back to Lily's room. They made up a new story with the princess, the fairy, and the dragon. They had a lot of fun. They were happy.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom bake cakes. One day, mom gave them a new mixer to use. It was shiny and fast and made a loud noise. Sara and Ben both wanted to hold the mixer and press the button.

"Let me do it!" Sara said, grabbing the mixer from Ben.

"No, it's my turn!" Ben said, pulling the mixer back.

They started to fight and tug on the mixer. The mixer slipped from their hands and fell on the floor. It broke into pieces and the batter splashed everywhere. Mom heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She was very angry.

"What have you done?" she asked. "You broke the mixer and made a mess! Why couldn't you share and take turns?"

Sara and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They knew they had been selfish and jealous. They wanted to make mom happy, not sad.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We were fighting over the mixer and we dropped it. We didn't mean to break it."

Mom sighed and hugged them. "I know you didn't mean to, but you have to learn to cooperate and respect each other. The mixer was a gift for both of you, not just one of you. Fighting over things won't make you happy, it will only cause trouble. Next time, you should surrender the mixer when it's not your turn and wait patiently for your turn. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They understood that sharing was better than fighting. They helped mom clean up the kitchen and apologized to each other. They promised to be more careful and kind with the mixer and with each other. Mom smiled and gave them each a slice of cake. They ate it happily and thanked mom for the cake and the mixer. They learned their lesson and never fought over the mixer again.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Fighting over things will only lead to problems. Surrendering the mixer when it's not your turn is a sign of respect and cooperation.

He wanted to show his rocket to his mom. He ran to the kitchen with his rocket in his hand. But he did not see the cat on the floor. He tripped over the cat and fell down. His rocket flew out of his hand and landed on the stove.

The stove was hot. The glue on the rocket started to melt. The paper and the stickers started to burn. Smoke came out of the rocket. Tom was scared. He cried out for his mom.

Mom heard Tom and ran to the kitchen. She saw the smoke and the fire. She was troubled. She turned off the stove and grabbed a towel. She put out the fire and threw the rocket in the trash. She hugged Tom and the cat. She was glad they were not hurt.

She told Tom that glue and fire are not good friends. She told him to be careful with his glue and his scissors. She told him to watch out for the cat. She told him she loved him and his rocket. She gave him a kiss and a cookie. Tom said he was sorry. He said he loved her and the cat too. He said he would make a new rocket with his glue, but not near the stove. Mom smiled and said that was a good idea.

Anna liked to paint. She had many colors and brushes. She painted flowers and trees and animals on paper. She was happy when she painted.

One day, it rained a lot. Anna could not go outside and play. She was bored and sad. She wanted to paint, but she had no paper left. She looked around her room and saw the wall. She had an idea.

She took her paints and brushes and started to paint on the wall. She painted a big rainbow and a sun and a bird. She smiled and said, "Look, Mommy, I made a beautiful picture for you!"

But Mommy was not happy. She saw the paint on the wall and got angry. She said, "Anna, what did you do? You made a big mess! You are not allowed to paint on the wall! You have to clean it up right now!"

Anna felt bad. She did not mean to make Mommy angry. She wanted to make her happy. She said, "I'm sorry, Mommy, I just wanted to paint. I had no paper. I like to paint."

Mommy sighed. She said, "I know you like to paint, Anna, but you have to ask me first. You can't paint on the wall. It's not good. Come on, let's get a cloth and some water and clean it up."

Anna and Mommy went to the bathroom and got a cloth and some water. They went back to the wall and tried to wipe off the paint. But the paint was not easy to remove. It was sticky and wet. It dripped down the wall and into the drain. The drain got clogged and the water overflowed. The floor got wet and slippery.

Anna and Mommy were miserable. They had to call Daddy to help them. Daddy came and fixed the drain and the wall. He was not happy either. He said, "Anna, you have to be careful with your paints. You can't paint on the wall or the drain. You have to paint on paper or canvas. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She said, "I understand, Daddy. I'm sorry. I won't do it again. Can I still paint?"

Daddy smiled. He said, "Yes, you can still paint, Anna. But only on paper or canvas. And only with Mommy's permission. OK?"

Anna said, "OK, Daddy. Thank you. I love you."

Daddy said, "I love you too, Anna. And I love your paintings. But please, no more on the wall or the drain."

Anna and Ben are best friends. They like to play with their toy cars and pretend to drive. They have a big box of mints that they share. Mints are their favorite candy. They are sweet and make their breath smell good.

One day, they are playing in the park. They find a big hill and decide to drive their cars down. Anna goes first. She pushes her red car and watches it zoom down the hill. "Wow, that was fun!" she says. "Your turn, Ben!"

Ben picks up his blue car and gets ready to push it. But then he sees a big dog running towards them. The dog is barking and looks angry. Ben is scared. He drops his car and runs away. He forgets about Anna and the mints.

Anna is left alone. She sees the dog too. She is scared too. But she does not run away. She picks up Ben's car and holds it in her arms. She also grabs the box of mints. She hopes the dog will not hurt her or the toys.

The dog reaches the hill. He sniffs around and sees Anna. He also sees the mints. He likes mints too. He tries to take the box from Anna. But Anna does not let go. She says, "No, dog! These are our mints! Go away!"

The dog growls and tugs harder. Anna holds on tighter. She is brave. She is loyal. She thinks of Ben and wishes he was here.

Then she hears a voice. It is Ben. He has come back. He saw the dog and felt bad. He wanted to help Anna. He brought a stick. He waves the stick at the dog and says, "Bad dog! Leave Anna alone! She is my friend!"

The dog sees the stick and gets scared. He lets go of the box and runs away. He does not want to fight. He just wanted some mints.

Anna and Ben hug each other. They are happy. They are safe. They are still best friends. They share the mints and the cars. They say, "We are sorry" and "We forgive you". They drive their cars down the hill again. They have fun. They are loyal.

They get in their car. They pretend to start the engine. They make vroom-vroom noises. They drive around the grass. They have fun.

But then, they see a big dog running towards them. The dog is barking and wagging its tail. It wants to play. But Anna and Ben are worried. They think the dog will bite their car. They are scared.

"Stop!" Anna says. "You are ruining our car!"

"Go away!" Ben says. "You are not our friend!"

But the dog does not listen. It thinks they are playing. It wags its tail. It barks happily.

Then, they hear a voice.

"I'm sorry!" She says. "He didn't mean to scare you. He just wanted to say hello. He likes cars. He is a good dog."

She pulls the dog off their car. She pets him. She smiles at Anna and Ben.

"Do you want to play with us?" She asks. "We can share our toys. We can be friends."

Anna and Ben look at each other. They look at their car. It has some scratches and dents. But it is still a car. They look at the dog. He has a friendly face. He is still a dog.

They nod. They smile. They say yes.

They get out of their car. They join the girl and the dog. They play with bikes and balls. They have fun.

They are not worried anymore. They are happy.

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. Ben had a brown apron that he tied around his waist. Lily had a pink hat that she put on her head.

"Today we are making soup," Ben said. "We need water, carrots, potatoes and salt."

"OK," Lily said. "I will get the water. You get the carrots and potatoes."

Lily turned on the faucet and filled a big pot with water. She carried it to the stove and put it on a burner. Ben opened the fridge and took out some carrots and potatoes. He washed them in the sink and then cut them with a plastic knife.

"Be careful with the knife," Lily said. "Don't cut yourself."

"I won't," Ben said. "I am a good chef. Look, I made small pieces of carrots and potatoes. Now we can put them in the pot."

Ben and Lily added the carrots and potatoes to the water. They also sprinkled some salt from a shaker. They stirred the soup with a wooden spoon.

"Yum, it smells good," Lily said. "Can we taste it?"

"Not yet," Ben said. "We have to wait for it to boil. Then it will be hot and ready."

They waited for a few minutes, watching the bubbles in the pot. Then they heard a loud beep.

"Oh no, it's the timer," Ben said. "Mom said we have to stop playing when the timer goes off. She will be home soon."

"OK, let's turn off the stove and clean up," Lily said. "We can have our soup later."

They turned off the stove and put the pot in the sink. They washed the spoon and the knife and dried them with a towel. They took off their apron and hat and hung them on a hook. They put the pots and pans back in the cupboard.

"Good job, chefs," Ben said. "We made a delicious soup."

"Good job, chefs," Lily said. "We had a lot of fun."

Sara says, "I will give you these two white shells. They are round and rough. They look like snowballs. Here you go."

"Tom, I want to go back," Sam says. "The mountain is too hard. And it is going to rain. We will get wet and cold and sick."

"Me too, Sam," Tom says. "But we are very far from home. We have to keep going. Maybe we can find a place to rest and hide."

They look around and see a big rock. It has a hole under it. It looks like a cave. They run to it and crawl inside. It is dark and dry and cozy. They pause and catch their breath.

"Tom, look!" Sam says. He points to something in the corner. It is a fat bear. It is sleeping and snoring. It has some honey and fish and berries. It smells good.

"Sam, shh!" Tom says. He is afraid. He grabs Sam's hand and backs away. He hopes the bear will not wake up and see them. He wishes they never went to the mountain. He wishes they were home with Mom. He wonders what they will do. He prays for help.

Lily and Ben were making a cake with Mom. They had eggs, flour, butter and milk. But they needed sugar to make it sweet. Mom looked in the cupboard and saw no sugar.

"Oh no, we have no sugar!" Mom said. "What can we do?"

Lily had an idea. "We can borrow some sugar from Mrs. Lee. She lives next door and she is very nice. She always gives us cookies."

"Good idea, Lily. Let's go and ask her." Mom said. She took a bowl and a spoon and went with Lily and Ben to Mrs. Lee's house.

They knocked on the door and Mrs. Lee opened it. She smiled when she saw them.

"Hello, Mom, Lily and Ben. What brings you here?" Mrs. Lee asked.

"Hello, Mrs. Lee. We are making a cake, but we have no sugar. Can we borrow some sugar from you, please?" Mom asked.

"Of course, you can. I have plenty of sugar. How much do you need?" Mrs. Lee said.

"Just a spoonful, thank you." Mom said.

Mrs. Lee took a jar of sugar and poured some into the bowl. She gave it to Mom and said, "Here you go. Enjoy your cake. What kind of cake are you making?"

"A mild cake. It has no nuts or spices. Just eggs, flour, butter, milk and sugar." Lily said.

"That sounds delicious. I like mild cakes too. Maybe you can share some with me later." Mrs. Lee said.

"Sure, we can. Thank you for the sugar, Mrs. Lee. You are very kind." Ben said.

"You're welcome, Ben. Have fun baking." Mrs. Lee said.

Mom, Lily and Ben said goodbye to Mrs. Lee and went back to their house. They finished making the cake and put it in the oven. It smelled good and looked yummy. They waited for it to cool down and then cut a slice for Mrs. Lee. They took it to her house and knocked on the door.

"Hello, again. We brought you some cake. We made it with your sugar." Mom said.

"Oh, thank you. That's so sweet of you. Can I have a taste?" Mrs. Lee said.

"Sure, you can. Here you go." Lily said.

Mrs. Lee took a bite and smiled. "Mmm, this is a very mild and moist cake. I love it. Thank you for sharing it with me."

"You're welcome, Mrs. Lee. We're glad you like it." Ben said.

They all sat down and ate some cake together. They talked and laughed and had a good time. They were happy and friendly neighbors.

Tom's dad heard the noise and ran into the room. He saw Tom crying and Coco flying. He quickly closed the door and the window and tried to catch Coco. He told Tom to calm down and not to move. He said Coco was harmless, but he didn't like to be touched by strangers.

After a few minutes, Tom's dad managed to get Coco back into the birdcage. He locked the door and checked Tom's finger. It was not bleeding, but it was red and sore. He put some ice on it and gave Tom a hug. He said he was sorry that Coco bit him, but he also said that Tom should not have opened the birdcage. He said that Coco needed his own space and that Tom should only supply him with food and water and talk to him from outside.

Tom nodded and said he was sorry too. He said he loved Coco and he didn't want to hurt him. He said he would be more careful next time. He looked at Coco and said "hello". Coco looked at him and said "hello". Tom smiled and said "cracker". Coco smiled and said "cracker". Tom's dad smiled and said "good bird".

"Sure, honey, but be careful, they are spicy," her mom says. She buys two hot dogs and gives one to Lily and one to Ben.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" the panda says. He spits out the hot dog and rubs his tongue. "That is not bamboo! That is spicy!"

Lily and Ben are shocked. They did not know the panda can talk. They also did not know he does not like spicy food.

"Sorry, panda, we did not mean to hurt you," Lily says. "We wanted to share our food with you."

"Yeah, sorry, panda, we thought you would like it," Ben says. "We like hot dogs."

The panda looks at them and sighs. He is not angry, but he is not happy either. He decides to forgive them.

"It's okay, kids, I know you were trying to be nice," the panda says. "But next time, please don't feed me anything but bamboo. That is what I like best."

Lily and Ben nod. They promise to never feed the panda anything spicy again. They finish their hot dogs and say goodbye to the panda. They go to see other animals and have fun. The panda goes back to eating his bamboo and feels better. He hopes the kids learned their lesson.

The rabbit eyed the squirrel and said "I'm gathering acorns". 

The squirrel was eager, so he asked "Can I join you?".

The rabbit nodded his head and said "Yes, but be gentle".

The moral of the story is: when you're doing something dangerous, it's important to wait for help before you try it.

The creature smiled and said, "Can I play with it?". The girl smiled back and said, "Yes, you can".

With that, the little creature was so happy. He began to play with the toy and the girl watched. They both laughed and had a good time.

Lily and Max were sad and hurt. They ran to their mom. They told her what happened. Their mom was angry and shocked. She took them to the doctor. The doctor gave them medicine and bandages. He said they would be okay. But they had to stay away from the slide.

She gave them warm towels and hot chocolate. They felt better. They said sorry to each other. They learned their lesson. They decided to play inside until the storm was over.

But then Lily got tired of the game. She wanted to do something else. She said to Ben, "I quit. I don't want to play with the hose anymore. Let's go on the swing."

Ben was sad. He liked the hose game. He said to Lily, "No, don't quit. The hose is fun. Please play with me."

Lily shook her head. She walked away from the hose and the bucket. She went to the swing and sat on it. She waited for Ben to push her.

Lily cried. She got off the swing and ran to the house. She told Mom what Ben did. Mom was mad. She came to the backyard and took the hose from Ben. She said, "Ben, that was not nice. You should not spray Lily with the hose. You should say sorry to her."

Ben felt bad. He realized he was wrong. He said, "Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Mom. I won't do it again."

Mom hugged Ben and Lily. She said, "It's okay. I love you both. But next time, play nicely and share the hose. Or find another game that you both like."

"No, Lily. Pigeon is nice. Pigeon is my friend," Sam said. He smiled as the pigeon ate from his hand. He stroked its soft feathers. The pigeon cooed.

"Wow, Sam. You are great. You can talk to pigeon," Lily said. She was impressed by Sam. She wanted to try too. She broke off a piece of bread and held it out to another pigeon. The pigeon flew over and landed on her arm.

"Hello, pigeon. I am Lily. You are pretty," Lily said. She giggled as the pigeon nibbled at the bread. She felt its warm body and its gentle beak.

"Hello, Lily. I am Pippa. You are kind," the pigeon said.

Lily gasped. She heard the pigeon talk. She looked at Sam. He heard it too. They were both amazed.

"Pigeon, you can talk?" Sam asked.

"Yes, Sam. I can talk. But I only talk to nice children who feed me and pet me. You and Lily are nice children. Thank you for the bread," Pippa said.

"You are welcome, Pippa. Thank you for talking to us. You are a great pigeon," Sam said.

"Yes, thank you, Pippa. You are a great pigeon. Can we be your friends?" Lily asked.

"Of course, Lily. You and Sam are my friends. You can come and play with me and my pigeon friends anytime. We like you," Pippa said.

Sam and Lily were very happy. They had made a new friend. A talking pigeon. They played with Pippa and the other pigeons until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and promised to come back soon. They never mentioned their secret to anyone. They knew it was special. They knew it was magic.

But Mom saw them. She was angry. She took the cart away. She took the toys out. She said they were naughty. They had to go home. They had no toys. They had no food and milk. They cried. They had a bad day.

Sara and Ben are friends who like to grow plants. They each have a pot with a sunflower seed. They water their seeds every day and put them in the sun.

One day, Sara sees that her sunflower has sprouted a green stem and a tiny leaf. She is very happy and runs to show Ben.

"Look, Ben, my sunflower is growing!" she says.

Ben looks at his pot and sees that his sunflower has not sprouted yet. He feels sad and angry.

"My sunflower is not growing. It is a bad seed. You have a better seed. That is not fair!" he says.

Sara tries to cheer him up.

"Don't be mad, Ben. Maybe your sunflower is just slow. It will grow soon. We can share our sunflowers when they are big and yellow."

Ben does not listen to Sara. He thinks she is lying. He wants to have the biggest and best sunflower. He is very competitive.

He decides to do something sneaky. He waits until Sara is not looking and takes her pot. He puts his pot in its place. He thinks Sara will not notice.

But Sara is very smart. She sees that her pot is gone and that Ben has it. She knows that Ben has switched their pots. She is very angry.

"Ben, give me back my pot! That is my sunflower! You are a bad friend!" she says.

Ben does not want to give back the pot. He thinks he can keep the sunflower. He is very stubborn.

"No, this is my sunflower! You are a bad friend! You gave me a bad seed!" he says.

They start to fight over the pot. They pull and tug and shout. The pot falls to the ground and breaks. The sunflower falls out and wilts. They both stop and look at the sunflower. They feel very sorry.

They look at each other and say:

"I'm sorry, Sara."

"I'm sorry, Ben."

They hug and make up. They decide to plant a new sunflower seed together. They promise to share and care for their sunflower. They learn to be good friends.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play in the pool. They had new swimsuits that their mom bought for them. Ben's swimsuit was blue and Mia's swimsuit was pink. They were very happy and excited to try them on.

They jumped into the pool and started to splash each other with water. They laughed and shouted and had fun. They also played with some toys that floated on the water. They had a ball, a duck, and a lime. The lime was green and sour and smelled good. Ben and Mia liked to squeeze the lime and make funny faces.

"Look at me, I'm a lime monster!" Ben said, holding the lime to his mouth and making a loud roar.

"I'm not scared of you, I'm a lime princess!" Mia said, putting the lime on her head like a crown and making a sweet smile.

They pretended to chase each other with the lime and giggled. They were having so much fun that they did not notice their mom calling them.

"Ben, Mia, time to get out of the pool! It's getting late and you need to dry off and have dinner!" their mom said.

But Ben and Mia did not listen. They wanted to play more with the lime and the water. They ignored their mom and kept splashing and squeezing the lime.

"Ben, Mia, I'm serious, get out of the pool now!" their mom said, louder and angrier.

But Ben and Mia still did not listen. They thought their mom was just joking and they did not want to stop their game. They turned their backs to their mom and kept playing.

Suddenly, they felt a big splash of cold water on their heads. They looked up and saw their mom standing over them with a bucket. She had poured the bucket of water on them to get their attention. She looked very mad and disappointed.

"Ben, Mia, how many times do I have to tell you to listen to me? You are being very rude and naughty. You need to respect me and do what I say. You are not babies anymore, you are big kids. You need to learn to follow the rules and be responsible. Do you understand?" their mom said, sternly.

Ben and Mia felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had made a mistake and hurt their mom's feelings. They nodded and said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We're sorry, mom. We love you, mom."

They hugged their mom and apologized. They got out of the pool and dried off. They put away their toys and their new swimsuits. They followed their mom to the kitchen and had dinner. They ate their food and said thank you. They learned their lesson and promised to listen to their mom next time.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and do what she says. She knows what is best for you and she loves you. Respect her and be polite. Don't be rude and naughty. Have fun, but follow the rules and be responsible.

One day, she sees a big lion sleeping under a tree. She has a silly idea. She wants to use her stripes to scare the lion. She sneaks up to the lion and says in a loud voice, "Boo!"

But the lion is not scared. He opens his eyes and sees Zara. He is angry. He roars and chases Zara. Zara runs away as fast as she can. She is scared.

She runs to her friends and tells them what happened. They are not happy. They tell her that she was silly and foolish. They tell her that lions are dangerous and she could have been hurt. They tell her that she should not use her stripes to play tricks on lions.

Zara feels sorry. She says she is sorry. She says she will not do it again. She says she will only use her stripes to play nice games with her friends. Her friends forgive her. They hug her and say they are glad she is safe. They go to find some grass to eat and some water to drink. Zara is happy. She learned her lesson.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They had a big hoop that they could roll on the grass. Tom liked to make the hoop go fast and far. Lily liked to jump inside the hoop and spin around.

"Look at me, Tom!" Lily said. "I can make the hoop dance!"

Tom looked at Lily and smiled. He wanted to try too. He ran to the hoop and jumped inside. But he was too big for the hoop. He got stuck and felt uncomfortable.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The hoop is too tight! It hurts!"

Lily ran to Tom and tried to help him. She pulled the hoop, but it did not move. She pushed the hoop, but it did not move. She did not know what to do.

"Maybe we can cut the hoop," Lily said. "Then you can get out."

Tom nodded. He saw a pair of scissors on the bench. He asked Lily to get them. Lily ran to the bench and got the scissors. She came back to Tom and cut the hoop. The hoop broke and Tom got out.

"Thank you, Lily!" Tom said. "You are a good friend."

Lily hugged Tom. "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too."

They threw away the broken hoop and went to play with something else. They had fun in the park.

Lily was a little girl who liked to keep her toys in her room. She had many toys, but her favorite was a soft bunny with long ears. She always hugged her bunny when she went to bed. She called her bunny Ear.

One day, Lily's mom told her that they had to move to a new house. Lily was sad and scared. She did not want to leave her room and her toys. She asked her mom, "Can I keep Ear with me?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, you can keep Ear with you. He is your special friend. But you have to pack your other toys in this box, so we can take them to the new house."

Lily nodded and started to pack her toys. She put them in the box, but she kept Ear in her arms. She did not want to let him go. She was afraid that he would get lost or lonely in the box.

The next day, they got in the car and drove to the new house. Lily was sleepy and bored. She closed her eyes and cuddled with Ear. She dreamed of her old room and her old toys.

When they arrived at the new house, Lily woke up and looked around. She saw a big yard with a swing and a slide. She saw a bright room with a window and a bed. She saw her mom and dad smiling and waving at her. She felt happy and excited. She wanted to explore the new house and play in the yard.

She got out of the car and ran to her mom and dad. She hugged them and said, "Thank you for the new house. It is very nice. I like it."

Her mom and dad hugged her back and said, "You're welcome, Lily. We're glad you like it. We love you very much."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too. Can I show you something?"

She ran back to the car and got Ear. She brought him to her mom and dad and said, "This is Ear. He is my special friend. He helped me feel brave and happy. He came with me to the new house. Can he stay with me?"

Her mom and dad looked at Ear and said, "Of course, he can stay with you. He is a very good friend. He can sleep with you in your new bed. He can play with you in your new yard. He can be with you wherever you go."

Lily hugged Ear and said, "Thank you, Ear. You are the best. I'm glad I kept you with me."

The end.

Moral value: Friends can help us cope with change and fear.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: Lily's attachment to Ear is established in the beginning and pays off in the end when he helps her adjust to the new house.

One day, the sky was gloomy and the wind was strong. Tom threw the ball to Lily, but the wind blew it away from her. Lily ran after the ball, but she did not see the cliff. She reached out her hand to grab the ball, but she missed it. The ball went over the cliff and Lily almost fell too.

"Help!" Lily cried. "I'm going to drop!"

Tom heard her and ran to her. He saw her holding on to a small rock with one hand. He was scared, but he was brave. He lay down on the ground and reached out his hand to Lily.

"Take my hand, Lily!" he said. "I'll pull you up!"

Lily was scared, but she was brave too. She let go of the rock and took Tom's hand. Tom pulled her up and hugged her. They were both safe.

"Hello, snake," he said softly. "You are very pretty. What is your name?"

"Hi, Ben," the snake said. "My name is Spot. I am a nice snake. I do not bite. I just want to sunbathe. Do you want to be my friend?"

Ben was surprised. He did not know snakes could talk. He was happy. He wanted to be Spot's friend. He nodded and reached out his hand.

"Yes, Spot, I want to be your friend," he said. "You are a nice snake. Can I touch you?"

Spot nodded and slithered closer to Ben. He let Ben touch his scales. They felt smooth and warm. Ben liked them. He smiled and hugged Spot.

The moral value of the story is: Friendship is a gift that can make us feel less lonely and sad. We can have more than one friend, and we can share our toys and feelings with them. We should be thankful for our friends and show them kindness.

They run to the truck. They climb on the cage. They see a lion, a bear, a monkey, and a snake. The animals are angry. They roar and hiss and growl. Tom and Sam are scared. They want to get down. But the cage is locked. They cannot open it.

"Help! Help!" they shout. "We are stuck!"

A man hears them. He is the driver of the truck. He is angry too. He comes to the cage. He sees Tom and Sam.

"What are you doing here?" he yells. "You are bad boys! You should not touch the truck. You should not bother the animals. You are in big trouble!"

He takes out a key. He opens the cage. He grabs Tom and Sam. He puts them in the back of the truck.

"You are going to jail!" he says. "You will learn your lesson!"

Tom and Sam are fearful. They cry and beg. They do not want to go to jail. They are sorry. They wish they never saw the truck. They wish they never climbed on the cage. They wish they listened to their moms. They hope someone will help them.

One day, Anna found an unknown letter in her mailbox. It was big and red and had no name on it. She was curious and excited. She opened it and saw a picture of a scary clown. The clown had a big nose and sharp teeth and mean eyes. He was holding a balloon that said "I'm coming for you".

Anna was very scared. She screamed and dropped the letter. She ran to her mom and hugged her. She told her about the unknown letter and the scary clown. Her mom looked at the letter and frowned. She said it was a bad joke from someone. She said she would call the police and find out who did it.

Anna was still scared. She did not want to mail letters anymore. She did not want to see the scary clown. She did not want to go outside. She wanted to stay in her bed and hide under the covers. She cried and had bad dreams. She did not feel happy anymore. The unknown letter ruined her fun.

Lily was a pupil in the yellow class. She liked to learn new things and play with her friends. One day, her teacher showed them something interesting. It was a big jar with many shiny stones inside.

"Who wants to touch the stones?" the teacher asked.

Lily raised her hand. She wanted to feel the stones. They looked so pretty and smooth. The teacher smiled and gave her the jar.

"Be careful, Lily. The jar is heavy. Hold it with both hands," the teacher said.

Lily nodded and took the jar. She felt the weight of the stones. She looked at them closely. They had different colors and shapes. Some were round, some were flat, some were pointy. She saw red, blue, green, yellow, and white stones.

Lily wanted to pick one stone and keep it. She thought it would be a nice gift for her mom. She reached her hand inside the jar. She felt the stones with her fingers. She tried to find the most beautiful one.

But then, something happened. The jar slipped from her other hand. It fell on the floor. It broke into many pieces. The stones rolled everywhere. Lily gasped. She was scared and sorry. She dropped the stone she was holding.

"Oh no! I'm sorry, teacher! I'm sorry, everyone!" Lily cried.

The teacher and the other pupils came to help. They picked up the broken glass and the stones. They were not angry with Lily. They knew it was an accident. They told her it was okay.

"Don't worry, Lily. It's not your fault. The jar was too big for you. You didn't mean to break it," the teacher said.

"Thank you, teacher. Thank you, friends. I'm sorry I made a mess. I just wanted to touch the stones. They were so interesting," Lily said.

The teacher hugged Lily. She gave her a tissue to wipe her tears. She also gave her a small stone to keep.

"Here, Lily. This is for you. It's a special stone. It's called a quartz. It sparkles in the light. You can take it home and show it to your mom. I'm sure she will like it," the teacher said.

Lily smiled. She felt better. She thanked the teacher. She looked at the stone. It was clear and shiny. It was the most beautiful stone she ever saw. She put it in her pocket. She was happy. She learned something interesting that day.

Sara was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had a blue dress and long hair. Sara took Anna everywhere with her.

One day, Sara and her mom went to visit her grandma. Sara was happy to see her grandma, who gave her a big hug and a cookie. Sara said, "Thank you, grandma. You are very nice."

Grandma said, "You are welcome, Sara. I am glad you are here. Do you want to play in the garden?"

Sara said, "Yes, please. Can I take Anna with me?"

Grandma said, "Of course, you can. But be careful with her. Don't let her get dirty or wet."

Sara said, "OK, grandma. I will take good care of Anna." She ran to the garden with Anna in her arms.

Sara had fun in the garden. She saw flowers, butterflies, and birds. She made a crown of daisies for Anna and put it on her head. She sang a song to Anna and hugged her.

But then, Sara saw a big dog. The dog was barking and running towards her. Sara was scared. She thought the dog wanted to bite Anna. She held Anna tight and shouted, "Help, help! Go away, dog!"

Grandma heard Sara's cry and came to the garden. She saw the dog and said, "Don't worry, Sara. The dog is not mean. He is my friend. His name is Spot. He just wants to play with you and Anna."

Grandma called the dog and petted him. She said, "Spot, this is Sara and Anna. They are my guests. You have to be gentle with them. Can you say hello to them?"

The dog wagged his tail and licked Sara's hand. Sara felt better. She said, "Hello, Spot. You are a nice dog. I am sorry I was afraid of you. Do you want to play with me and Anna?"

The dog barked and nodded. Sara smiled and said, "OK, let's play. But don't touch Anna's dress or hair. She is very pretty."

Grandma said, "That's very kind of you, Sara. You are a good friend to Anna and Spot. I am proud of you."

Sara, Anna, and Spot played in the garden until it was time to go home. Sara said goodbye to her grandma and the dog. She said, "Thank you, grandma, for the cookie and the fun. I love you."

Grandma said, "You are welcome, Sara. I love you too. Come back soon."

Sara hugged her grandma and her mom. She said, "I had a great day. I made a new friend. His name is Spot. He is a big dog, but he is not mean. He is nice."

Mom said, "That's wonderful, Sara. I am happy for you. You are a brave and sweet girl."

Sara said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. And so is Anna. She is my favorite doll."

Sara kissed Anna and put her in her bag. She said, "Let's go home, Anna. We have a lot to tell daddy."

Tom and Anna were friends. They liked to play in the park and look for treasure. Treasure was anything shiny or pretty that they found on the ground. They had a big box of treasure at home.

One day, Tom said to Anna, "Let's marry when we grow up. Then we can share our treasure and be happy." Anna said, "Yes, let's marry. You are my best friend."

But then, Tom's family had to move to a distant place. Distant means very far away. Tom was sad and Anna was sad. They hugged and said goodbye. They promised to write letters and keep their treasure.

But they did not write letters. They forgot about each other. They made new friends and found new treasure. They grew up and married other people. They were not happy.

They never saw each other again. They never shared their treasure. They never remembered their promise. The end.

Tim was a little boy who liked milk a lot. He drank milk every morning and every night. He had a big cup of milk with his breakfast and a small cup of milk before bed. He did not like to share his milk with anyone.

One day, Tim went to the park with his mom and his sister. His mom packed some snacks and drinks for them. She gave Tim a bottle of milk and his sister a bottle of juice. Tim was happy with his milk and did not want to try the juice. His sister was curious about the milk and asked Tim if she could have a sip.

Tim said no. He held his bottle tight and turned away from his sister. His sister was persistent. She tried to grab the bottle from Tim. They started to fight over the bottle. Tim pulled hard and his sister pushed hard. The bottle flew out of their hands and landed on the ground. The milk spilled out and soaked the grass.

Tim saw his milk was gone. He was very sad and angry. He started to weep. He wept loud and long. He did not listen to his mom or his sister. He did not want to play or eat or drink anything else. He just wept and wept.

The other kids at the park saw Tim weeping. They did not like his noise. They did not want to play with him. They called him a baby and a crybaby. They laughed at him and teased him. Tim felt worse and worse. He wished he had shared his milk with his sister. He wished he had not wept so much. He wished he had been nicer and happier. But it was too late. His milk was gone and his day was ruined. He had a bad ending.

Tim is a tall boy who likes to play with his toys. He does not like to study or do his homework. He thinks he is very smart and does not need to learn new things.

One day, his teacher tells him that he has to get an exam. The exam is about numbers and letters and shapes. Tim does not care. He does not listen to his teacher or his mom. He says he will do well on the exam without studying.

The next day, Tim goes to school and gets the exam. He looks at the questions and does not know the answers. He feels scared and confused. He tries to guess, but he makes many mistakes. He does not finish the exam on time.

When the teacher gives him his exam back, he sees a big red F on it. He feels sad and ashamed. He does not want to show his mom or his friends. He wishes he had studied and listened to his teacher and his mom.

The teacher tells him that he has to study harder and do his homework. She says that he can do better if he tries. She says that being tall does not make him smart. He has to work hard and learn new things.

The moral of the story is: Do not be lazy and arrogant. Study and learn new things. Listen to your teacher and your mom. They want to help you.

"I want to paint my circle yellow," Sue says.

They finish their snack and go back to their circles. But their circles are not soft anymore. They are hard and dry.

"Oh no, our circles are dry!" Tom says.

"They are too tough to paint!" Sue says.

They are sad and angry. They try to break their circles, but they can't. They hurt their hands.

"Who made our circles dry?" Tom asks.

"Maybe the sun did it," Sue says.

They look at the window. The sun is shining bright. They think the sun is mean.

"Sun, why did you make our circles dry?" Tom shouts.

"Sun, please make our circles soft again!" Sue begs.

But the sun does not answer. The sun does not care. The sun keeps shining.

Tom and Sue cry. They hug each other. They wish they had painted their circles before. They learn a lesson. They will not leave their clay shapes on the tray next time. They will paint them right away.

They ran to their mom. She was sitting on the porch. She saw the smoke too.

"Mom, what is that?" Tom and Lily asked.

"That is a volcano. It is a big hole in the ground that sometimes spits out fire and rocks and ash," Mom said.

"Is it dangerous?" Lily asked.

"It can be, but we are far away. We are safe here," Mom said.

"Can we go see it?" Tom asked.

"No, it is too hot and too far. We have to stay here," Mom said.

Tom and Lily were curious, but they listened to their mom. They went back to the garden. They saw some ash falling from the sky. It was gray and soft. They touched it with their fingers.

"It feels funny," Lily said.

"It looks like snow, but it is not cold," Tom said.

They decided to make ash pies instead of mud pies. They mixed the ash with water and put it in their pans. They pretended to bake them in the sun. They smelled them and said they were delicious.

"Would you like some ash pie, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Thank you, but no. I prefer real pie," Mom said.

She smiled and gave them a hug. She was glad they were not worried. She was glad they were having fun.

"Yes, mom, let's go!" Lily said. She grabbed her mom's hand and ran to the car.

At the party, there were many kids and toys and games. Lily had fun playing with Ben and his friends. She showed them her dress and they said it was pretty. She felt happy.

But then, she saw a girl with a dress that looked like hers. It was also pink and shiny and had a big bow on the back. The girl's name was Mia and she was Ben's cousin. She was older and taller than Lily.

"Hey, that's my dress!" Mia said. She walked up to Lily and frowned. "You copied me! You can't wear the same dress as me!"

"No, I didn't copy you!" Lily said. She felt scared and angry. "This is my dress! My mom bought it for me!"

"Well, it's ugly and cheap!" Mia said. She pulled Lily's hair and ripped her bow. "There, now it's different!"

Lily cried out in pain and shock. She felt her dress tear and saw the bow fall to the floor. She felt sad and hurt. She ran to her mom and hugged her.

"Mia, what did you do?" Ben's mom said. She saw Lily's dress and bow and was angry. "That was very mean and rude! You have to apologize to Lily and give her your dress!"

"No, I won't!" Mia said. She stomped her foot and crossed her arms. "This is my dress! I don't care about Lily!"

Ben's mom shook her head and sighed. She took Mia by the hand and dragged her to the car. She said sorry to Lily's mom and left the party.

Lily's mom tried to comfort her and fix her dress. She said it was still beautiful and that Mia was a bad girl. She said they would go home and have ice cream and watch a movie.

But Lily didn't feel brilliant anymore. She felt awful. She hated her dress and she hated Mia. She wished she never went to the party. She wished she never saw that dress.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with many flowers and trees. One day, they decided to explore the path that led to the woods. They took their backpacks and some snacks and set off.

"Look, Ben, a squirrel!" Lila said, pointing to a furry animal that ran up a tree. "It has a big nut in its mouth. I wish I had a nut like that."

Ben smiled and reached into his backpack. He took out a peanut butter sandwich and broke it in half. He gave one half to Lila and said, "Here, this is better than a nut. It has bread and butter and peanut. It is yummy and soft."

Lila took the sandwich and thanked Ben. She bit into it and made a happy sound. She looked at the squirrel again and felt sorry for it. It had to work hard to find nuts and crack them open. She wondered if it had a friend to share with.

She decided to be kind and share her sandwich with the squirrel. She tore off a small piece and threw it towards the tree. But the squirrel was scared and ran away. The piece of sandwich fell to the ground and a bird swooped down and ate it.

"Oops, I dropped it," Lila said, feeling sad. "I wanted to give it to the squirrel, but it did not want it."

Ben hugged Lila and said, "That's okay, Lila. You tried to be nice. Maybe the squirrel was not hungry or maybe it did not like peanut butter. Maybe it was envious of our sandwich and wanted to keep its nut. But we still have more sandwich and we can enjoy it together."

Lila smiled and nodded. She hugged Ben back and said, "You are right, Ben. We have each other and we have sandwich. We are lucky and happy. Let's keep walking and see what else we can find on the path."

They climb up the hill and look at the rocks. They see some shiny ones, some smooth ones, and some colorful ones. Lily picks up a shiny one and says, "Look, this is a mineral. It is shiny and pretty." Ben picks up a smooth one and says, "This is a mineral too. It is smooth and round."

They try to pick up the big rock, but it is too heavy. They pull and tug, but it does not move. They push and shove, but it does not budge. They get tired and frustrated. They start to cry.

A man sees them and comes over. He says, "What are you doing, kids? Why are you crying?" Lily and Ben say, "We want this mineral! It is the best mineral ever! But it is too heavy! We can't move it!"

The man laughs and says, "That is not a mineral, kids. That is a silly sculpture. Someone made it with clay and paint. It is not real. It is just for fun."

The man says, "It's OK, kids. You were just curious and excited. But you should not try to move things that are too heavy. You could hurt yourselves or damage the sculpture. Why don't you play with the other rocks? They are real minerals. You can keep some if you want."

Lily and Ben say, "Thank you, mister. We will play with the other rocks. They are real minerals. They are shiny and smooth and colorful. We like them."

They run to the other rocks and forget about the silly sculpture. They find some more minerals and put them in their pockets. They are happy and have fun.

Tim felt happy. He had a surprise and a gift. He had a mom and a grandma who loved him. He had a teddy bear who was his friend. He was not miserable anymore. He was glad.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room upstairs. One day, their mom tells them to come down for lunch. She says, "I made you some healthy soup and bread. Come and eat, please."

Anna and Ben do not want to stop playing. They say, "No, mom. We are not hungry. We want to play more." They ignore their mom and keep playing with their toys.

Their mom is sad and angry. She says, "Anna and Ben, you are being rude and naughty. You need to eat your healthy soup and bread. It is good for you. If you do not eat, you will get sick and weak. Do you want that?"

Anna and Ben still do not listen. They say, "No, mom. We do not care. We do not like soup and bread. We want to play more." They hide their toys under the bed and pretend they do not hear their mom.

Their mom is very sad and angry. She says, "Fine. If you do not want to eat, you can stay upstairs. But you will not get any dessert or snacks later. And you will not watch TV or read books. You will be bored and hungry. Maybe then you will learn to be polite and grateful."

Anna and Ben do not believe their mom. They think she is joking. They say, "Okay, mom. We do not need dessert or snacks or TV or books. We have our toys. We are happy." They laugh and play with their toys.

But soon, they get tired of playing with the same toys. They start to feel hungry and thirsty. They start to miss their mom and their lunch. They start to feel sorry for being rude and naughty. They say, "Maybe we should go downstairs and eat our soup and bread. Maybe mom will forgive us and give us dessert and snacks and TV and books. Maybe we should say sorry and thank you to mom."

They go downstairs and look for their mom. They see her in the kitchen. She is washing the dishes. She looks sad and tired. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We were rude and naughty. We should have listened to you. We should have eaten our healthy soup and bread. Can we have some now, please?"

Their mom is surprised and happy. She says, "Anna and Ben, I am glad you came downstairs. I am glad you are sorry. I am glad you want to eat your healthy soup and bread. Yes, you can have some now. And you can also have some dessert and snacks and TV and books later. But you have to promise me something."

Anna and Ben say, "What, mom? What do we have to promise?"

Their mom says, "You have to promise me that you will always be polite and grateful. You have to promise me that you will always mention when you are hungry or thirsty or tired or bored. You have to promise me that you will always come down when I call you for lunch or dinner or bedtime. You have to promise me that you will always love me and respect me."

Anna and Ben say, "We promise, mom. We promise. We love you and respect you. You are the best mom in the world."

Their mom says, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. You are the best twins in the world. Now, let's eat our healthy soup and bread and enjoy our time together."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be polite and grateful, to listen to their parents, to eat healthy food, and to communicate their needs and feelings.

"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"

Lily was very sad. She cried and cried. She said, "No, no, no."

Then, she heard a voice. It was the teddy bear. It said, "Don't cry, Lily. I like you too. But I have to stay here with my friends. They will miss me if I go. You can come and visit me anytime. And maybe one day, you can take me home. But for now, can you give me a kiss and say goodbye?"

Lily was surprised. She looked at the teddy bear. It smiled at her. She said, "You can talk?"

The teddy bear nodded. It said, "Yes, I can. But only to you. Because you are special. And you have a big heart."

Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, teddy bear. You are special too. And you have a big bow."

She gave the teddy bear a kiss and said goodbye. She put it back on the shelf. She said, "I will come and see you again. I promise."

The teddy bear said, "I will wait for you. I promise."

The cashier gave Lily a sticker. It had a picture of a teddy bear. Lily was happy. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you."

She put the sticker on her shirt. She said, "Look, mom, I have a teddy bear sticker. It is like my friend."

Her mom smiled. She said, "You are very welcome, Lily. I am proud of you. You were brave and kind. You deserve a sticker."

The people saw Lily and smiled. They said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you."

"What happened here?" she asks. She sees the water on the floor, the toys and the curtain. The curtain is wet, too. Anna and Ben pulled it down when they fell.

"We were playing with the toys, mama, and we made them splash, and then the fish and Anna fell out, and then the curtain fell, too," Ben says. He is eager to explain.

"I see," mama says. She is not angry, but she is not happy, either. She picks up the fish and the curtain. She wraps Anna and Ben in towels. She hugs them and kisses them.

"Next time, be more careful, okay?" she says. "And don't splash so much. You can make a mess, but not a flood."

"Okay, mama, we're sorry," Anna and Ben say. They are sorry, too. They love mama. They love the bath. But they don't love the flood.
