Tom and Mia are scared, but they do not want to give up their game. They say, "No, this is our ball and our hoop. We were here first. You go away, you big bully. You are too rude and too mean to play basketball."

The big boy gets angry. He grabs the ball from Mia and throws it at Tom. The ball strikes Tom in the face. Tom falls down and cries. He has a red mark and a big pain. Mia runs to him and hugs him.

The big boy laughs and says, "Ha ha, that's what you get for being smart. Now, I will take your ball and your hoop and play by myself. You can go home and eat some spicy food. Maybe that will make you stronger and braver."

He takes the ball and the hoop and walks away. Tom and Mia are sad and hurt. They go home and tell their mom what happened. Their mom is angry and sad too. She says, "That big boy is very bad and very wrong. He should not strike you or take your things. He should be nice and share. I will call his mom and tell her what he did. Maybe she will teach him a lesson."

But she does not find his mom. The big boy does not have a mom. He lives in a dark and dirty place with no one to love him or care for him. He is lonely and unhappy. He plays basketball by himself, but he does not have fun. He eats spicy food, but he does not like it. He has a big ball and a hoop, but he has no friends. He is very bad and very wrong, and he has a bad ending.

"Thank you, waiter," Sue said. She took the cup and the napkin. She pretended to sip the juice and wipe her mouth. "This is very good tea."

Tom smiled. He went back to the table to get another cup and napkin. He did not see the cat on the floor. He tripped over the cat and fell down. The juice spilled all over him and the floor. The napkin flew in the air and landed on the stove. The stove was on and the napkin caught fire.

Tom and Sue screamed. They were very scared and worried. The fire alarm went off. The smoke filled the kitchen. Their mom and dad ran into the kitchen. They saw the fire and the mess. They were very angry and sad.

"What have you done?" their mom yelled. "You could have burned the house down!"

"We're sorry, mom," Tom and Sue cried. "We were just playing tea party."

Their mom and dad put out the fire and cleaned up the kitchen. They sent Tom and Sue to their room. They said they were not allowed to play in the kitchen anymore. They said they had to stay in their room until dinner. They said they were very disappointed in them.

Tom and Sue felt very bad. They hugged their dolls and cried. They wished they had not played in the kitchen. They wished they had not served the tea. They wished they had not used the napkin. They wished they had a happy ending.

He took her hand and led her to the car. He drove her to a place where they made waffles. He ordered two waffles with butter and honey. He gave one to Lily and said, "Here you go, Lily. A warm and crispy waffle. Just like mom's. I hope you like it."

Lily took a bite and smiled. She said, "Thank you, dad. I love waffles. And I love you."

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with water. They had a big van that their dad used for work. Sometimes, dad let them use the van to spray water on the plants and the grass. They had a hose that they could attach to the van and make water come out.

One day, they decided to have a game. They wanted to see who could spray more water on the flowers. They took turns to hold the hose and aim at the flowers. Anna went first. She sprayed a lot of water on the red flowers. She was very happy. She said, "I sprayed more water than you, Ben. I win!"

Ben was not happy. He wanted to win too. He said, "No, you did not. I can spray more water than you, Anna. Watch me!" He took the hose from Anna and sprayed water on the yellow flowers. He sprayed so much water that the flowers looked like they were drowning. He said, "See, I sprayed more water than you, Anna. I win!"

Anna was not happy. She wanted to win too. She said, "No, you did not. You sprayed too much water, Ben. You hurt the flowers. That is not fair!" She tried to take the hose back from Ben, but Ben did not let go. They started to pull and tug on the hose. They did not see that the hose was getting loose from the van.

Suddenly, the hose came off the van and water started to spray everywhere. The water sprayed on Anna and Ben, on the van, on the plants, on the grass, and on the dog. The dog barked and ran away. Anna and Ben got wet and cold. They stopped fighting and looked at the mess they made. They felt sorry for the flowers and the dog. They said, "Oh no, what have we done?"

Dad came out of the house and saw the water and the hose and the van and the twins. He was not happy. He said, "What have you done? You wasted a lot of water and you ruined the flowers and the van and the hose. You were too competitive and you did not share. You need to learn to play nicely and to respect nature. Now, you have to clean up this mess and apologize to the flowers and the dog. And no more water games for a week!"

Anna and Ben felt ashamed and sad. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We are sorry, flowers. We are sorry, dog. We will not do it again. We will play nicely and share and respect nature. We love you, dad. We love you, flowers. We love you, dog." They hugged dad and the flowers and the dog. They helped dad to clean up the mess and to fix the hose and the van. They learned their lesson and they never sprayed too much water again.

"Let's unite the screws and make a robot!" Tom said.

"Yes, that sounds lovely!" Anna said.

They took the screws and tried to put them together. They used a hammer and a wrench. They made a head, a body, and two arms for the robot.

"Now we need legs," Tom said.

"I have an idea," Anna said. "Let's use our legs!"

She took two screws and tried to poke them into her shoes. Tom did the same. They thought they looked like robot legs.

"Look, we are robots now!" Anna said.

"Beep boop beep!" Tom said.

They walked around the room, making robot noises. They were having fun.

But then, something bad happened. The screws in their shoes hurt their feet. They started to bleed. They cried out in pain.

"Ow ow ow! The screws are hurting us!" Anna said.

"Help help! We want to take them off!" Tom said.

But they could not take them off. The screws were stuck in their shoes. They could not walk. They could not run. They could not play.

They were very sad. They wished they never found the screws. They wished they never tried to make a robot. They wished they were just friends.

One day, Tommy was crawling under the bookshelf when he heard his mom call him. "Tommy, where are you? It's time for lunch!" Tommy did not answer. He wanted to stay under the bookshelf a little longer. He ignored his mom and kept playing.

But then, he heard a loud noise. It was the bookshelf falling over. Tommy was scared. He felt the books and the wood hit his back and his head. He cried out in pain. "Mommy, help me! I'm under the bookshelf!"

His mom heard his cry and ran to him. She lifted the bookshelf and saw Tommy. He was bleeding and bruised. He looked terrible. She hugged him and said, "Oh, Tommy, I'm so sorry. Are you okay? What were you doing under the bookshelf?"

Tommy sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I was playing. I didn't listen to you. I was bad."

His mom said, "No, Tommy, you're not bad. You're a good boy. But you made a mistake. You have to listen to me when I tell you something. It's for your own good. I love you and I want you to be safe and happy. Do you understand?"

Tommy nodded and said, "I understand, Mommy. I love you too. I won't crawl under the bookshelf anymore. I promise."

His mom kissed him and said, "I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now let's go to the doctor and get you fixed up. And then we can read some of the books together. How does that sound?"

Tommy smiled and said, "That sounds good, Mommy. Thank you."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents. They know what's best for you.

After a few minutes, the swan swam closer and Lily threw some bread to it. The swan ate the bread and then swam away. Lily said, "I believe the swan liked the bread!" Her mom smiled and said, "I think you're right, Lily."

"Don't worry, I will help you get your kitten down," Mr. Smith said. He climbed up the tree and brought Mittens back down to Lily. 

"Thank you so much, Mr. Smith! You saved my Mittens!" Lily exclaimed. 

"You're welcome, Lily. It's always important to help our friends, even if they are small like Mittens," Mr. Smith replied. 

Lily and Mittens went back home, happy and grateful for their kind neighbor.

"No, it's mine!" Tom said. He did not want to give it back. He liked the sticker too. He thought it was great. He wanted it for himself.

"It's okay," Mom said. She wiped their tears. She smiled. "We can fix this. We can glue the paper and the sticker back together. We can share it. We can put it on the fridge. We can all enjoy it."

"Really?" Lily asked. She brightened. She liked that idea.

"Really," Tom said. He nodded. He liked that idea too.

Tom and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big bird with a sharp beak and long claws. It was a wild hawk. The hawk was looking for food. It saw a small mouse running in the grass.

"Look, Mia, a hawk!" Tom said. "It is very fast and strong."

"Yes, Tom, it is. But we are safe here. The hawk will not hurt us," Mia said.

The hawk flew down and tried to catch the mouse. But the mouse was smart and quick. It hid under a rock. The hawk was angry and persistent. It scratched the rock with its claws and pecked it with its beak. It made a lot of noise.

"Go away, hawk! Leave me alone!" the mouse squeaked.

"Shh, mouse, I am hungry. You are my lunch!" the hawk screeched.

Tom and Mia watched the hawk and the mouse. They felt sorry for the mouse. They wanted to help it. They picked up some sticks and stones. They threw them at the hawk.

"Hey, hawk, stop it! The mouse is not your lunch!" Tom shouted.

"Leave the mouse alone! He is our friend!" Mia yelled.

The hawk was surprised and scared. It saw Tom and Mia throwing things at it. It felt a stone hit its wing. It hurt. It decided to give up. It flew away.

The mouse came out of the rock. It was safe. It was grateful to Tom and Mia. It thanked them.

"Thank you, Tom and Mia. You are very brave and kind. You saved me from the hawk," the mouse said.

"You are welcome, mouse. We are glad you are okay. You are very smart and quick," Tom said.

"Yes, you are. We are happy to be your friends," Mia said.

Tom and Mia smiled. The mouse smiled. They became friends. They played together in the park. They had fun.

Sam was a little boy who liked to play in the garden. He liked to dig and plant and water the flowers. One day, he found a big, brown root in the soil. He wondered what it was and where it came from. He decided to take it home and show his mom.

He ran to the kitchen, where his mom was making soup. He put the root on the table and said, "Look, mom, what I found!" His mom looked at the root and frowned. She said, "Sam, this is not a good root. This is a bad root. It is from a weed that makes people sick. You should not touch it or eat it. You should throw it away."

Sam was confused and sad. He liked the root. He thought it was interesting and fun. He did not want to throw it away. He said, "But mom, maybe it is not a bad root. Maybe it is a good root. Maybe it can make soup better. Can I stir it in the soup?"

His mom said, "No, Sam, you cannot stir it in the soup. It will make the soup bad and make us sick. You have to listen to me. I know what is good and what is bad. You do not know. You are too little. You have to trust me."

Sam did not listen to his mom. He waited until she was not looking and he sneaked the root into the soup pot. He stirred it in the soup and smiled. He thought he was clever and brave. He thought he would surprise his mom and make her happy.

But he was wrong. When his mom tasted the soup, she spat it out and said, "Yuck! This soup is awful! What did you do, Sam?" She saw the root in the pot and said, "Oh no! You put the bad root in the soup! How could you, Sam? You did not listen to me. You did not trust me. You did a bad thing."

Sam felt ashamed and sorry. He saw his mom was angry and sad. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to make you happy. I thought the root was good. I did not know it was bad. I did not mean to make you sick. Please forgive me."

His mom hugged him and said, "I forgive you, Sam. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to listen to me and trust me. I love you and I want you to be safe and healthy. Sometimes, things that look good are bad. Sometimes, things that are unknown are dangerous. You have to be careful and wise. Do you understand?"

Sam nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I love you too. I will listen to you and trust you. I will not put bad roots in the soup again. I will be careful and wise."

Bunny was a little rabbit who liked to hop. He hopped all day in the grass and the flowers. He had many friends who hopped with him. They played games and had fun.

One day, Bunny saw a big fence. He wondered what was behind it. He hopped closer and saw a sign. The sign had big letters. Bunny could not read them, but he saw a picture of a rabbit with a red cross. He did not know what it meant.

He asked his friend Mouse, who was good at reading. Mouse said, "The sign says, 'No rabbits allowed. This is the farmer's garden. He has a law that rabbits cannot hop here. He will be angry if he sees you.'"

Bunny was curious. He wanted to see the garden. He said, "I will hop over the fence. It is not fair that the farmer has a law. I want to see the flowers and the carrots. Maybe I can take one for a snack."

Mouse said, "No, Bunny, don't do that. It is dangerous. The farmer has a dog who barks and chases rabbits. He also has a trap that can hurt you. You should hop away and find another place to play."

But Bunny did not listen. He was brave and silly. He hopped over the fence and landed in the garden. He saw many beautiful flowers and tasty carrots. He smiled and hopped towards them.

But then he heard a loud bark. He turned and saw a big dog running towards him. He was scared and tried to hop back to the fence. But he was too late. The dog was faster and caught him. He bit him and shook him. Bunny cried and wished he had listened to Mouse.

The farmer heard the noise and came out. He saw the dog and the rabbit. He was angry and shouted, "Bad dog! Bad rabbit! You are breaking my law! You are ruining my garden! Go away and never come back!"

He took the dog and the rabbit and threw them over the fence. Bunny landed on the grass. He was hurt and tired. He saw Mouse waiting for him. Mouse said, "Bunny, are you okay? I told you not to hop over the fence. It was a bad idea. You are lucky to be alive."

Bunny said, "I'm sorry, Mouse. You were right. I was wrong. I should have followed the law. It was there to keep me safe. I will never hop over the fence again. I learned my lesson."

Mouse said, "I'm glad you are sorry. I'm your friend and I care about you. Come on, let's hop home and rest. You need to heal your wounds and get some sleep."

Bunny nodded and hopped with Mouse. He was happy to have a good friend. He decided to be more careful and smart. He realized that hopping was fun, but not when it was against the law.

Mom and Dad said they had another surprise for Lily. They took her to a place where there were many dogs. Lily loved dogs. She saw big dogs and small dogs, black dogs and white dogs, fluffy dogs and smooth dogs. She wanted to pet them all.

Mom and Dad said they had a special dog for Lily. They showed her a brown dog with floppy ears and a wagging tail. The dog was very friendly. He licked Lily's face and wagged his tail more. Mom and Dad said the dog was a gift for Lily. They said he needed a home and a family. They said Lily could name him and take care of him.

Lily was very excited. She hugged the dog and said his name was Spot. She said thank you to Mom and Dad. She said Spot was her new best friend. She said she would feed him and walk him and play with him. She said she would care for him a lot.

Mom and Dad smiled. They said they were proud of Lily. They said she was a good big sister and a good dog owner. They said they loved her and Ben and Spot. They said they were a happy family. They said Lily and Spot were welcome in their home. They said they had one more surprise for Lily.

They gave Lily a big backpack. They said it was for her school. They said she would start school soon and learn many new things. They said she would make many new friends. They said they would miss her but they would always be there for her.

Lily was a little scared. She said school was a big place and she did not know anyone. She said she would miss Mom and Dad and Ben and Spot. She said she did not want to go.

Mom and Dad hugged Lily. They said they understood. They said school was a big change and it was normal to feel scared. They said they felt scared too when they started school. They said school was also a fun place and a good place. They said they would help her get ready and they would take her and pick her up. They said they would always support her and cheer for her.

Lily felt better. She said she would try school and see how it was. She said she would be brave and curious. She said she would still love Mom and Dad and Ben and Spot. She said she would tell them all about school.

Mom and Dad said they were happy. They said they loved Lily very much. They said she was a smart and kind girl. They said they were lucky to have her.

Lily smiled. She said she loved Mom and Dad very much. She said they were the best parents. She said she was lucky to have them.

They all hugged. They said they were a happy family. They said they cared for each other a lot. They said they were ready for school and for anything. They said they had each other and that was enough.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with dolls and cars. One day, they see a big poster at school. It says there is a contest. The contest is to draw a picture of your favorite animal. The best picture will get a prize.

Lily and Ben want to win the prize. They ask their teacher to explain the contest. The teacher says they have to use crayons and paper. They have to draw an animal they love. They have to write their name on the paper. They have to give the paper to the teacher by Friday.

Lily and Ben go home and start to draw. Lily loves cats. She draws a cat with orange fur and green eyes. She writes "Lily" on the paper. Ben loves dogs. He draws a dog with black fur and brown eyes. He writes "Ben" on the paper. They are happy with their pictures.

On Friday, they bring their pictures to school. They give them to the teacher. The teacher says thank you and puts them on the wall. Lily and Ben look at the other pictures. There are many pictures of animals. There are lions, birds, fish, and more. Some pictures are big and some are small. Some pictures are colorful and some are not.

The teacher says it is time to choose the winner. She asks the class to vote. They have to raise their hand for the picture they like the most. Lily and Ben hope their pictures will win. They look at the wall and wait.

The teacher counts the votes. She says the winner is... Ben! Ben's picture of the dog is the most popular. The class claps for Ben. Ben is very happy. He jumps up and down. The teacher gives him the prize. It is a book about dogs. Ben loves the prize. He says thank you to the teacher and the class.

Lily is sad. She wanted to win the prize. She thinks her picture of the cat is good too. She looks at the wall and sees her picture. She sees that some people voted for her picture. She feels a little better.

Ben sees that Lily is sad. He is a good friend. He goes to Lily and says, "I like your picture of the cat. It is very pretty. Do you want to see my book about dogs? We can share it." Lily smiles. She says, "Yes, I want to see your book. Thank you for sharing it. You are a good friend." Ben and Lily hug. They sit down and look at the book together. They are happy.

One day, a little shrimp was swimming in the sea. He was looking for food and friends. He saw a big fish with sharp teeth. The fish saw him too and opened his mouth. The little shrimp was scared and trembled.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "The big fish wants to eat me!"

He swam as fast as he could, but the big fish was faster. He was about to catch the little shrimp, when a bigger fish came out of nowhere and bit the big fish. The big fish let go of the little shrimp and swam away.

"Thank you! Thank you!" the little shrimp said to the bigger fish. "You saved me!"

The bigger fish smiled and said, "You're welcome, little shrimp. I'm not a bad fish. I'm a whale. I don't eat shrimps. I eat krill. Do you want to be my friend?"

The little shrimp was happy and said, "Yes, I want to be your friend. You are very kind and brave. What is your name?"

The whale said, "My name is Wally. What is yours?"

The little shrimp said, "My name is Shelly. Nice to meet you, Wally."

They swam together and became good friends. They found food and more friends in the sea. The little shrimp was not scared and trembled anymore. He was glad he met Wally the whale.

Tom and Ann are twins. They like to play with their toys. But sometimes they fight over them. One day, they both want to play with the same doll. The doll has a dress made of wool. It is soft and pretty.

"Give me the doll!" Tom says. He pulls the doll from Ann's hands.

"No, it is mine!" Ann says. She pulls the doll back from Tom's hands.

They pull and pull until the doll's dress rips. The wool comes out and falls on the floor. The doll looks sad and naked.

"Oh no!" Tom and Ann say. They feel sorry for the doll. They do not want to fight anymore.

"Let's repair the doll's dress," Tom says. He finds some glue and some paper.

"Let's make a new dress," Ann says. She finds some scissors and some cheap fabric.

They work together to fix the doll. They glue the paper on the wool to stop the hole. They cut the fabric and wrap it around the doll. They make a bow and a button.

"There, the doll is happy again," Tom says.

"And so are we," Ann says.

They hug each other and the doll. They share the doll and play nicely. They learn to be kind and helpful.

Anna and Ben liked to play with the rope in the park. They would swing on it, jump over it, and make shapes with it. One day, they saw that the rope was broken. It had a big hole in the middle.

"Oh no, our rope is ruined!" Anna said. "Who did this?"

"I don't know, maybe a dog or a bird," Ben said. "Can we fix it?"

They tried to tie the ends of the rope together, but it was too short and loose. They tried to wrap the rope around a stick, but it was too thick and hard. They tried to find another rope, but they could not see any.

They were sad and angry. They did not want to play with anything else.

Then, they saw a man walking by with a new rope. He was wearing a modest hat and a modest coat. He smiled at them and said, "Hello, children. Do you like ropes?"

"Yes, we love ropes, but our rope is broken," Anna said, pointing at the hole.

"That's too bad. Do you want to replace it?" the man said, holding out his new rope.

"Really? Can we have your rope?" Ben said, his eyes wide.

"Sure, why not? I have plenty of ropes at home. This one is for you," the man said, giving them his rope.

"Wow, thank you so much! You are very kind!" Anna and Ben said, hugging the rope.

"You're welcome. Have fun with it. And remember, be careful and share," the man said, waving goodbye.

Anna and Ben were very happy. They thanked the man again and ran to the park. They played with the new rope all day. They swung on it, jumped over it, and made shapes with it. They also let other children play with it. They learned that replacing something broken can make you happy, and that being modest and generous can make others happy.

One day, Sara's mom told her they had to go to the store. Sara wanted to bring her crown with her, but her mom said no. She said the crown was too big and could get lost or broken. She said Sara had to leave it at home. Sara was sad, but she did what her mom said.

Sara and her mom went to the store and bought some things. Sara saw many things she liked, but her mom said they had no money for them. Sara was bored and wanted to go home. She missed her crown.

When they came back home, Sara ran to her room to get her crown. But she could not find it. She looked everywhere, but it was gone. She started to cry. She asked her mom where her crown was.

Her mom said she did not know. She said maybe someone took it. She said they had to call the police. Sara was scared. She did not understand why someone would take her crown. Sara and Ben were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. Spot was a nosy dog who liked to sniff everything. He saw a big hole in the fence and ran to it. He wanted to see what was on the other side.

"Spot, come back!" Sara shouted. "You don't know what's there!"

But Spot did not listen. He squeezed through the hole and ran away. Sara and Ben followed him. They saw him barking at a cat on a tree. The cat was scared and hissed at Spot.

"Spot, stop it!" Ben said. "You are being mean to the cat!"

But Spot did not stop. He jumped and tried to catch the cat. The cat climbed higher and higher on the tree. Then the cat slipped and fell. He was hanging by his neck from a branch. He was in trouble.

"Help! Help!" the cat cried.

Sara and Ben felt sorry for the cat. They wanted to rescue him. They looked for something to help. They saw a ladder near a house. They ran to get it. They put the ladder against the tree. Sara climbed up the ladder. She reached the cat and untangled him from the branch. She held him in her arms and climbed down.

"Thank you, thank you!" the cat said. "You saved me!"

"You're welcome," Sara said. "Are you okay?"

"Yes, I'm okay," the cat said. "But I'm scared of that dog. He is very nosy and rude."

"I'm sorry," Ben said. "He is our dog. He was just curious. He didn't mean to hurt you."

"Curious or not, he should learn to be nice to others," the cat said. "And you should watch him better. He could get into trouble or cause trouble."

"You're right," Sara said. "We will be more careful with him. And we will teach him to be friendly and polite."

They took the cat and the ladder back to the house. They knocked on the door and gave the cat to his owner. The owner was happy to see his cat. He thanked Sara and Ben for their help. He gave them some cookies and milk as a reward.

Sara and Ben went back to the park with Spot. They gave him some cookies too. They told him what happened and how he should behave. Spot wagged his tail and licked their faces. He was sorry for being nosy and mean. He promised to be a good dog from now on.

The end.

Moral value: Being nosy can get you into trouble or hurt others. You should be respectful and kind to everyone.

Tommy loved to play with his toy fireman and his fire truck. He liked to pretend that he was a brave fireman who saved people and animals from fires. He also liked to soak his fire truck with water from his hose, to make it look like he was putting out real fires.

One day, Tommy saw a big cloud of smoke in the sky. He ran to his mom and said, "Mom, look! There is a fire! Can we go see it?" His mom said, "No, Tommy, it is too dangerous. We have to stay away from fires. They can hurt us and burn things. The real firemen will take care of it."

But Tommy was curious and did not listen to his mom. He sneaked out of the house with his fire truck and his hose. He followed the smoke until he saw a big fire in a building. He saw the real firemen working hard to put out the fire. He wanted to help them, so he ran towards the fire with his hose.

But he did not know that the fire was too hot and too big for his hose. He also did not see the enormous hose that the firemen were using. It was much bigger and stronger than his hose. As he got closer to the fire, the firemen saw him and shouted, "Stop! Go back! It is not safe!" But Tommy did not hear them. He kept running with his hose.

Suddenly, the enormous hose sprayed a lot of water on the fire. The water was so powerful that it knocked Tommy down and soaked him and his fire truck. Tommy was scared and wet and cold. He started to cry. The firemen ran to him and picked him up. They wrapped him in a blanket and took him to his mom.

His mom was very worried and angry. She hugged him and said, "Tommy, what were you thinking? You could have been hurt or burned by the fire. You should have listened to me and stayed away from the fire. You are not a real fireman. You are a little boy who needs to be careful and obey your mom."

Tommy felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to be a brave fireman and help the firemen. But I was not brave. I was foolish and reckless. I learned my lesson. I will never go near a fire again. And I will always listen to you and do what you say."

His mom said, "I'm glad you learned your lesson, Tommy. I love you and I want you to be safe and happy. Maybe when you grow up, you can be a real fireman. But for now, you have to be a good boy and play with your toys at home."

Tommy nodded and said, "I love you too, mom. And I'm sorry for soaking my fire truck. Can we dry it and play with it later?" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can. But first, let's go home and change your clothes. You are still soaked." Tommy agreed and went home with his mom and his fire truck. He thanked the firemen for saving him and said goodbye. He never forgot that day and the lesson he learned.

"Wow, you have a lot of things in your sack," Ben said.

"Distant places are places that are far away," the man said. "Like the park, or the zoo, or the beach. Do you like to go to distant places?"

The little bird forgave him and they became friends again. From that day on, the raven never insisted on keeping all the food to himself and always shared with his friends. They all lived happily ever after in the big tree. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy octopus named Ollie. Ollie loved to sleep all day and never did any work. One day, Ollie's friend Sammy the crab came to visit.

"Ollie, why are you always sleeping? You should raise your tentacles and do something fun!" said Sammy.

But Ollie just yawned and said, "I don't feel like it."

Later that day, Ollie and Sammy went for a swim. As they were swimming, they saw a big rock. Ollie wanted to rest on the rock, but when he got there, he saw that there were lots of clams on it. Ollie was too lazy to move them, so he just lay down on top of them.

Suddenly, the clams started to open their shells and pinch Ollie's tentacles! Ollie quickly realized that he should have listened to Sammy and raised his tentacles to do something fun instead of being lazy all day.

They started to argue and pull the bananas and cookies. Their mom saw them and said, "Stop that, you two. You are making a mess. You can't have everything you want. You have to share and be nice." She took away the bananas and the cookies and put them back on the shelf.

Tom and Lily felt sad and sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were being bad kings and queens. We don't want to fight anymore. Can we have something else, please?" Their mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But you have to agree on what you want. How about some apples? They are juicy and red."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, apples are good. We like apples. They are good for our teeth and our kingdom." They hugged their mom and took some apples. They paid for them and went home. They ate their apples and played nicely. They learned to be good kings and queens. The end.

But on the way, their car got stuck in a lot of traffic. There were too many cars and trucks and buses on the road. They had to wait and wait and wait. Tom and Sue got bored and tired and hungry.

"Soon, I hope, Tom. We just have to be patient. There is a delay on the road. Something happened up ahead. Maybe an accident or a broken car." Dad said.

"But I want to see the boats now!" Sue said. "And I want a snack. I'm hungry."

"I know, Sue. Me too. But we have to stay in the car. It's not safe to get out. And we don't have any snacks. We were going to buy some at the harbor." Dad said.

Tom and Sue started to cry. They didn't like the delay. They didn't like the traffic. They didn't like the car. They wanted to go to the harbor.

Then, they saw something different. Something bright and colorful and noisy. It was a fire truck. It had red lights and a loud siren. It was going to the place where the delay was. It was going to help.

"Look, Tom, look, Sue. A fire truck!" Dad said. "Maybe it will clear the road soon. Maybe we will get to the harbor after all."

Tom and Sue stopped crying. They looked at the fire truck. They liked the fire truck. It was different. It was fun. It was cool.

"Wow, a fire truck!" Tom said.

"Wow, a fire truck!" Sue said.

They smiled and clapped. They forgot about the delay. They forgot about the traffic. They forgot about the car. They remembered the harbor. They were happy and excited again.

Ben and Mia are playing in the garden. They see a big hole in the fence. They want to know what is on the other side.

"Let's go and look," says Ben.

"OK, but be careful," says Mia.

They crawl through the hole and find a big field with many animals. They see cows, sheep, pigs and chickens. They are very happy and run around.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a farmer with a big dog. He is angry and shouts at them.

"Hey, you kids, get out of my field! You are scaring my animals!"

He runs towards them with his dog. Ben and Mia are scared and try to run back to the hole. But they are too late. The farmer has put a trap near the hole. It is a big cage with a door that closes when something goes inside.

Ben and Mia run into the trap and the door shuts behind them. They are trapped and cannot get out. They cry and hug each other.

"Help, help, let us out!" they scream.

The farmer comes and looks at them. He is not so angry now. He sees that they are just children who were curious.

"Sorry, kids, I didn't mean to scare you. I put this trap here to catch some foxes that have been eating my chickens. You are not foxes, you are just silly."

He opens the trap and lets them out. He gives them a warm blanket and some cookies. He tells them to be more careful and not to go into other people's fields.

Ben and Mia say sorry and thank him. They promise not to do it again. They go back to the garden and tell their mom what happened. She is glad that they are safe and hugs them. She tells them to play nicely and not to make trouble. They agree and play with their toys. They are happy and warm.

"Give me the acorn!" Lily said.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said.

They pulled and tugged at the acorn. They were both very selfish. They did not want to share.

Suddenly, the acorn slipped from their hands. It rolled down the hill and into a hole. They ran after it, but they could not reach it.

"Oh no, we lost the acorn!" Lily cried.

"It's your fault!" Ben shouted.

They were both very sad and angry. They did not talk to each other. They went home alone.

Instead, they saw something amazing. In the hole where the acorn had rolled, a tiny green sprout had grown. It had two little leaves and a small bud.

"Look, it's a baby oak tree!" Lily said.

"It's beautiful!" Ben said.

They realized that the acorn had planted itself in the soil. It had used the sun and the rain to grow. It was going to bloom into a big and strong oak tree.

They felt ashamed of their selfishness. They had fought over a silly acorn, and they had almost lost their friendship. They had not seen the magic of nature.

They looked at each other and smiled. They held hands and said sorry.

"Can we be friends again?" Lily asked.

"Of course we can!" Ben said.

They hugged and laughed. They decided to take care of the baby oak tree together. They watered it, sang to it and watched it grow. They learned to share and to be kind. They were happy again.

When they got back to the park, Lily and her mom tried to fly the kite. But it was hard! The wind was strong and the kite kept falling. Lily was sad. She said, "Mommy, I don't know how to do it." Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. We'll keep trying. The power of practice will help us fly the kite. And maybe one day, we'll discover the unknown power of the wind!"

Once upon a time, in a furry forest in the east, there lived a small rabbit named Bobo. Bobo had many friends, but his best friend was a big bear named Buzzy. They liked to play and have fun together.

One day, Bobo and Buzzy were playing near the river when they saw a little bird crying. "Why are you sad?" asked Bobo. The little bird said, "I can't fly! My wing is hurt, and I need to go home." Bobo and Buzzy looked at each other and knew they had to help.

Buzzy told Bobo, "I will support the bird, and you can lead the way." So, Bobo hopped in front, and Buzzy gently carried the little bird on his back. They walked through the furry forest, helping the bird get back to its nest.

As they walked, they heard a loud noise. A big, mean wolf was blocking their way! The wolf growled, "You can't pass! This is my part of the forest!" Buzzy looked at Bobo, and they knew they had to be brave for their new friend.

Bobo hopped up to the wolf and said, "Please, let us pass. We are trying to help our friend go home." The wolf saw the hurt bird on Buzzy's back and felt sorry for them. He let them pass and even said sorry for being mean. Bobo, Buzzy, and the little bird thanked the wolf and continued on their way. They finally reached the bird's nest, and the little bird was happy to be home. Bobo and Buzzy knew they had done a good thing, and they went back to playing in their furry forest in the east.

Matt was scared and put the scissors back in the grass. He said sorry to the old man and asked who did the scissors belong to. But the old man just said that was an unknown mystery. 

Then, the old man gave Matt a kind smile and said, "If you really want to have a pair of scissors, why don't you save your pocket money and go buy your own." 

Matt smiled and thanked the old man before walking away. He realized that although he still didn't know who the scissors belonged to, he could still buy his own so he could cut paper for art projects and make cool things. 

The end.

David felt happy that he had buried the medicine. Now nobody else would find it because it was deep in the ground. He stepped back and admired his hard work. Everyone said that the little boy was so intelligent!

Once upon a time, there was a hippo who lived near the lake. Every day he liked to bounce around the lake and meet his neighbors. He had two neighbors, a giraffe and a lion. One day the lake got very dry and the hippo couldn't bounce anymore. He made a plan to get water for the lake. 

The hippo asked his neighbors to help him. The giraffe and the lion said yes and all three of them worked together. The giraffe ran to the river and filled his long neck with water. The lion used his strong paws to carry the water from the river. Then the hippo bounced to the lake and used his wide mouth to pour out the water. 

The lake was filled with fresh water! Everyone was so happy and the hippo was able to bounce around the lake again. The hippo, giraffe and lion became great friends after that and were the best of neighbors.

Once there was a mommy and a baby. The baby was very happy playing, but then the mommy gave him a pinch. The baby felt a terrible pinch in his muscle. It was a very sharp feeling and it made him cry. The mommy said, "It's ok, it was just a pinch!" But the baby didn't know what a pinch was. 

He looked around and saw his mommy pinch her own muscle. This time it was soft, not sharp at all. She then said, "See, that's a gentle pinch. Not like the pinch I gave you before - that was a terrible pinch!" 

The baby nodded and then tried to pinch his own muscle. It wasn't sharp, but it still felt funny. He smiled and waved his pinchy finger around. The mommy laughed and said, "Yes, that's right! Now you know what a pinch is!" 

The baby smiled, happy to understand his funny new feeling. Now he knew that there were gentle pinches and terrible pinches, and he was sure to never get the wrong kind again.

Once there was an old man who wanted to go fishing. He needed help, so he asked his 3 year-old grandson. "Can you come fishing with me?" he said.

The little boy replied, "Yes, Grandpa." So they went and the old man set up the boat. He put food and some bait in the boat.

The old man cast out the line and nothing happened. He set out the line again, but again he got no bites.

The old man said, "I think I need a tip." The little boy replied, "What is a tip, Grandpa?"

The old man said, "A tip is when you give advice. My advice is for you to try using dull bait. Dull bait can catch bigger fish." 

So the little boy found dull-coloured bait and put it on the line. After a few minutes, he felt a strong tug and shouted, "I got one! I got one!" 

The old man was proud of the little boy, who caught the biggest fish of them all.

The sailor was so thankful to the fish. He wished he could do something to show his gratitude. So, the sailor promised to give the fish lots of food and a new home.

The sailor brought the fish back to the port and gave it a big feast. From then on, the fish and the sailor became best friends. The sailor was so happy that his new friend had saved his life. They were very wealthy indeed!

Once upon a time, there was a big, smart elephant. He wanted some cream to eat. He asked the little mouse nicely, "Please, can I have some cream?" The mouse said, "Yes, of course!" He gave him a big tub of cream. 

The elephant was very excited and started to eat it right away. But it was so delicious that he wanted MORE. He asked the mouse again, "Please, can I have some more cream?" The mouse said, "Sure! You are so intelligent!"

The elephant was so happy that he ate the cream with a smile and thanked the mouse. He said, "Thank you very much!" and the mouse said, "You're welcome!" 

From then on, the elephant and the mouse were good friends who shared cream food whenever they met. They had lots of fun and were very happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a bright pond. It was very big and sparkled in the sun.

Everyday, a duck came to the pond to get a drink and a snack. The duck quacked and said "Please, pond, please give me something to eat". 

The pond rippled and bubbled, but it could not talk. Instead, a big fish popped out of the water! It splashed around and waved its fin at the duck.

The duck said "Please, fish, can you give me something to eat?" The fish smiled and opened its mouth. Suddenly, the duck found lots of tasty insects inside!

The duck said "Thank you, fish! Please come back soon." The fish swam back into the pond and the duck flew away with a full belly. 

The pond sparkled even brighter in the sun.

Lily and Ben like to play with blocks. They make towers with the blocks. They see who can make the tallest tower. Lily makes a red tower. Ben makes a blue tower. They are both very proud of their towers.

But then, Max comes. Max is a big boy. He is rough. He does not like to share. He sees the towers and says, "I want those towers. They are mine. I own them." He pushes Lily and Ben away. He grabs the towers and breaks them. He laughs and says, "Ha ha, now they are no towers. They are just blocks."

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They cry and say, "No, Max, that is not nice. You do not own the towers. We made them. You broke them. You are mean." They try to get the blocks back, but Max is stronger. He pushes them again and says, "Go away. These are my blocks. I own them."

But then, Miss Rose comes. Miss Rose is the teacher. She sees what Max did. She is not happy. She says, "Max, what are you doing? Why did you break Lily and Ben's towers? Why did you take their blocks? Why are you rough with them?"

Max is scared. He says, "I don't know. I just wanted the towers. They are pretty. I own them."

Miss Rose says, "No, Max, you do not own the towers. You do not own the blocks. They belong to the class. We share them. You have to ask before you take something. You have to be gentle and kind. You have to say sorry to Lily and Ben. You have to help them make new towers."

Max feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry, Lily and Ben. I'm sorry, Miss Rose. I was wrong. I will share the blocks. I will be gentle and kind. I will help you make new towers."

Lily and Ben forgive Max. They say, "It's okay, Max. We are glad you are sorry. We can be friends. We can make new towers together."

Miss Rose smiles. She says, "That's good, Max. That's good, Lily and Ben. You are learning to play nicely. You are learning to own your mistakes and fix them. You are learning to own your feelings and express them. You are learning to own your words and use them. You are good children. I am proud of you."

"Lily won't share her sunglasses!" Ben said.

Mom looked at them and shook her head. She was not happy with their behavior.

"Ben, you know you can't take things that don't belong to you. That's not nice. You have to give Lily's sunglasses back to her," Mom said.

"But I want sunglasses too!" Ben said.

"I understand, Ben, but you can't take Lily's sunglasses. They are hers. Maybe you can ask her nicely if you can borrow them for a little while. Or maybe you can find something else to play with. There are many fun things in the park," Mom said.

She turned to Lily and said, "Lily, I know you like your sunglasses, but you can also be kind and generous to your brother. Maybe you can let him wear them for a little while. Or maybe you can trade with him. You can wear his hat and he can wear your sunglasses. How does that sound?"

Lily and Ben thought about what Mom said. They realized that they were being mean and selfish to each other. They felt sorry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have taken your sunglasses. Here, you can have them back," Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I shouldn't have yelled at you. Here, you can wear my sunglasses for a little while. And I can wear your hat. It's a nice hat," Lily said.

They hugged and said sorry to each other. They also said sorry to Mom.

Mom smiled and hugged them too. She was proud of them for making up and being nice to each other.

"That's better. I'm glad you two are friends again. Now, let's go and have some fun in the park. Are you ready?" Mom said.

"Yes, we are ready!" Lily and Ben said.

They put on their hats and sunglasses and ran to the slides. They had a lot of fun in the park. They also learned to share and care for each other. Mom was happy to see them happy. She recommended that they always be kind and respectful to each other. And they agreed.

Lily was a princess who liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but she always wanted more. She asked her mom and dad for new toys every day. They gave her some toys, but not all. They said she had enough toys and she should share them with others.

Lily did not like to share. She said her toys were hers and no one else could touch them. She hid her toys in her room and locked the door. She played alone with her toys and did not talk to anyone. She was not happy.

One day, a new girl came to the castle. Her name was Mia. She was a princess too, but she had no toys. She had lost her toys when her home was burned by a dragon. She was sad and lonely. She wanted to make friends and play with other children.

Lily saw Mia and felt curious. She wanted to see what Mia had in her bag. She sneaked into Mia's room and opened her bag. She found nothing but a book and a doll. The book was old and torn. The doll was dirty and missing an eye. Lily laughed and said, "These are not toys. These are trash. You are a poor princess. You have nothing."

Mia heard Lily and felt hurt. She ran to her bag and hugged her book and doll. She said, "These are not trash. These are my treasures. They are the only things I have left from my home. They make me happy. You are a mean princess. You have everything, but you are not happy."

Lily felt ashamed. She realized she had been rude and selfish. She had many toys, but she did not appreciate them. She had no friends, because she did not share. She said, "I'm sorry, Mia. You are right. I have been mean and selfish. I have many toys, but I am not happy. I want to be your friend. Can I play with you?"

Mia smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You can play with me. You can also play with my book and doll. They are available for you. I like to share. Sharing makes me happy."

Lily and Mia became friends. They played together with their toys and books. They learned from each other and had fun. They were happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Having more things does not make you happy. Having friends does make you happy.

Sara liked to play with water. She had a big tub of water in the garden. She also had many toys that she could soak in the water. She liked to see how they got wet and made bubbles.

One day, she saw a new toy in her room. It was a wooden horse with a long mane and a tail. It was very pretty and shiny. Sara wanted to play with it. She took it to the garden and put it in the tub of water. She said, "Hello, horse. Do you like water? I will soak you and make you clean."

But the horse did not like water. It started to swell and crack. The mane and the tail came off. The paint peeled and faded. The horse looked very sad and ugly. Sara was shocked. She did not know that water could hurt the horse. She took it out of the tub and tried to dry it with a towel. But it was too late. The horse was ruined.

Sara started to cry. She ran to her mom and showed her the horse. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I soaked the horse and it broke. I wanted to play with it. I didn't know."

Mom hugged Sara and said, "It's okay, honey. You didn't mean to hurt the horse. You were curious and wanted to have fun. But some toys are not meant for water. They are made of wood or paper or cloth. They can get damaged by water. You have to be careful and gentle with them."

Mom took Sara to her room and opened a drawer. She said, "Look, Sara. I have a surprise for you. I found this old toy in the attic. It was mine when I was a little girl. It is a soft and fluffy bear. It is very mild and cuddly. You can play with it and hug it and sleep with it. It doesn't mind water, but it doesn't need it either. It just needs your love."

Sara smiled and took the bear. She said, "Thank you, Mom. I love the bear. It is very nice and cozy. I'm sorry for the horse. Can we fix it?"

Mom said, "Maybe we can. We can try to glue it and paint it. But it will never be the same as before. It will always have scars and marks. But that doesn't mean it is worthless. It means it has a story. And it can still be your friend, if you want."

Sara nodded and said, "I want. I will be kind to the horse and the bear. And to all my toys. They are all special to me."

Mom kissed Sara and said, "I'm proud of you, Sara. You are a good and sweet girl. Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. And then we can play with your toys together."

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, books and games to have fun with. But sometimes they also liked to explore other parts of the house, especially when their mom and dad were busy.

One day, they decided to sneak into their parents' bedroom, where they saw a big bed, a closet, a dresser and a nightstand. On the nightstand, there was a shiny object that caught their eyes. It was an alarm clock, with numbers, buttons and a bell. Tom and Lily thought it was very attractive and wanted to touch it.

"Look, Lily, what is this?" Tom asked, reaching for the alarm clock.

"I don't know, Tom, maybe it tells time?" Lily guessed, following him.

They picked up the alarm clock and started to press the buttons. They heard different sounds, like beeps, rings and music. They giggled and smiled, thinking it was a fun toy.

But they did not know that they were also disturbing their mom and dad, who were taking a nap in the bed. Their mom and dad heard the loud noises and woke up with a start. They saw Tom and Lily holding the alarm clock and making a mess.

"Tom! Lily! What are you doing?" their mom asked, in a stern voice.

"Sorry, mom, we were just playing with this," Tom said, showing the alarm clock.

"That's not a toy, that's an alarm clock. It's for waking up in the morning, not for making noise in the afternoon. You disturbed our nap and you could have broken it," their dad said, in a firm voice.

"Sorry, dad, we didn't know. It looked so attractive and we were curious," Lily said, in a small voice.

Their mom and dad sighed and took the alarm clock from them. They explained to them that some things in the house were not for playing with, and that they should always ask before touching them. They also told them to be quiet and respectful when someone was sleeping or working. Tom and Lily felt sorry and apologized. They hugged their mom and dad and promised to be more careful next time. Then they went back to their room, where they played with their own toys, books and games.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They also saw many insects, like ants and bees and butterflies. Ben liked to chase the insects and try to catch them. Lily liked to watch them and talk to them.

"Hello, little ant," Lily said to an ant that was carrying a leaf. "Where are you going with your leaf?"

The ant stopped and looked at Lily. "I am going to my home with my leaf," the ant said. "My home is under the ground. I have many friends there. We share our leaves and food."

"That is very nice of you," Lily said. "You are very generous. Can I see your home?"

The ant nodded. "Yes, you can. But you have to be careful. There are many dangers in the park. Some birds and animals like to eat ants. And some people like to step on ants. You have to watch out for them."

"OK, I will," Lily said. She followed the ant to a small hole in the ground. She bent down and peeked inside. She saw many ants working and playing and eating. They looked happy and busy.

"Wow, you have a very nice home," Lily said. "Thank you for showing me."

"You are welcome," the ant said. "You are very kind. Do you want a leaf?"

Lily smiled. "No, thank you. I have my own food. But I appreciate your offer. You are very generous."

Ben came running to Lily. He had a jar in his hand. He had caught a butterfly and put it in the jar. He was very proud.

"Look, Lily, look what I caught," Ben said. "It is a beautiful butterfly. I am going to keep it as my pet."

Lily frowned. She did not like what Ben did. She thought it was mean.

"Ben, that is not nice," Lily said. "The butterfly does not want to be in the jar. The butterfly wants to be free. The butterfly has a home and friends too. You should let it go."

Ben shook his head. "No, I want to keep it. It is mine. I caught it."

Lily sighed. She did not know what to do. She looked at the ant. The ant looked at her. The ant had an idea.

"Ben, I have a question for you," the ant said. "Do you like insects?"

Ben nodded. "Yes, I do. I like to catch them and look at them. They are fun and interesting."

The ant smiled. "Then, I have a gift for you. I will show you something very special. Something that you have never seen before. Something that only insects can see. Do you want to see it?"

Ben nodded again. He was curious. He liked surprises. He put the jar down and followed the ant. Lily followed them too.

The ant led them to a big flower. The flower was yellow and bright. The ant climbed on the flower and told Ben and Lily to look closely. They did. They saw something amazing. The flower had many colors and patterns that they could not see before. The flower was like a rainbow.

"This is what insects see," the ant said. "We see more colors than people. We see the beauty of the flowers and the plants. We see the secrets of nature. We see the magic of life."

Ben and Lily gasped. They were amazed. They had never seen anything like that. They felt happy and grateful.

"Wow, this is wonderful," Ben said. "Thank you for showing us. You are very generous."

"You are welcome," the ant said. "You are very brave. You are not afraid of insects. You are not afraid of learning new things. But you have to remember. Insects are not toys. Insects are not pets. Insects are living beings. They have feelings and needs and rights. They deserve respect and freedom. Just like you."

Ben nodded. He understood. He felt sorry for the butterfly. He ran back to the jar and opened it. He let the butterfly go. The butterfly flew away. It looked happy and free.

"Bye, butterfly," Ben said. "I am sorry for catching you. I hope you find your home and friends. I hope you have a good life."

The butterfly fluttered its wings and thanked Ben. It flew to the flower and joined the other insects. They all smiled and thanked Ben and Lily. They all said goodbye.

Ben and Lily waved to the insects. They felt happy and proud. They had learned a lot. They had made new friends. They had been generous and kind.

They went back to their mom. She hugged them and asked them what they did. They told her everything. She smiled and praised them.

Tom and Mia like to play with their kayak. It is a big toy boat that they can sit in and paddle on the water. They have a yellow kayak and a blue paddle. They like to go to the lake with their mom and dad and kayak together.

One day, they see a big fish in the water. It is gray and shiny and has a long tail. Tom and Mia are curious and want to see the fish better. They paddle closer to the fish and lean over the kayak.

"Look, Mia, it is a big fish!" Tom says.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Mia says.

They watch the fish swim around the kayak. Then, Tom has an idea. He takes the paddle and pokes the fish gently with it. He wants to make the fish move faster.

"Hey, fish, are you slow?" Tom says.

But the fish does not like to be poked. It splashes the water with its tail and makes a loud noise. Tom and Mia get wet and scared. They drop the paddle and sit back in the kayak.

"Tom, why did you poke the fish?" Mia says.

"I wanted to see it swim faster. I did not mean to make it angry." Tom says.

"Sorry, fish, we did not want to hurt you." Mia says.

The fish swims away from the kayak. Tom and Mia look for their paddle. They see it floating near the shore. They paddle with their hands and get the paddle back. They are happy to have their paddle again.

They decide not to poke any more fish. They paddle back to their mom and dad and tell them what happened. Their mom and dad hug them and dry them with a towel. They say they are proud of them for being brave and kind.

Tom and Mia learn a lesson. They learn that fish do not like to be poked. They learn to respect the animals in the lake. They still like to kayak, but they do not poke any more fish. They only watch them and say hello.

Tom and Ben were friends who liked to play with marbles. They had many marbles of different colors and sizes. Some were shiny, some were dull, some were smooth, some were rough. But Tom's favorite marble was a brilliant blue one that sparkled in the sun. He never let anyone touch it or play with it. He kept it in a special box in his room.

One day, Ben came to Tom's house to play. He saw the brilliant blue marble in the box and wanted to see it. He asked Tom, "Can I look at your blue marble? It is so pretty."

Tom said, "No, you can't. It is mine and only mine. You might break it or lose it or keep it. Go away and play with your own marbles."

Ben felt sad and angry. He thought Tom was mean and selfish. He waited until Tom was not looking and took the blue marble from the box. He ran outside and hid behind a tree. He looked at the blue marble and smiled. He thought, "Now I have the prettiest marble. Tom will be sorry."

But then he heard a loud bark. A big dog came running towards him. The dog saw the blue marble and thought it was a ball. The dog jumped and snatched the blue marble from Ben's hand. He bit it hard and crushed it with his teeth. The blue marble broke into pieces and fell to the ground.

Ben screamed and cried. He tried to get the blue marble back, but it was too late. The dog ran away with some of the pieces in his mouth. Ben looked at the broken blue marble and felt sorry. He thought, "I should not have taken Tom's marble. It was wrong and mean. Now I have nothing and Tom has nothing."

He went back to Tom's house and told him what happened. Tom was very angry and sad. He said, "You are a bad friend. You stole my blue marble and ruined it. I don't want to play with you anymore. Go away and don't come back."

Ben left and walked home. He felt lonely and guilty. He thought, "I wish I had been a good friend. I wish I had let Tom keep his blue marble. I wish I had not been greedy and selfish. I learned a hard lesson today. I hope Tom will forgive me someday."

The moral of the story is: Don't take what is not yours. Be a good friend and share. Greed and selfishness can lead to loss and sorrow.

The people inside had done bad things and had to go to a place where they could not have fun or see their families. They had lost their life.

Lily felt sorry for the people in the orange car. She wished they could be happy and free like her. She decided to wave at them again, even if they didn't wave back. She wanted to show them that someone cared about them. She wanted to give them a little bit of life.

Sam smiles and says, "You are a good hider, Mia!" Mia says, "You are a good seeker, Sam!" They hug and laugh. They are happy. They like to play hide and seek. The sun is shining and the air is mild. It is a good day to play in the park.

One day, Tom went to the park with his mom and Hero. He saw a girl with a doll and a boy with a truck. He wanted to play with them, but they did not want to share their toys. Maybe they don't like your car, but you do, and that's what matters. You should not try to take their toys, because that is not nice. You should ask them nicely if you can play with them, and maybe they will allow you to. And if they don't, you can find other kids who will. There are many kids in the park who would love to play with you and Hero."

Tom listened to his mom and felt sorry for being mean. He said, "You are right, mom. I should not be mean. I should be kind. I will ask them nicely if I can play with them. And if they don't want to, I will find other kids who do. Thank you, mom. You are the best."

He learned that he should respect and share his toys, and others will do the same. He learned that his car, Hero, was not weird, but special. Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big snowman in the park. He had a green hat, a carrot nose, and a comb in his mouth.

"Wow, look at the snowman!" Tom said. "He is so funny and cool!"

"Can we touch him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, why not?" Tom said. "But be gentle, he might melt."

They ran to the snowman and touched his hat, his nose, and his comb. They felt cold and wet.

"Ouch, this comb hurts!" Lily said. "Why does he have a comb in his mouth?"

"Maybe he likes to brush his teeth," Tom said. "Or maybe he is a barber."

They laughed and played with the snowman. They made him a scarf, a belt, and a pair of glasses. They had a lot of fun.

But then, the sun came out and shone brightly. The snowman started to melt. His hat fell off, his nose drooped, and his comb slipped out.

"Oh no, the snowman is melting!" Tom said. "We have to save him!"

"How?" Lily asked.

"Maybe we can put him in the shade," Tom said. "Or maybe we can find some ice."

They looked around, but they could not find any shade or ice. The snowman melted more and more. He lost his scarf, his belt, and his glasses. He became a small pile of snow.

Tom and Lily felt sad. They liked the snowman. He was their friend.

They heard a voice behind them. It was the old man who lived near the park. He had a kind face and a long beard.

"Hello, children," he said. "Did you enjoy playing with the snowman?"

"Yes, we did," Tom and Lily said. "But he melted. We could not save him."

The old man smiled. "Don't be sad," he said. "The snowman was happy to play with you. He gave you his hat, his nose, and his comb. He wanted you to have them."

He handed them the green hat, the carrot nose, and the comb. "These are for you," he said. "You can keep them as a memory of the snowman. And maybe, when it snows again, you can make another snowman and play with him."

Tom and Lily smiled. They thanked the old man. They put on the hat, the nose, and the comb. They looked funny and cool.

They learned that snowmen are not forever, but friendship is. They also learned to be grateful for the gifts they receive. They hugged the old man and each other. They were happy.

They laughed and admired themselves in the mirror. They felt like pirates who had found a great treasure.

But then they heard Mom coming up the stairs. They got scared. They knew they had done something wrong. They quickly took off the jewelry and threw it back in the drawer. They closed the drawer and ran to their bed.

Mom entered the room and smiled at them.

"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" she asked.

"Nothing, Mom. Just playing," Lily and Tom said.

Lily and Tom learned a lesson. They realized that entering the drawer and touching the jewelry was not fun. It was wrong and risky. They decided to play with their own toys and respect Mom's things. They felt happier and safer.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big gate. The gate is tough. It is made of metal. It has a lock.

"Let's number the gate," Tim says. He likes to count things.

"OK," Sam says. He likes to play with Tim.

Tim starts to number the gate. He points to each part of the gate and says a number.

"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten," he says.

Sam watches him. He thinks Tim is smart.

"Can you number the gate too?" Tim asks Sam.

Sam nods. He tries to number the gate. He points to each part of the gate and says a number.

"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten," he says.

But he makes a mistake. He points to the same part twice. He says ten twice.

Tim laughs. He sees Sam's mistake.

"Sam, you said ten twice. That's not right. You have to say eleven," he says.

Sam feels sad. He thinks he is not smart.

"Sorry, Tim. I don't know eleven. I only know ten," he says.

Tim stops laughing. He sees Sam's sad face.

"It's OK, Sam. Don't be sad. I can teach you eleven. Eleven is after ten. It's one more than ten. Look, this is eleven," he says.

He points to another part of the gate and says eleven.

"Eleven," Sam repeats. He smiles. He learns a new number.

"Good, Sam. You are smart. You can number the gate too. Let's number the gate together," Tim says.

He holds Sam's hand. They number the gate together. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, he went to the park with his mom and saw a big hill. He wanted to go down the hill on his scooter. He asked his mom, "Can I go down the hill, mom?"

His mom looked at the hill and said, "It's too steep, Sam. You might fall and hurt yourself. Why don't you ride on the flat path instead?"

But Sam did not listen. He thought he could do it. He said, "No, mom. I can do it. I'm powerful on my scooter." He pushed his scooter to the top of the hill and got ready to go down.

He started to go down the hill, but soon he realized it was too fast and scary. He tried to stop, but his brakes did not work. He screamed, "Help, mom! Help!"

His mom ran after him and shouted, "Reverse, Sam! Reverse! Turn your scooter around and go back up the hill!"

Sam did not know what reverse meant, but he tried to turn his scooter around. He twisted the handle and pushed with his feet. He managed to reverse his scooter and go back up the hill. He was still scared, but he felt relieved.

He reached the top of the hill and hugged his mom. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I should have listened to you. I don't like the hill. It's too steep."

His mom hugged him back and said, "It's okay, Sam. I'm glad you're safe. You're powerful on your scooter, but you also need to be careful and follow the rules. Next time, let's ride on the flat path, okay?"

Sam nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you for helping me. I love you."

They got on their scooters and rode on the flat path. They had fun and enjoyed the park. Sam learned his lesson and never went down the hill again. He also learned a new word: reverse.

"Mia, I'm hungry," Ben said. "Can we have some food?"

They walked to the kitchen and saw their mom making a sandwich. She smiled and said, "Hi, kids. Do you want some food?"

Mom cut the sandwich in half and put some grapes and crackers on the side. She handed the plate to Mia and Ben and said, "Here you go. Enjoy your food."

"Thank you, mom," Mia and Ben said. They started to eat their food and talk about their game.

"Mom, can we go outside after we finish our food?" Mia asked. "We want to play with our bikes."

"Sure, honey, but you have to wear your helmets and stay close to the house," mom said. "It's getting dark and I don't want you to go too far."

"Me too," Mia said. She wiped her mouth and put her plate in the sink.

"Okay, kids, but be careful and come back soon," mom said. She kissed them and watched them run to the door.

They had fun and forgot about the time. They didn't notice the moon was rising and the stars were shining. They only heard their mom calling them from the porch.

Mia and Ben heard mom and stopped their bikes. They looked at the sky and saw how dark it was. They realized they had played for a long time. They felt tired and sleepy.

Ben likes music. He likes to sing and dance and play his drum. But Ben is deaf. He cannot hear the music or the words. He only feels the beat and the vibrations.

The match fell on their clothes and set them on fire. Tom and Sue ran and rolled on the ground. They tried to put out the fire.

Their mom heard their screams and came to the backyard. She saw them on fire and ran to help them. She used a blanket to smother the fire. She hugged them and checked their burns. She was very angry and scared. She took them to the hospital to get treated.

Tom and Sue learned a hard lesson. They learned that fire is not a toy and matches are not for fun. They learned that fire can hurt them and others. They learned that playing with fire is not attractive, but dangerous. They said sorry to their mom and promised to never play with fire again.

Then they saw a man they did not know. He was a stranger. He had a big bag and a hat. He looked at Tom and Anna and smiled. He walked towards them.

"Hello, little ones," he said. "Do you want to see what I have in my bag? I have some toys and candy for you. Come with me and I will show you."

Tom and Anna felt scared. They did not want to go with the stranger. They did not like his smile. They remembered what their mom and dad had told them. They said, "No, thank you. We have to go home now. Bye."

They picked up their ball and ran away. They ran as fast as they could. They hurried to find their mom and dad. They were sitting on a bench nearby. They were reading a book.

"Mom, dad, we saw a stranger!" Tom and Anna said. "He wanted us to go with him. He had a big bag and a hat. He said he had toys and candy. But we said no and we ran away."

Mom and dad hugged Tom and Anna. They were proud of them. They said, "You did the right thing, Tom and Anna. You are very brave and smart. You should never go with a stranger. You should always stay with us or someone you know and trust. We love you very much."

Mom and dad nodded. They were cheerful. They said, "Yes, you can play some more. But stay close to us, okay?"

Tom and Anna agreed. They played with their ball again. They had fun and laughed. They forgot about the stranger. They enjoyed the park.

"OK," Tom said. "But how do we make a wish?"

Lily thought for a moment. Then she said, "We can blow a dandelion. That's what my mom told me. She said if you blow a dandelion and make a wish, it will come true."

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. If you are greedy and mean, you will lose your friends and make your family unhappy. If you are generous and polite, you will have peace and joy.

They went to grandma's house. Grandma was happy to see them and gave them hugs and cookies. She said they could stay with her until they found a new house. She said they were lucky and brave. She said the fire was rare and not their fault.

Sam slept in grandma's bed with his teddy bear. He still felt sad and angry. He missed his house and his toys and his books. He dreamed of the fire and the ash and the smoke. He woke up and cried.

Grandma heard him and came to his bed. She held him and his teddy bear. She said she was sorry and she loved him. She said they would get new things and make new memories. She said his teddy bear was special and he could keep it forever. She said he could sleep with her as long as he wanted.

Sam felt a little better. He hugged his grandma and his teddy bear. He said he loved them too. He said he was sorry for the fire and the ash and the smoke. He said he hoped the firemen were okay. He said he wanted to sleep with grandma and his teddy bear. He closed his eyes and slept.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big puzzle with many pieces. They wanted to make the picture of a farm with animals and trees.

Lily and Ben started to fit the pieces together. But soon they had a problem. They both wanted the same piece. It was a piece with a cow and a flower. Lily said, "It is mine! I saw it first!" Ben said, "No, it is mine! I need it for my side!" They pulled and pushed the piece, but it did not break.

They were very selfish. They did not think about the other. They did not think about the puzzle. They only thought about themselves. They did not use their brains to find a solution. They only used their hands to fight.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the puzzle and the piece. She saw Lily and Ben. She was not happy. She said, "Why are you fighting over one piece? There are many pieces in the puzzle. You can share and take turns. You can work together and make the picture. You can have fun and be happy. But if you are selfish and greedy, you will not finish the puzzle. You will not have fun. You will not be happy. You will only make each other sad and angry."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They knew their mom was right. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were selfish and greedy. We did not use our brains. We will share and take turns. We will work together and make the picture. We will have fun and be happy. We will not make each other sad and angry."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "That is good, Lily and Ben. I am proud of you. You learned a lesson today. You learned that being selfish and greedy is not good. You learned that being kind and generous is good. You learned that using your brain is better than using your hands. You learned that working together is better than fighting alone. You learned that sharing and taking turns is better than grabbing and keeping. You learned that having fun and being happy is better than being sad and angry."

Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They thanked their mom and went back to the puzzle. They shared and took turns. They worked together and made the picture. They had fun and were happy. They did not make each other sad and angry. They used their brains and not their hands. They were not selfish and greedy. They were kind and generous. They were good twins.

"Let's go and see the vase," Lily whispered to Max. "But we have to be quiet. Mommy said it is very old and we can't break it."

They tiptoed to the table and reached for the vase. It was heavy and cold. They looked inside. It was empty.

"Maybe we can put something in it," Max whispered to Lily. "Like flowers or toys or candy."

They ran to their room and came back with some things. They put a daisy, a car, a ball, and a lollipop in the vase. They smiled and clapped.

"Look, we made the vase pretty and fun," Lily whispered to Max.

But then they heard Mommy coming. She walked into the living room and saw the vase. She gasped and frowned.

"Who did this?" she asked in a loud voice. "Who put these things in my vase?"

Lily and Max hid behind the couch. They felt scared and sorry. They whispered to each other.

"We did it, Mommy," Lily whispered. "We wanted to make the vase happy. It was empty and sad."

"We didn't mean to be bad, Mommy," Max whispered. "We like the vase. It is shiny and blue."

Mommy sighed and shook her head. She took the things out of the vase and put them back in their room. She picked up the vase and hugged it.

"I know you like the vase, kids," she said in a soft voice. "But it is not a toy. It is very old and fragile. It belonged to my grandma. She gave it to me before she went to heaven. It is very special to me. It is not empty and sad. It is full of memories and love."

She put the vase back on the table and smiled. She called Lily and Max and hugged them too.

"I love you, kids," she said. "But please don't touch the vase again. OK?"

"OK, Mommy," Lily and Max said. "We love you too. And we love the vase. We are sorry we made you angry."

They kissed Mommy and the vase. They learned a lesson. They played with their own toys and left the vase alone.

But then, Timmy's loyal dog, Max, found the toy dinosaur and brought it back to Timmy. Timmy was so happy and hugged Max tightly. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always wear his toy dinosaur securely on his shirt so he wouldn't lose it again. The end.

Suddenly, a little blue car arrived at the intersection. The silly driver didn't see it and he crashed into the little blue car. 

Everyone was okay, but the silly driver felt very bad. He realized he needed to be more careful when driving on the street.

His friend was very curious and asked if he could have a blue carrot too. Benny thought for a moment and then said, "I don't have any more blue carrot seeds, but I can share some of my carrots with you."

Once upon a time, there was a monkey named Max who lived in the jungle. Max loved to climb trees and eat bananas. One day, Max met a parrot named Polly. Polly said, "Max, have you heard about the new printing machine in the jungle?"

Max did not know what a printing machine was, so Polly explained, "It's a machine that can make copies of pictures and words on paper."

Max was curious, so he went to see the printing machine. He saw a pile of spoiled bananas nearby and had an idea. He asked the printing machine to print a picture of a banana. Soon, Max had a whole pile of paper bananas to eat!

From that day on, Max visited the printing machine often, printing pictures of his favorite things like trees and bananas. He was a happy monkey, and Polly was happy too because she had made a new friend.
