Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Quackers. Quackers lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Quackers saw a big purple flower near the pond. He wanted to go see it, but his mama said, "No, Quackers, it's not safe to go alone."

Quackers was sad, but then his friend, a frog named Ribbit, said, "I'll come with you, Quackers!" So they hopped over to the flower together. When they got there, they saw that the flower was covering something. "What's under there?" asked Quackers.

"I don't know," said Ribbit. "Let's uncover it!" They pushed the flower aside and saw a shiny rock. "Wow!" said Quackers. "It's so pretty!"

Just then, Mama Duck came over and saw the rock. "That's a special rock," she said. "It's called an amethyst. It's purple like the flower you found, Quackers." Quackers was so happy that he found something special with his friend Ribbit. They covered the rock back up with the flower and went back to the pond to tell their friends all about their adventure.

"Come on, Ben, let's go!" Lily said. She crawled out of the bush and ran towards the door. But Ben did not follow. He was stuck under the bush. He tried to crawl out, but the branches were too tight. He cried for help.

He crawled and crawled, but he could not get out. He wished Lily would come back. He wished the storm would stop. But it did not. The storm was too strong. The bush was too weak. The lightning struck the bush. The bush caught fire. Ben screamed. But no one heard him. He burned. He died. The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big clock that their dad gave them. The clock had a face, two hands, and many numbers. It made a tick-tock sound every second. Tom and Lily liked to watch the clock and learn how to tell time.

One day, Tom and Lily had a fight. They wanted to play with the clock at the same time, but they did not want to share. They pulled and pushed the clock, trying to take it from each other. They did not listen to their mom, who told them to stop and be nice. They were angry and selfish.

Then, something bad happened. The clock broke. The face cracked, the hands fell off, and the numbers scattered. The clock did not make any sound. Tom and Lily were shocked and sad. They had destroyed their favorite toy. They looked at each other and felt sorry. They realized they had been foolish and mean.

They hugged and said sorry to each other. They also said sorry to their mom and dad, who came to see what happened. Their mom and dad were not happy, but they forgave them. They told them that the clock was not just a toy, but a gift of love and time. They said that time was precious and could not be fixed. They said that they should always cherish time and use it well. They said that they should always be sweet and kind to each other, because they were family and friends.

Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They promised to share and care for their toys and each other. They also helped their mom and dad to clean up the mess. They hoped that one day, they could find a new clock that was as beautiful and fun as the old one. But they knew that the most important thing was not the clock, but the love and time they had together.

Tom was a prince who lived in a big castle. He liked to play with his toys and his dog, Rex. Rex was a mighty dog who could run fast and bark loud. Tom and Rex were best friends.

One day, Tom and Rex went to the garden to have a picnic. Tom had a basket with bread, cheese and apples. Rex had a bowl with meat and water. They found a nice spot under a tree and laid a blanket on the grass.

"Let's feed each other, Rex," Tom said. "You can have some of my bread and cheese, and I can have some of your meat."

Rex wagged his tail and licked Tom's face. He liked the idea of sharing food with his friend. He took a bite of the bread and cheese and gave it to Tom. Tom took a bite of the meat and gave it to Rex.

They ate and ate until they were full. Then they lay down on the blanket and looked at the sky. They saw clouds that looked like animals and shapes.

"Look, Rex, that cloud looks like a dragon," Tom said. "And that one looks like a castle."

Rex barked and nodded. He saw the clouds too. He imagined that he and Tom were flying on the dragon and visiting the castle.

They closed their eyes and dreamed of their adventures. They were happy and content. They were a prince and a mighty dog who loved each other.

Anna and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks. The ducks were swimming and quacking. Anna and Ben liked the ducks. They wanted to feed them some bread.

Mom gave them some bread and said, "Be careful. Don't go too close to the water. And don't throw the bread too hard. The ducks might get scared."

Anna and Ben nodded. They broke the bread into small pieces and tossed them to the ducks. The ducks came closer and ate the bread. They looked happy.

But one duck was naughty. He wanted more bread. He saw Anna's bottle of juice on the grass. He ran to the bottle and bit the cap. He tried to drink the juice.

Anna saw the naughty duck and shouted, "Hey! That's my juice! Give it back!"

She ran to the duck and tried to grab the bottle. But the duck was faster. He ran away with the bottle. He quacked loudly.

Ben saw the naughty duck and laughed. He said, "Look! The duck likes your juice!"

Anna was angry. She said, "No! The duck is naughty! He took my juice!"

She chased the duck around the pond. The duck was clever. He dodged and ducked. He made Anna run and run.

Mom saw Anna and the duck. She said, "Anna, stop! You can't catch the duck. He is too fast. And you might fall into the water. Come here. I have more juice for you."

Anna stopped. She was tired and thirsty. She said, "OK, Mom. But the duck is naughty. He should say sorry."

Mom smiled. She said, "Maybe he will. But he is also hungry. He likes your juice because it is sweet. Maybe you can share some with him."

Anna thought for a moment. She said, "OK, Mom. I can share some juice with the duck. But only a little bit."

She walked to the duck and held out the bottle. The duck saw the bottle and quacked. He came closer and sniffed the bottle. He licked the cap.

Anna said, "Here, duck. You can have some juice. But not too much. And you have to say sorry."

The duck looked at Anna and nodded. He drank some juice and then gave the bottle back to Anna. He quacked softly.

Anna said, "Thank you, duck. And I'm sorry too. I didn't mean to scare you. You are cute."

The duck smiled and wagged his tail. He said, "Quack, quack."

Anna and the duck became friends. They fed each other some bread and juice. Ben and Mom joined them. They all had a fun time at the pond.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to taste new things. He tasted fruits, vegetables, cheese, bread, and even some dirt. He wanted to know how everything tasted. But one day, he saw something shiny and red on the stove. It looked like a toy. He reached out his hand to touch it and taste it.

"Ow!" Tommy cried. "It hurts! It hurts!" He dropped the shiny thing and ran to his mom. His mom saw his hand was red and blistered. She hugged him and said, "Oh, Tommy, what did you do? That was a hot pot. It was not a toy. It was very dangerous. You could have burned yourself badly."

She took him to the sink and ran cold water over his hand. Then she wrapped it in a bandage and called the doctor. The doctor said they had to go to the hospital. Tommy was scared. He did not like the hospital. He did not want to go.

On the way to the hospital, they saw a big truck with a siren and a ladder. It was a fire truck. Tommy liked fire trucks. He liked the firemen who wore helmets and coats and boots. He wondered what they tasted like. He asked his mom, "Mom, can I taste a fireman?"

His mom smiled and said, "No, Tommy, you can't taste a fireman. Firemen are not for tasting. They are for helping. They help people who are in trouble. They put out fires and rescue people and animals. They are very brave and kind. They make people feel safe."

Tommy thought about what his mom said. He realized that he had been in trouble because he tasted something he should not have. He felt sorry for being naughty. He said, "Mom, I'm sorry I tasted the hot pot. I won't taste things that are not food anymore. I want to be safe. And I want to be like a fireman. I want to help people and be brave and kind."

His mom kissed him and said, "I'm glad you learned your lesson, Tommy. I love you very much. And I'm sure you can be a good fireman when you grow up. But for now, you have to be careful and listen to me. And you have to go to the hospital and let the doctor check your hand. OK?"

Tommy nodded and said, "OK, Mom. I will be careful and listen to you. And I will go to the hospital and let the doctor check my hand. And I will say thank you to the firemen if I see them. Because they are not for tasting. They are for helping."

The end.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run, swing and slide. They also liked to look for bugs and flowers. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw something new in the park. It was a big box with a hole in it. It was on the side of the path. They were curious. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go and look," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Mia said.

They walked to the box and peeked inside. They saw a lot of shiny things. There were balls, books, toys and clothes. They were happy. They wanted to play with them.

"Wow, look at all these things!" Ben said.

"Who do you think they belong to?" Mia asked.

"I don't know. Maybe someone left them here for us," Ben said.

He reached for a ball and threw it in the air. Mia reached for a book and opened it. They smiled.

Suddenly, they heard a voice. It came from the hole.

"Hey, what are you doing with my stuff?" the voice said.

They were scared. They looked at the hole. They saw a face. It was a boy. He was older than them. He looked angry.

"Who are you?" Ben asked.

"I'm Sam. This is my box. I live here. This is all I have. You can't take it," Sam said.

He climbed out of the box and grabbed the ball and the book. He put them back in the box. He glared at Ben and Mia.

"Go away. Leave me alone," he said.

Ben and Mia felt sorry for Sam. They wondered why he lived in a box. They wondered where his family was. They wondered if he had any friends. They felt bad for taking his things.

"We're sorry, Sam. We didn't know. We just wanted to play," Mia said.

"Yeah, we're sorry. We won't bother you again," Ben said.

They turned to leave. But then they stopped. They had an idea. They looked at each other. They nodded. They were thoughtful.

"Wait, Sam. We have something for you," Mia said.

She took out a cookie from her pocket. She gave it to Sam.

"Here, this is for you. It's yummy," she said.

Ben took out a sticker from his pocket. He gave it to Sam.

"Here, this is for you. It's pretty," he said.

Sam looked at the cookie and the sticker. He was surprised. He didn't expect anything from them. He felt a warm feeling in his chest. He smiled.

"Thank you, Ben and Mia. That's very nice of you," he said.

He took the cookie and the sticker. He put them in his box. He looked at Ben and Mia. He felt a new feeling in his heart. He felt friendly.

"Do you want to play with me?" he asked.

Ben and Mia smiled. They nodded. They wanted to play with him.

"Sure, Sam. We'd love to," they said.

They went to the box and looked inside. They saw a lot of shiny things. They also saw a new friend. They were happy. They played together.

Sara is a big girl. She likes to do things by herself. She is independent. She can brush her teeth, put on her clothes, and eat her breakfast. But there is one thing she cannot do by herself. She cannot take a bath.

Every night, Mama helps Sara take a bath in the bathtub. Sara likes the warm water and the bubbles. She likes to play with her rubber duck and her boat. But she does not like when Mama washes her hair. She says it hurts her eyes and makes her cry.

One night, Sara has an idea. She says to Mama, "Mama, I want to own the bathtub. I want to take a bath by myself. I am a big girl. I can do it."

Mama smiles and says, "Sara, you are a big girl. But you are not big enough to own the bathtub. The bathtub is for everyone in the house. And you still need my help to take a bath. I will be gentle when I wash your hair. I promise."

Sara pouts and says, "No, Mama. I want to own the bathtub. I want to be independent. Please, Mama. Please."

Mama thinks for a moment. She says, "Okay, Sara. I will let you own the bathtub for tonight. But you have to follow some rules. You have to stay in the water. You have to use soap and shampoo. And you have to let me check on you every few minutes. Do you understand?"

Sara nods and says, "Yes, Mama. I understand. Thank you, Mama. Thank you."

Mama fills the bathtub with water and bubbles. She gives Sara her rubber duck and her boat. She says, "Have fun, Sara. But be careful. I will be back soon."

Sara smiles and says, "Okay, Mama. I will be careful. I love you, Mama."

Mama says, "I love you too, Sara. Enjoy your bathtub."

She hears Mama knock on the door. She says, "Sara, are you ready to get out of the bathtub?"

The moral of the story is: do not hide in dangerous places, do not go with strangers, and always stay close to your loved ones.

Suddenly, he heard a loud roar. He turned and saw a big, scary lion coming out of the bushes. The lion was hungry and wanted to eat Ollie. Ollie was terrified. He tried to run, but the lion was faster. He tried to hide, but the lion saw him. He tried to fight, but the lion was stronger.

"Help! Help!" Ollie cried, hoping his friends would hear him.

But his friends did not hear him. They were too far away, and they were too busy playing with each other. They had forgotten about Ollie.

Ollie thought he was doomed. He closed his eyes and waited for the lion to bite him.

But then, he heard a splash. He opened his eyes and saw a big wave of water coming towards him. The water hit the lion and knocked him off his feet. The lion was surprised and confused. He did not like water. He ran away, roaring in pain.

Ollie looked up and saw his friends. They had come back to save him. They had worked together to pour a lot of water from the river and make a big wave. They had used their tails, their paws, and their beaks.

"Ollie, are you okay?" they asked, running to him.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Ollie said, hugging them. "You are the best friends ever. I'm sorry I was so mean to you. I was selfish and greedy. I did not share with you. I did not play with you. I did not care about you. Can you forgive me?"

"Of course we can, Ollie," they said, smiling. "We are glad you are safe. We are your friends, and we love you. But you have to learn to be nice, to share, to play, and to care. That's what friends do."

Ollie nodded. He had learned his lesson. He realized that being kind and generous was more fun and more useful than being rude and stingy. He decided to change his ways and be a better friend.

From that day on, Ollie shared his rock, his fish, and his water with his friends. He played with them, talked to them, and helped them. He was happy and so were they. They had a lot of fun together by the river. And they never saw the lion again.

The end.

"Mom, can we have a balloon?" they asked.

"Look, there's one balloon left in the bag," Ben said. "It's green, my favorite color."

"Maybe the man will give it to us for free," Lily said. "Let's go ask him."

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play outside with their bikes. But they have only one bike. They always fight for the bike.

One day, Tim has an idea. He says to Sam, "I am more intelligent than you. I can ride the bike faster and better. Let me show you." Sam says, "No, you are not. I am more intelligent than you. I can ride the bike longer and farther. Let me show you."

They decide to have a race. They go to the park. They find a big tire. They put the tire on the ground. They say, "The first one who rides the bike around the tire three times wins. The other one has to give the bike to the winner."

They get ready. They say, "One, two, three, go!" They start to ride the bike. Tim is faster. He rides the bike around the tire once. Then he rides the bike around the tire twice. He is almost done. He thinks, "I am going to win. I am more intelligent than Sam."

But Sam is clever. He waits for Tim to come near the tire. Then he steps on the tire. The tire moves. Tim does not see it. He hits the tire. He falls off the bike. He hurts his knee. He cries.

Sam picks up the bike. He says, "I win. I am more intelligent than Tim. The bike is mine." He rides the bike away. He is happy.

"Oh no!" Tom said. "My truck is broken!"

"Oh no!" Anna said. "My doll is broken!"

"What happened here?" she asked. "Why are you crying?"

Tom and Anna told her what they had done. They said they were sorry and asked for her help.

Their aunt hugged them and said, "It's okay. I know you didn't mean to break your toys. But you should be more careful and kind with each other. Sharing is better than fighting. And being humble is better than being proud. Do you know what humble means?"

Tom and Anna shook their heads.

"Yes, auntie. We understand. We will be humble and share our toys. We will not fight again. We are sorry."

Tom and Anna smiled too. They liked their aunt's idea. They thanked her and said they loved her. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be humble and kind. And they learned that broken toys can be fixed with love.

"Let's set a tea party for our toys!" Mia said. "We can use the cups and plates from the kitchen."

"Okay!" Ben agreed. "But we have to be careful not to make a mess."

They went to the kitchen and got some cups and plates. They also got some cookies and juice. They brought everything to the living room and set a table on the floor. They put their toys on the chairs and gave them cups and plates.

"Hello, Mr. Bear, would you like some tea?" Mia asked in a polite voice.

"Yes, please, Miss Doll, thank you very much," Ben answered in a deep voice.

They pretended to pour tea and eat cookies. They also made some small talk.

"How are you today, Mr. Bear?" Mia asked.

"I'm fine, Miss Doll, how are you?" Ben replied.

"I'm good, thank you. But I have a question for you, Mr. Bear. Why are you so big and furry? You look very weird to me," Mia said.

Ben was surprised by Mia's question. He thought his bear was very nice and normal. He didn't like Mia calling his bear weird.

"My bear is not weird, he's just different. He's big and furry because he comes from a cold place where he needs to keep warm. He's also very soft and cuddly. I love my bear," Ben said.

Mia felt sorry for hurting Ben's feelings. She didn't mean to be rude. She just wanted to know more about his bear.

"I'm sorry, Ben, I didn't mean to be mean. I'm sure your bear is very nice and cuddly. I just never saw a bear like him before. He's very special," Mia said.

Ben smiled and forgave Mia. He realized that his bear was special, but so was Mia's doll. They were both different, but they were both fun to play with.

"Thank you, Mia, I'm sorry too. I like your doll too. She's very pretty and smart. She's also very special," Ben said.

They hugged and continued their tea party. They learned that being different is not weird, it's just interesting. They also learned to be kind and curious about each other's toys. They had a lot of fun and became better friends.

Sally pointed the magic finger at Tim's toy. The toy flew into the air and landed in Sally's hands. Tim was surprised and said, "How did you do that?" Sally smiled and said, "It's a magic finger!"

Now, Sally and Tim both had fun playing with the toy. They learned that sharing is better than fighting. The magic finger helped them become better friends.

Mia loved to learn new words from Blue, and they would talk for hours. They had many fun adventures together, and Mia was never lonely again.

Sam sighs and gets up. He shakes his head and his ears. He walks out of the stall and follows Tom and Lily. He is still sleepy, but he likes the children. He lets them pet him and give him some carrots. He even lets them ride on his back, but only for a little while.

"Thank you, Sam!" Tom and Lily say. "You are a good mule, and a good friend!"

Luckily, his friends saw him and came to help him. They carried him to a shady spot and gave him some water and salad. They also shared some of the salad with other animals who were hungry.

"Tom, you are a good friend, but you have to rest and eat too," said his friends. "You cannot help others if you are not well yourself."

Tom nodded and said, "You are right, I was silly. I wanted to deliver salad to everyone, but I did not think of myself. Thank you for helping me and sharing the salad. I learned my lesson. Next time, I will be more careful."

Tom felt better after resting and eating. He thanked his friends again and hugged them. Then he went home, feeling happy and grateful. He had delivered salad, but he had also received love and kindness. He realized that giving and receiving are both important.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear. They hugged it, dressed it, and told it stories. Sometimes they fought over who could hold it.

One day, they were playing with the teddy bear on the sofa. Tom wanted to make it dance, but Lily wanted to make it sleep. They pulled the teddy bear from each other, and it made a loud rip sound. The teddy bear's arm came off, and stuffing came out.

"Look what you did!" Tom cried. "You broke our teddy bear!"

"No, you did!" Lily shouted. "You pulled too hard!"

They both felt very sad and angry. They threw the teddy bear's arm and the stuffing on the floor. They did not want to play with each other anymore. They went to separate corners of the room and turned their backs.

The teddy bear lay on the sofa, with one arm missing. It felt very lonely and helpless. It wished Tom and Lily would stop fighting and fix it. It wanted to be hugged and loved again.

After a while, Tom and Lily heard their mom come home. She saw the mess in the living room and the teddy bear on the sofa. She asked them what happened.

"We broke our teddy bear," Tom and Lily said in low voices.

Mom picked up the teddy bear and the arm. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, I can fix it. But first, you need to fix something else. Can you guess what it is?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they did. They knew mom meant their friendship. They walked towards each other and hugged.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We're sorry, teddy bear."

Mom hugged them and said, "That's good. Now let's go to the kitchen and get some thread and a needle. We'll make your teddy bear as good as new."

Tom and Lily nodded and followed mom. They held the teddy bear and the arm in their hands. They felt happy and hopeful. They learned that toys can be fixed, but friends are more important.

Sam and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big black dog. The dog was unusual. It had one blue eye and one green eye. It wore a red collar with a bell.

"Wow, look at that dog!" Sam said. "It is so cool. I want to pet it."

"Me too," Lily said. "But maybe we should ask the owner first. Maybe the dog is not friendly."

Sam did not listen to Lily. He ran to the dog and tried to touch its fur. The dog did not like that. It barked and snapped at Sam. Sam was scared and ran away. He dropped his toy car on the ground.

"Sam, are you okay?" Lily asked. She followed Sam and hugged him.

"I'm okay," Sam said. "But the dog was mean. It tried to bite me."

"I'm sorry, Sam," Lily said. "But you should have listened to me. You should not pet a strange dog without asking. That is not safe."

Sam nodded. He looked at his toy car. The dog had picked it up and was chewing on it. The car was broken and dirty.

"I regret running to the dog," Sam said. "Now my toy car is ruined. It was my favorite."

"I regret it too," Lily said. "But maybe we can fix it. Or maybe we can get a new one. Come on, let's go home and tell our moms what happened. Maybe they can help us."

Sam and Lily held hands and walked home. They learned a lesson. They would not pet a strange dog again. They would be more careful and respectful. They hoped the dog would be okay too. They still thought it was unusual, but not cool.

Anna liked to run. She ran fast, faster than her friends. She ran in the park, in the yard, in the school. She felt happy when she ran. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She felt free.

But Anna had to mind her mom. Her mom said, "Don't run too fast, Anna. You might fall and hurt yourself. You might bump into someone or something. You have to be careful." Anna nodded, but she did not listen. She wanted to run faster and faster.

One day, Anna saw a big hill. She wanted to run up the hill and down the hill. She thought it would be fun. She thought it would be amazing. She did not mind her mom. She ran up the hill as fast as she could. She felt proud and excited.

But when she reached the top, she saw something that made her stop. She saw a big truck. The truck was coming down the hill. The truck was loud and scary. The truck was going very fast. Anna was afraid. She did not know what to do.

She tried to run back, but it was too late. The truck was too close. The truck hit Anna. Anna fell down. She felt pain. She felt blood. She felt sad. She wished she had minded her mom. She wished she had not run so fast. She wished she had been careful.

Lily and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. One day, they saw a big statue of a lion in the park. The lion looked strong and brave. Lily and Ben wanted to touch the lion.

They ran to the statue and climbed on it. They felt the lion's mane, nose, ears and tail. They pretended to roar like the lion. They had fun. But they did not see the sign that said "Do not climb on the statue".

Suddenly, they heard a loud crack. The lion's tail broke off. Lily and Ben were scared. They did not mean to break the lion. They jumped off the statue and ran away.

The next day, they came back to the park. They saw a man with a tool box and a ladder. He was fixing the lion's tail. He was using glue and tape to repair the statue. Lily and Ben felt sorry. They went to the man and said "We are sorry. We broke the lion's tail. We did not see the sign. We will not climb on the statue again."

The man smiled and said "It's okay. I know you did not mean to break the lion. You are good children to say sorry. The lion will be strong again soon. You can look at the statue, but please do not touch it. It is very old and fragile."

Lily and Ben nodded and said "Thank you. We will be careful. We like the lion. He is strong and brave."

They waved to the man and went to play in the park. They did not climb on the statue again. They learned to respect the lion and the man who repaired it.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big box. The box was from a new fridge that Mom and Dad bought. Ben and Lily pretended the box was a castle, a spaceship, or a cave.

One day, they wanted to make the box into a train. They cut out windows and doors with scissors. They drew wheels and smoke with crayons. They found a long rope and tied it to the front of the box. They were ready to go on a trip.

"Choo choo!" Ben said. He was the driver. He pulled the rope and made the box move. "All aboard!" he shouted.

Lily was the passenger. She climbed into the box with her teddy bear. She looked out of the window and waved. "Bye bye!" she said.

But the box was too small for Lily and her teddy bear. She could not fit inside. She tried to push and squeeze, but she was stuck. She felt sad and scared.

"Help!" she cried. "I can't fit!"

Ben heard Lily and stopped the box. He ran to the back and saw Lily's legs and arms sticking out of the box. He tried to pull her out, but she was too tight.

"Don't worry, Lily. I will help you." Ben said. He was a strong boy. He used all his strength and pulled harder. He pulled and pulled until Lily popped out of the box.

"Thank you, Ben. You are so strong." Lily said. She hugged Ben and her teddy bear. She was happy and safe.

"You're welcome, Lily. You are my sister. I love you." Ben said. He hugged Lily back. He was proud and kind.

They decided to make the box bigger. They found another box and taped them together. They made more windows and doors. They drew more wheels and smoke. They had a bigger and better train.

They climbed into the box and went on a trip. They saw many things and had fun. They told each other stories and laughed. They were the best friends.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with paper and crayons. They can print many things on the paper. They can print their names, shapes, animals, and flowers.

One day, they find a big book with many pictures of fruits. They see apples, bananas, oranges, and cherries. They like the cherries best. They are red and round and shiny.

"Let's print some cherries on the paper," Lily says.

"OK, how do we do that?" Tom asks.

Lily thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea. She picks up a clear cup and dips it in red paint. She presses the cup on the paper. It makes a circle. She does it again and again. She makes many circles.

"Look, these are the cherries," she says.

Tom likes the idea. He picks up a green crayon and draws a stem and a leaf on each circle. He makes the cherries look more real.

"Look, these are the stems and the leaves," he says.

They are happy with their work. They show their paper to their teacher. She smiles and praises them.

"Wow, you printed some beautiful cherries," she says. "You are very creative and clever."

Lila nodded and made a funny noise. She swung from a branch and reached out her hand. Ben grabbed it and they pretended to be monkeys together. They made faces, scratched their heads, and jumped up and down.

But then, the sky turned dark and it started to rain. Ben and Lila got wet and cold. Ben's mom came with an umbrella and said, "Ben, it's time to go home. You can see Lila another day."

Lila hugged Ben and said, "Bye, Ben. You are a good friend. Come back soon."

Ben and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of toys and they made a lot of noise. They did not like to clean up their toys. They left them all over the grass and the dirt.

One day, a snake came into the garden. It was long and green and had a forked tongue. It saw the toys and thought they were food. It slithered towards the box and opened its mouth.

"Look, Lily, a snake!" Ben shouted. He ran to the box and picked up a toy car. He wanted to scare the snake away.

"Ben, no!" Lily cried. She was afraid of the snake. She wanted to run inside the house.

But Ben did not listen. He threw the toy car at the snake. The snake was angry. It hissed and bit Ben on the arm. Ben screamed and dropped the car. He felt a sharp pain and saw blood.

Lily ran to Ben and hugged him. She called for their mom. Their mom came out and saw the snake and the bite. She was very scared. She took Ben and Lily inside and called the doctor.

The doctor came and gave Ben some medicine. He said Ben was lucky. The snake was not very poisonous. But he said Ben had to stay in bed for a few days. He also said Ben and Lily had to clean up their toys. He said the snake might come back if they left them messy.

Ben and Lily were sorry. They did not like the snake. They did not like the bite. They did not like the medicine. They did not like the bed. They wished they had cleaned up their toys. They learned their lesson. They never left their toys messy again.

Tommy liked to whistle. He whistled all the time. He whistled when he woke up, when he ate, when he played, and when he went to bed. He whistled loud and happy.

One day, Tommy found a shiny penny on the ground. He was eager to show it to his friend Billy. He ran to Billy's house, whistling all the way. He knocked on the door and waited.

Billy opened the door and saw Tommy holding the penny. He wanted the penny for himself. He said, "What do you have there, Tommy?"

Tommy smiled and said, "Look, Billy, I found a penny! It's so shiny and pretty!"

Billy snatched the penny from Tommy's hand and said, "It's mine now! You can't have it!"

Tommy was sad and angry. He tried to get the penny back, but Billy was stronger. He pushed Tommy away and slammed the door.

Tommy cried and whistled softly. He wished he had his penny back. He wished Billy was a better friend.

Then, he heard a voice behind him. It was Mrs. Jones, Billy's neighbor. She said, "Hello, Tommy. What's the matter?"

Tommy told her what happened. He showed her his empty hand and said, "Billy took my penny. He was mean to me."

Mrs. Jones frowned and said, "That's not nice of Billy. He should share with you. Come with me, Tommy. I have something for you."

She took Tommy to her house and gave him a cookie and a glass of milk. She also gave him a shiny quarter. She said, "This is for you, Tommy. You can buy something nice with it. And you can keep whistling. You have a lovely whistle."

Tommy smiled and thanked Mrs. Jones. He felt better. He whistled loud and happy again. He decided to buy a whistle with his quarter. He thought, "Maybe Billy will want to play with me if I have a whistle. Maybe he will give me my penny back. Maybe he will whistle with me."

Lily was a very enthusiastic girl who loved to explore. She liked to look at flowers, bugs, and rocks in her garden. One day, she found a strange bottle under a bush. It had a label that said "Shrink Juice". Lily was curious and wanted to try it.

She opened the bottle and drank a little sip. She felt a funny tingling in her body. She looked around and saw that everything was much bigger than before. She had shrunk! She was as small as a bug. She saw a big ant crawling towards her. She was scared and ran away.

She ran into a flower and hid inside. It was a purple lily. It smelled nice and was soft and cozy. She felt safe and calm. She wondered how she could get big again. She saw the bottle on the ground, far away. She wished she could reach it.

She heard a familiar voice calling her name. It was her mom. She was looking for her in the garden. Lily tried to shout, but her voice was too tiny. She hoped her mom would see the bottle and figure out what happened.

She saw her mom's face coming closer. She smiled and waved. Her mom saw her and gasped. She picked up the bottle and read the label. She understood what Lily had done. She poured some juice into a spoon and gave it to Lily. Lily drank it and felt the tingling again. She grew back to her normal size. She hugged her mom and said sorry. Her mom hugged her back and said it was okay. She was just glad she found her. She told her not to drink strange things again. Lily nodded and promised. She learned her lesson. She was happy to be big again. She still liked to explore, but she was more careful. She never forgot her adventure in the lily.

"But we are hungry," Lily said.

Ben was on the log. He looked around and pretended he was a captain. He saw a bird in the sky. He pointed at it and said, "Look, Lila, a bird! It is flying to the island. We should follow it!"

Lila was still on the ground. She was almost at the log. She heard Ben and looked up. She saw the bird too. It was pretty and colorful. She wanted to see it closer.

"OK, Ben, I'm coming!" she said. She reached the log and tried to climb on it.

But the log was slippery and wobbly. Lila slipped and fell. She hurt her knee. She cried.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she said. She was sad and scared.

Ben heard Lila and looked down. He saw her on the ground. She was crying. He felt sorry for her.

"Lila, are you OK?" he said. He jumped off the log and ran to her. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lila. I didn't mean to make you fall. It was my fault. I was too impatient. I should have waited for you."

Lila stopped crying. She looked at Ben. He was kind and gentle. She smiled and said, "It's OK, Ben. I'm not mad at you. You are my friend. But can you tell me a story to make me feel better?"

Ben nodded. He said, "Of course, Lila. I will tell you a story. A story about a bird and an island and a boat. A story that we can imagine together."

Lila and Ben sat on the ground. They held hands and listened to Ben's story. They forgot about the log and the pain. They were happy and curious. They dreamed of adventures and wonders.

The gorilla heard Ben and smiled. He made another noise, like "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!" He waved his hand at Ben and Lily. He was glad they were his friends. He was a proud and friendly gorilla.

He puts the ring in his pocket. He walks away. He looks for the owner.

Tom and Sam peek from behind the tree. They see the police leave. They are sad. They lost the ring. They say, "Sorry" to each other. They hug. They are friends again.

One day, a fox was walking in the forest. He saw a big lake with clear water. He was thirsty, so he went to drink. But when he looked at his reflection, he saw that his fur was dirty and messy.

"Oh no!" he said. "I need to clean myself. I want to look nice and shiny."

He jumped into the water and started to scrub his fur with his paws. He splashed and played and had fun. He felt happy and fresh.

But then he heard a voice behind him. It was a serious owl, who was sitting on a branch.

"Fox, what are you doing?" the owl asked. "You are wasting time and water. You should be hunting and learning, not playing and cleaning. You are a wild animal, not a pet."

The fox felt ashamed. He got out of the water and shook his fur.

"I'm sorry, owl," he said. "I just wanted to look nice and shiny. I didn't mean to be silly."

The owl looked at him with his big eyes.

"Fox, you don't need to look nice and shiny. You need to be smart and strong. That's what makes you a good fox. And you are not silly. You are curious and playful. That's what makes you a happy fox. But you also need to balance your fun and your work. That's what makes you a wise fox."

The fox nodded. He understood what the owl said.

"Thank you, owl," he said. "You are a good friend. You teach me a lot. Can I ask you a question?"

"Of course, fox," the owl said. "What do you want to know?"

The fox smiled.

"Can I clean myself again tomorrow?" he asked.

"Anna, come and see my bike!" he shouted as he ran to the garage. "It is red and shiny and has a bell!"

Anna followed him and saw his bike. She liked it too, but she noticed something was missing.

"Tom, where is your helmet?" she asked. "You need a helmet to be safe on your bike."

Tom frowned. He did not like helmets. They were big and heavy and made his head hot. He did not think he needed one.

"I don't need a helmet," he said. "I am very good at biking. I never fall or hit anything."

Anna shook her head. She wanted to explain to Tom why helmets were important, but he did not listen. He jumped on his bike and rode away.

"Wait for me, Tom!" she called. She put on her helmet and followed him on her bike.

Tom was having fun. He rode faster and faster, and rang his bell. He did not see the big rock on the road. He hit it with his front wheel and flew off his bike. He landed on the ground with a thud.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cried. He felt pain in his knee, his elbow, and his head.

Anna stopped her bike and ran to him. She saw blood on his knee and his elbow, and a bump on his head.

"Tom, are you okay?" she asked. She was scared and worried.

Tom looked at her and started to cry. He realized he had made a mistake. He wished he had worn a helmet.

"Anna, I'm sorry," he sobbed. "You were right. I should have worn a helmet. Can you explain to me why helmets are important?"

Anna hugged him and said, "Of course, Tom. Helmets are important because they protect your head from getting hurt. Your head is very important. It has your brain, your eyes, your ears, and your mouth. You need your head to think, to see, to hear, and to talk. If you hurt your head, you might not be able to do those things. That's why you should always wear a helmet when you ride your bike."

Tom nodded. He understood. He said, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. Can you help me get up and go home?"

Anna smiled and said, "Yes, Tom. I will help you. And next time, please wear your helmet."

They walked back to their bikes, holding hands. Tom learned a lesson that day. He decided to be more careful and listen to Anna. He also decided to get a new helmet, one that was red and shiny and matched his bike.

Sara and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to make up songs and sing them to each other. Sara had a red ball and Ben had a blue one. They threw the balls in the air and caught them, and sang:

"Red ball, blue ball, we love you all,
You make us happy when we play,
We toss you high and catch you low,
You are our friends every day."

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was their grumpy neighbor, Mr. Fox. He was burning some leaves in a big metal can. He did not like children or songs. He shouted at Sara and Ben:

"Stop that noise, you little brats!
You are hurting my ears with your silly songs!
Go away and leave me alone,
Or I will take your balls and throw them in the fire!"

Sara and Ben were scared. They did not want to lose their balls or make Mr. Fox angrier. They ran inside the house and told their mom what happened. Their mom was not happy. She said:

"That is not nice, Mr. Fox!
He has no right to threaten you or your balls!
He should be careful with fire, it can be dangerous!
I will go and talk to him and make him say sorry!"

She went outside and knocked on Mr. Fox's door. He opened it and looked at her with a sour face. She said:

"Hello, Mr. Fox. I am Sara and Ben's mom. I came to talk to you about your behavior. You should not yell at my children or try to take their balls. They were just playing and singing, they did not mean to bother you. And you should not burn leaves in a can, it is bad for the air and the plants. Why don't you join us for some cookies and milk, and we can be friends?"

Mr. Fox was surprised. He did not expect such a kind offer. He felt a little ashamed of his actions. He said:

"Well, I suppose I was a bit harsh. I am sorry, I am just grumpy because I have a headache and I don't sleep well. I don't like fire, either, but I have to get rid of these leaves somehow. Maybe I can use a rake instead. Cookies and milk sound nice, thank you. Can I bring my guitar? I like to play songs, too, sometimes."

Sara and Ben's mom smiled. She said:

"Of course, you can bring your guitar. We would love to hear your songs. Come on, let's go. Sara and Ben are waiting for you. Maybe you can teach them some new songs, and they can teach you some of theirs."

They walked together to Sara and Ben's house. Sara and Ben saw them and ran to greet them. They hugged Mr. Fox and said:

"We are sorry, Mr. Fox. We did not want to make you mad. We like your guitar. Can you play us a song?"

Mr. Fox smiled. He said:

"I am sorry, too, Sara and Ben. You did not make me mad. I was just grumpy. I like your balls. Can I play with you?"

"OK, Anna, but you have to give it back," Ben said, handing his rock to Anna.

Anna took the rock and looked at it. She liked how it sparkled in the sun. She wanted to keep it for herself.

"Anna, can I have my rock back?" Ben asked, holding out his hand.

"No, Ben, I want to keep it," Anna said, putting the rock in her bag.

"That's not fair, Anna, that's my rock!" Ben said, getting angry.

"Why is it your rock, Ben?" Anna asked, holding her bag tight.

"Because I found it first, Anna, and you have a big rock already," Ben said, trying to grab his rock.

"But I like your rock more, Ben, and you can have my big rock," Anna said, pushing Ben away.

"That's not a fair trade, Anna, my rock is smaller and prettier than your rock," Ben said, feeling sad.

Anna and Ben started to argue and shout. They forgot to have fun and be nice to each other. They did not question why they wanted the rocks so much. They only cared about their own rocks. They did not share or listen. They were not good friends.

The big fish followed the shrimp to the rock. He tried to poke his nose into the hole, but it was too small. He could not reach the shrimp.

"Come out, come out, little shrimp! I am hungry!" the big fish said.

The shrimp did not come out. He stayed in the hole and waited. He wished he had a friend to help him.

"Hey, big fish! Leave the shrimp alone! He is my friend!" the crab said. He came out of his hole and pinched the big fish's tail with his claw.

The big fish yelped and swam away. He did not like to be pinched. He decided to look for another snack.

The shrimp was happy. He thanked the crab for saving him.

"Thank you, crab! You are very brave and kind!" the shrimp said.

The crab smiled and invited the shrimp to his hole.

"You are welcome, shrimp! You are very jolly and fun! Do you want to be my friend?" the crab asked.

The shrimp nodded and sprang into the crab's hole. They became friends and played together. They sprang up and down in the water and made bubbles. They were happy.

Ben nodded and climbed on a chair. He took a mixer from the drawer. It was a shiny thing with two whisks. He plugged it in the wall and turned it on. The mixer made a loud noise and spun very fast. Ben held it over the bowl and watched the things become smooth and creamy.

"Good job, Ben!" Mom said. "You are a great helper. Now we need to add some chocolate chips and vanilla. Can you pour them in the bowl?"

Ben did as mom said. He poured the chocolate chips and the vanilla from the jars. They smelled very good. He watched mom stir them with a spoon. The cake batter was ready.

"Let's put it in the pan and bake it in the oven," Mom said. She poured the batter in a round pan and put it in the oven. She set the timer for 25 minutes. "Now we have to wait until the cake is done. Do you want to play with Rex while we wait?"

Ben smiled and ran to the living room. Rex was his dog. He was a big, brown, furry dog. He was very loyal and friendly. He always played with Ben and protected him. Ben threw a ball and Rex chased it. He brought it back and wagged his tail. Ben hugged him and said, "You are the best dog ever, Rex. I love you."

Rex licked Ben's face and barked. He loved Ben too. They played until the timer beeped. Ben and Rex ran back to the kitchen. The cake was done. It smelled very good. Mom took it out of the oven and let it cool. She said, "Ben, you and Rex did a great job. Dad will be very happy when he sees the cake. Do you want to help me decorate it?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, please. Can we write 'Happy Birthday Dad' on it?"

Mom said, "Of course. Let's do it together." She gave Ben a tube of icing and showed him how to write the letters. Ben and mom decorated the cake with icing, sprinkles and candles. They put it on a plate and covered it with a cloth. They waited for dad to come home.

When dad came home, he saw Ben, mom and Rex waiting for him. He said, "Hello, my family. What a nice surprise. What are you hiding under the cloth?"

Ben said, "It's a cake, dad. We made it for you. Happy birthday!"

Dad lifted the cloth and saw the cake. He was very happy and touched. He said, "Wow, what a beautiful cake. Thank you, Ben, mom and Rex. You are the best family ever. I love you."

He hugged them and kissed them. He blew out the candles and cut the cake. He gave a piece to Ben, mom and Rex. They ate the cake and enjoyed it. It was very yummy. They had a wonderful birthday party. They were very happy.

Anna and Ben feel sorry and sad. They say they are sorry and they love their mom. They say they will share and be nice. They say they will help their mom and clean their room. They say they will eat the oat porridge and water. But they hope their mom will change her mind and give them some cake too.

One day, a boy named Ben went to the zoo with his mom. He liked to see all the animals, but his favorite was the octopus. He wanted to touch it and play with it, but his mom said no.

"Octopus lives in the water, Ben. You can't touch it, or it will be sad and hurt. You can look at it and say hello, but that's all," his mom said.

Ben nodded, but he was not happy. He wanted to be friends with the octopus. He thought it was not fair that he could not touch it. He wondered what it felt like, and what it could do with its eight arms.

He waited until his mom was looking at another animal, and then he ran to the octopus tank. He climbed on a stool and reached his hand into the water. He felt something soft and slimy. He smiled and said, "Hi, octopus. I'm Ben. Do you want to play with me?"

The octopus did not say anything, but it wrapped its arms around Ben's hand and pulled him into the water. Ben screamed and tried to get away, but the octopus was too strong. He felt scared and sorry. He wished he had listened to his mom.

His mom heard his scream and ran to the tank. She saw Ben's head under the water and the octopus holding him. She shouted for help and grabbed a net. She tried to free Ben from the octopus, but it was not easy. The octopus did not want to let go of Ben. It thought he was a toy or a snack.

Finally, a zookeeper came and helped Ben's mom. He used a stick to poke the octopus and make it let go of Ben. He lifted Ben out of the water and gave him to his mom. Ben was wet and cold and crying. His mom hugged him and said, "Oh, Ben, are you okay? You scared me so much. Why did you do that? You know you can't touch the octopus. It's not an ordinary animal. It's dangerous and wild. You could have been hurt or drowned."

Ben nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was curious. I wanted to play with the octopus. But it was not fun. It was scary. I don't want to play with it anymore. I want to go home."

His mom nodded and said, "Okay, Ben. We'll go home. But you have to promise me that you'll never do that again. You have to respect the animals and follow the rules. They are not toys. They are living creatures. Do you understand?"

Ben nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I promise. I love you."

His mom said, "I love you too, Ben. Come on, let's go." She took his hand and walked away from the tank. The octopus watched them go and waved its arms. It was not angry or sad. It was just an octopus.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a small house with a big yard and many toys. One day, they saw a new house being built across the street. It was enormous, with many windows and doors and a tall roof.

"Wow, look at that house!" Tom said. "It is so big and shiny. I want to live there."

"Me too," Lily said. "Maybe they have a pool and a slide and a swing. And lots of candy and ice cream."

They ran across the street and peeked through the fence. They saw a man and a woman working on the house. They had hammers and nails and paint.

"Hello," Tom said. "Can we see your house?"

The man and the woman looked at them and smiled.

The woman shook her head.

"I'm sorry, kids, but this is not a place to play. It is dangerous. There are sharp things and loud things and messy things. You could get hurt or make a mess. You should go back to your house and play there."

Tom and Lily sighed. They were sad and disappointed. They wanted to see the enormous house and have fun.

"OK," Tom said. "Bye, nice people. Have a good day."

"Bye, kids," the woman said. "Be careful and have fun."

Tom and Lily walked back to their house. They looked at their toys and their yard. They were not so shiny and big as the new house. But they were still theirs and they loved them.

"Maybe our house is not so bad," Lily said. "We have each other and we have our toys. And we have mom and dad who love us."

"You're right," Tom said. "Our house is not enormous, but it is cozy and happy. And we can still dream about the new house and what it has inside."

They hugged each other and smiled. Then they played with their toys and had a good time. They forgot about the enormous house across the street. They were happy in their small house with their big yard.

But then Sara saw a big box on the table. It had a label that said "Do not open". Sara was curious. She wanted to know what was inside. She left her car and went to the box.

"Hey, where are you going?" Ben asked. He followed her to the table.

"I want to see what's in the box," Sara said. She tried to lift the lid.

"No, you can't!" Ben said. He grabbed her arm. "The label says 'Do not open'. That means it's not for us. It's for Mom and Dad. They will be mad if we open it."

Sara paused. She looked at Ben. She looked at the box. She looked at the label. She felt torn. She wanted to obey, but she also wanted to peek.

"Please, Ben, just a little look," Sara said. She pulled her arm away. "Maybe it's a surprise for us. Maybe it's a new toy or a cake or a puppy."

Ben shook his head. He was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. He did not want to spoil the surprise. He did not want to lose his car.

"No, Sara, no," Ben said. He pushed the box away. "Come on, let's go back to our cars. They are more fun than the box. Trust me."

Sara sighed. She looked at Ben. She looked at the box. She looked at the label. She made a choice. She left the box and went back to her car.

"Okay, Ben, you win," Sara said. She smiled at him. "Let's play with our cars. But maybe, just maybe, we can open the box later."

Jazz was a rare cat. He had black and white fur and blue eyes. He liked to play with balls and strings and mice. He also liked to number his toys. He had one ball, two strings, three mice, and so on. He was very proud of his toys and did not like to share.

One day, a new cat came to the house. Her name was Lily. She had orange fur and green eyes. She was very friendly and wanted to play with Jazz. But Jazz did not want to play with her. He said, "Go away! These are my toys. You can't have them. I numbered them all. They are mine!"

"Boys, why did you do this?" Mr. Lee asked. "This was my special bean plant. I grew it from a seed that my wife gave me before she died. She loved beans. This plant was a memory of her. Now it is dead, like her."

Ben went to the girl and said hello. He asked her if he could ride her bicycle. The girl smiled and said yes. She said she was bored and lonely. She had no one to play with. Her balloon was her only friend.

Ben thanked the girl and took her bicycle. He rode it around the park and had fun. He liked the basket and the horn. He waved to his mom and dad.

Then he saw the girl again. She was still sitting on the bench. She looked sad. Her balloon was gone. It had flown away in the wind. She had nothing to play with. She was empty.

Ben felt sorry for the girl. He stopped riding the bicycle and went back to her. He gave her back the bicycle and said thank you. He asked her if she wanted to play with him. He said he had a red bicycle with a bell. He said they could share and be friends.

The girl smiled and said yes. She thanked Ben and took his hand. They went to his bicycle and rode it together. They rang the bell and laughed. They were happy. They had each other. They were not empty.

"Look, Sam, a spot!" Tim says.

"Wow, it is pretty. Can we touch it?" Sam asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is paint. Mom says paint is wet and sticky. We should not touch it." Tim says.

"But I want to see how it feels. Maybe it is soft and smooth. Come on, Tim, let's touch it." Sam says.

Sam goes to the wall and reaches for the spot. Tim follows him. They touch the spot with their fingers. It is not paint. It is hot and burns. They scream and pull their fingers back. The spot is fire. It hurts.

Mom hears them and runs to the room. She sees the fire and the boys. She is angry and scared. She grabs a blanket and puts out the fire. She checks the boys' fingers. They are red and sore.

"What did you do? How did you start the fire? You could have burned the house down!" Mom yells.

"We saw a spot. We wanted to touch it. We didn't know it was fire." Tim says.

"You should have listened to me. I told you not to play with matches. They are not toys. They are dangerous. You could have hurt yourself and others. You are very naughty." Mom says.

She takes the boys to the bathroom and puts cold water on their fingers. She puts bandages on them. She tells them to sit on the couch and think about what they did. She is not proud of them. She is disappointed and sad.

The boys sit on the couch and cry. They are sorry and ashamed. They wish they had not touched the spot. They wish they had listened to Mom. They have learned a hard lesson. They will not play with fire again.

"Swim, Sara, swim!" Ben shouted. "Follow me!"

They swam as fast as they could. They left the reef and went to the shore. They were scared and tired.

Sara liked to draw with her pen. She had many colors of pen and she kept them in a box. She was very organized. She always put her pen back in the box when she was done.

One day, her brother Tom came to her room. He wanted to play with her pen. He saw a red pen and he took it from the box.

"Tom, give me back my pen!" Sara said. "That is my pen. You have your own pen."

"But I like your pen. It is bright and shiny. My pen is old and dull." Tom said. He did not want to give back the pen.

Sara was angry. She tried to grab the pen from Tom, but he was stronger. He ran away with the pen.

"Tom, that is not nice. You have to share. You have to let me use my pen." Sara said. She followed Tom.

Tom ran to the living room. He saw a big white paper on the table. He wanted to draw on the paper with the red pen.

"Tom, stop! That is not your paper. That is Mom's paper. She needs it for work." Sara said. She caught up with Tom.

But Tom did not listen. He started to draw on the paper with the red pen. He made big circles and lines and dots.

"Tom, you are making a mess. You are ruining Mom's paper. She will be very mad." Sara said. She tried to take the pen from Tom, but he held it tight.

"Go away, Sara. I am having fun. I am making art." Tom said. He did not care about Mom's paper.

Sara was sad. She did not know what to do. She wanted her pen back. She wanted to save Mom's paper. She needed help.

She saw Dad coming from the kitchen. She ran to him and told him what Tom did.

"Dad, Tom took my pen and he is drawing on Mom's paper. He will not let me have my pen. He will not stop. He is being bad. Please help me." Sara said.

Dad looked at the living room. He saw Tom and the paper. He saw the red pen. He was not happy.

"Tom, what are you doing? That is not your pen. That is not your paper. That is Sara's pen and Mom's paper. You have to give back the pen and say sorry. You have to be nice and share." Dad said.

He went to the living room and took the pen from Tom. He gave it back to Sara. He looked at the paper. It was full of red marks.

"Tom, you made a big mistake. You ruined Mom's paper. She will be very upset. You have to apologize and help me fix it." Dad said.

Tom realized he was wrong. He felt sorry. He did not mean to hurt Sara and Mom.

"I am sorry, Sara. I am sorry, Dad. I am sorry, Mom. I was selfish and careless. I should have let you use your pen. I should have respected your paper. Can I help you fix it?" Tom said.

Sara and Dad nodded. They forgave Tom. They hugged him.

"Thank you, Tom. We love you. But you have to be more careful and respectful. You have to ask before you take something. You have to listen when someone says no. You have to be more organized and clean up your mess." Sara and Dad said.

Tom agreed. He learned his lesson. He helped Sara and Dad find a new paper for Mom. He helped them clean up the living room. He put his pen back in his box. He played nicely with Sara and her pen. They all had fun.

She helped them clean up the mess and gave them some new notebooks. She said, "You can draw and write new things in your new notebooks. And you can keep them in a safe place where Spot can't reach them. And you can still love Spot, because he is a good dog who made a mistake."

One day, they decided to have a race with their cars. They made a track with books and boxes and tape. They each chose their favorite car and put it on the start line. Tom had a red car that made a lot of noise. Sam had a blue car that was very shiny.

"Ready, set, go!" Tom shouted, and pressed a button on his car. The car roared and moved forward, but not very fast. Sam pressed a button on his car, and it zoomed ahead, leaving Tom behind.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Tom cried. "Your car is fake! It has a battery inside! My car is real! It has a motor and gas!"

Sam laughed and said, "No, your car is fake! It has a speaker inside! It only makes noise, but it has no speed! My car is real! It has a motor and wheels!"

They argued and argued, and did not notice that their cars had crashed into each other. The cars broke into pieces and stopped working. Tom and Sam were very sad and angry. They blamed each other for ruining their cars.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken cars and the angry brothers. She shook her head and said, "Boys, boys, what have you done? You have destroyed your cars and hurt your feelings. It does not matter if your cars are real or fake, big or loud, small or fast. What matters is that you share and play nicely with each other. Cars are just toys, but brothers are forever. Can you say sorry and hug each other?"

Tom and Sam looked at each other and felt ashamed. They realized that their mom was right. They said sorry and hugged each other. They picked up the pieces of their cars and put them in a box. They decided to play with something else, something that they both liked. They learned that being kind and fair is more important than being right and winning.

"Okay, mom!" Ben and Lily said. They ran to the door, but then they stopped. They looked at their room and saw how messy it was. They knew their mom would not be happy.

"Uh-oh, we have to restore our room," Ben said. "Restore means to make it nice and clean again."

"But how?" Lily asked. "There are so many things to put away. And we are hungry."

Ben thought for a moment. He had an idea. He smiled and said, "I know! Let's make it a game. We can pretend we are spies and we have to hide all the clues before the bad guys come. We can use this basket as our secret base and put everything inside. And we can make funny noises like beep, beep, boop, boop, as we do it."

Lily liked Ben's idea. She nodded and said, "That sounds fun! Let's do it!"

They grabbed the basket and started to restore their room. They picked up their toys and books and games and put them in the basket. They made funny noises and pretended to be spies. They had fun, but they also worked fast. Soon, their room was nice and clean again.

"Good job, spies!" Ben said. "We did it! We restored our room!"

"Yay, we did it!" Lily said. "Now let's go eat lunch!"

They ran downstairs, holding the basket. Their mom was waiting for them in the kitchen. She saw their room and smiled. She was happy.

"Wow, you restored your room very well!" she said. "You are very good spies. And very good kids. I'm proud of you."

"Thank you, mom!" Ben and Lily said. They hugged their mom and put the basket away. Then they sat down and ate their lunch. They were hungry, but they were also happy. They had a lot of fun, and they also learned a new word: restore.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to run and jump and chase each other. They saw a big green plant with many sharp points. It was a cactus.

"Look, Ben, a cactus!" Lily said. "Can we touch it?"

"No, Lily, it will hurt you. Mom said so. It has needles." Ben said.

But Lily was curious. She wanted to see how the cactus felt. She reached out her hand and touched the cactus. Ouch! It pricked her finger. She cried out in pain.

"See, Lily, I told you. Are you okay?" Ben asked.

Lily looked at her finger. It had a small drop of red on it. It was blood. She felt sad and ashamed. She had not listened to Ben or Mom. She had been naughty.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry, Mom. I was bad. The cactus hurt me." Lily said.

Ben hugged Lily. He felt sorry for her. He knew she had learned her lesson.

"It's okay, Lily. Don't cry. I will help you. Let's go to Mom. She will make it better." Ben said.

They ran to Mom. Mom saw Lily's finger and knew what had happened. She cleaned it and put a band-aid on it. She kissed Lily and Ben.

"Thank you, Mom. I love you." Lily said.

"I love you too, Lily. And you, Ben. You are a good brother. But next time, please be careful. The cactus is not a toy. It can hurt you." Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They had learned their lesson. They never touched the cactus again.

"Look, I can fly!" Lily said. She climbed on the sofa and jumped off. She landed on the floor with a thud.

"Wow, you are great!" Ben said. He wanted to try too. He climbed on the sofa and jumped off. But he did not land on the floor. He landed on the television.

CRASH!

The television broke. The screen was cracked and the sound was gone. Lily and Ben were scared. They knew Mom and Dad would be angry.

"Uh-oh, what did we do?" Lily said.

"We broke the television!" Ben said.

They heard Mom and Dad coming. They hid behind the sofa. They hoped Mom and Dad would not see the broken television. They hoped Mom and Dad would not be mad. They hoped they could still be superheroes.

One day, she had a new friend over. His name was Max. He liked to play with cars and trains. He saw Lily's box of thread and was curious.

"What is this?" he asked, picking up a spool of red thread.

"That is thread," Lily said. "I use it to sew."

"Sew? What is sew?" Max asked.

"Sew is when you join pieces of cloth together with a needle and thread. Like this," Lily said, showing him a doll she had made.

"Wow, that is cool," Max said. "Can you teach me how to sew?"

Lily was enthusiastic. She liked to share her hobby with others. She nodded and smiled.

"Sure, I can teach you. Come, I will introduce you to my needle and thread. They are my friends. We can make something together," she said.

Max followed her to the table. He was eager to learn. He liked to try new things. He hoped he could make something as nice as Lily's doll. He thought Lily was a good friend.

Lily is organized. She has a book with pictures of animals and colors. She reads the book every night before bed. She knows all the names and sounds of the animals. She knows all the colors of the rainbow.

Sam is not organized. He does not have a book with pictures of animals and colors. He likes to watch TV and play games. He does not read or study. He does not know many names or sounds of the animals. He does not know many colors.

Sam is sad. He answers many questions wrong. He does not pass the quiz. He gets a sad face from the teacher.

Lily sees Sam crying. She goes to him.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big dog with a long tail and a red collar. The dog runs to them and wags its tail. Anna likes dogs and wants to pet it, but Ben is scared of dogs and hides behind a tree.

"Hello, doggy! You are so cute and fluffy!" Anna says. She reaches out her hand and the dog licks it. Anna giggles and strokes the dog's fur. The dog is happy and jumps around Anna.

"Anna, come here! That dog is bad! It might bite you!" Ben shouts. He is still behind the tree and does not want to come out.

"No, Ben, the dog is good! It is harmless and friendly! See, it is smiling at me!" Anna says. She points to the dog's mouth, which is open and showing its teeth. Anna thinks the dog is smiling, but Ben thinks the dog is snarling.

"Anna, please, ignore the dog and come to me! I don't like it!" Ben begs. He is crying and shaking.

"Ben, don't be silly! The dog is not scary! It just wants to play!" Anna says. She ignores Ben and keeps playing with the dog. She throws a stick and the dog fetches it. Anna and the dog have fun, but Ben is sad and lonely.

Lily and Anna are sisters. Lily is big and Anna is little. They like to play with dolls and books. But sometimes they fight over toys.

One day, Lily sees a new doll in Anna's room. She wants to play with it. She takes the doll from Anna's bed. Anna sees Lily and gets angry.

"Give me back my doll!" Anna shouts. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Lily says. "You have too many dolls!"

They pull the doll from each other. They struggle and tug. The doll's hair and dress get messy.

"Stop it, stop it!" their mom says. She comes into the room. She sees the doll and the sisters. She is not happy.

"Look what you did to the doll!" she says. "You are both naughty! You need to share and be kind to each other!"

She takes the doll from them. She puts it on a shelf. She tells them to say sorry and hug.

Lily and Anna feel bad. They don't like to make mom angry. They don't like to hurt the doll. They say sorry and hug.

They decide to play with books instead. They read and laugh. They are happy sisters again.

One day, a big lion saw a small rabbit in the grass. The lion was hungry and wanted to eat the rabbit for meat. He ran after the rabbit and roared, "I will catch you and make you my meat!"

The rabbit was very scared and ran as fast as he could. He saw a hole in the ground and jumped in. The lion could not fit in the hole and was angry. He said, "Come out, you coward! You are not fair! You should let me eat you!"

The rabbit said, "No, you are not fair! You are big and strong and I am small and weak. You have many other animals to eat, but I have only grass and carrots. Why do you want to eat me?"

The lion said, "Because I am the king of the jungle and I can do what I want. You are just a snack for me."

The rabbit said, "That is not a good reason. You should be kind and share with others. You should not scare and hurt those who are smaller than you. That is not how a king should act."

The lion thought about what the rabbit said. He realized that he was being greedy and mean. He said, "You are right, little rabbit. I am sorry for scaring you and trying to eat you. You are brave and smart. You can come out of the hole and I will not harm you."

The rabbit came out of the hole and thanked the lion. The lion said, "You are welcome, little rabbit. From now on, I will be a better king and a better friend. I will not scare or eat you or any other animal who is not fair meat for me."

The rabbit and the lion smiled and went their separate ways. They learned a lesson that day: it is not fair to scare or hurt others who are different from you. It is better to be kind and share with others. That is how you make friends and peace.

Lily and Ben love to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They like to make them speed on the floor and pretend they are racing.

One day, they find a new car in their toy box. It is shiny and red, and it has a button on the side. Lily presses the button and the car makes a loud noise. It sounds like music, but very fast and noisy.

"Wow, what a cool car!" Ben says. "Can I try it?"

"Sure, here you go," Lily says. She gives the car to Ben and he presses the button. The car zooms across the floor and bumps into the wall.

"Ouch, that hurt!" the car says in a voice. Lily and Ben are surprised. They did not know the car could talk.

"Sorry, car, are you okay?" Lily asks.

"I'm okay, but I don't like to speed so much. It makes me dizzy and scared," the car says.

"Then why do you make such loud music?" Ben asks.

"That's not music, that's my alarm. I make it when I'm in danger or need help," the car says.

"Oh, we didn't know that. We thought you liked to speed and make music," Lily says.

"No, I like to be gentle and quiet. I like to listen to soft music and sing along. Do you want to hear me sing?" the car asks.

"Yes, please, we would love to hear you sing," Lily and Ben say.

The car presses a different button and starts to sing a sweet song. It sounds like a lullaby. Lily and Ben smile and sing along. They hug the car and say they are sorry for making it speed. They promise to be gentle and kind to it.

The car is happy and says it likes them too. They become friends and play together. They learn to share and respect each other's preferences. They have fun with their toy cars, but they also enjoy listening to music and singing.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They named him Bob.

"Bob is so cool!" Lily said. "He is our new friend."

"Yes, he is!" Sam agreed. "He is very fun to play with."

They hugged Bob and took a picture with him. They were very happy.

But the next day, the sun was very bright and warm. Lily and Sam went outside to see Bob. But Bob was not the same. He was smaller and wet. His hat and scarf were on the ground. His nose and eyes were gone.

"Oh no!" Lily cried. "Bob is melting!"

"Bob is not fun anymore!" Sam said. "He is not available to play with!"

They were very sad. They wanted Bob to stay with them.

Then they saw a bird on a tree. The bird was singing a pretty song. It had bright feathers and a shiny beak. It looked at them and smiled.

"Hello, Lily and Sam!" the bird said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They wiped their tears and smiled.

"Hello, bird!" they said. "Yes, we want to play with you!"

They ran to the tree and climbed on a branch. They talked and laughed with the bird. They learned its name and its favorite food. They sang along with its song. They had a lot of fun.

They forgot about Bob and the snow. They made a new friend.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes things change and we lose what we love, but we can always find new friends and new fun if we are open and kind.

"Queen Lily, you are so pretty and kind," said King Ben. "You can do magic with your wand."

"Thank you, King Ben. You are so brave and strong," said Queen Lily. "You can protect our castle from the bad guys."

They were having fun until they saw a big dog. The dog was not mean, but he was very curious. He ran to the box and sniffed it. He wanted to play with Lily and Ben.

"Go away, dog!" said Ben. "This is our castle. You are not a bad guy, but you are not a friend either."

But the dog did not listen. He jumped on the box and made it fall. He licked Lily and Ben with his wet tongue. He wagged his tail and barked.

"Help, help!" said Lily. "The dog is ruining our game. He is making us dirty and wet."

Ben grabbed his wand and waved it at the dog. He hoped it would work. He said, "Dog, dog, go away. Leave us alone. We want to play."

But the wand did not work. It was only a stick. The dog thought it was a toy. He took it from Ben and ran away.

Lily and Ben were sad. They lost their castle, their wand, and their game. They looked at each other. They were covered in mud and saliva.

"Let's go inside," said Lily. "We need to wipe ourselves. We are not a queen and a king anymore. We are just a mess."

"OK," said Ben. "But we can play again tomorrow. Maybe we can find a new wand. And a new castle. And a new game."

Their dad sighed. He looked at Tom and Lily. He saw their sad faces. He felt sorry for them. He said, "I'm sorry, too. I know you were trying to be nice. But you have to ask me before you decorate my things. My hat is important to me. It helps me catch fish. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "We understand, dad. We won't do it again. Can we hug you?"

Their dad smiled. He said, "Of course, you can. I love you, too. Come here and give me a hug."

Tom and Lily ran to their dad and hugged him. They were happy again. They learned a lesson. They decided to decorate their own hats instead. They made them very impressive, too.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. It sounded like a monster or a giant. They looked at each other and felt scared. They panicked and hugged each other.

"What is that?" Lily whispered.

"I don't know," Tom whispered back. "Maybe it's a dragon or a dinosaur."

They heard the noise again. It was louder and closer. They panicked more and screamed.

"Help! Help! Mom! Dad!"

Their mom and dad heard them and ran to their room. They opened the door and turned on the light. They saw Lily and Tom in their bed, shaking and crying.

"What's wrong, sweeties?" their mom asked.

"There's a monster outside!" Lily said.

"A dragon or a dinosaur!" Tom said.

Their dad looked out the window and smiled. He saw a big truck with a crane. It was moving a tree from their neighbor's yard.

"It's not a monster, kids. It's just a truck. It's moving a tree. See?" he said.

He lifted Lily and Tom out of their bed and carried them to the window. He showed them the truck and the tree. They saw the lights and the workers. They realized it was not scary. It was interesting.

"Oh," Lily said.

"Wow," Tom said.

They calmed down and stopped crying. They smiled and hugged their mom and dad.

"Sorry, we panicked," Lily said.

"We thought it was a monster," Tom said.

"It's okay, sweeties. You were just scared. It's normal to panic sometimes. But you're safe now. And you have a very original bed. It's like a castle or a spaceship," their mom said.

"Can we go back to our bed?" Lily asked.

"Can we read another story?" Tom asked.

"Sure, why not. But only one more. Then you have to sleep. It's late," their dad said.

He put them back in their bed and tucked them in. He gave them their flashlight and their book. He kissed them good night and turned off the light.

"Good night, Lily. Good night, Tom. We love you," he said.

"Good night, mom. Good night, dad. We love you too," they said.

They snuggled in their bed and read another story. They forgot about the noise and the truck. They felt happy and cozy. They fell asleep and dreamed of adventures.
