"Let's go, Ben!" Mia said. "Maybe there are animals or treasures in the pipe!"

"OK, Mia!" Ben said. "But be careful. The pipe might be fragile and break."

They ran to the hill and climbed on the pipe. They looked inside and saw nothing but dirt and rocks. They were disappointed.

"Aw, this is boring!" Mia said. "Let's go back and play with the ball."

"Wait, Mia!" Ben said. "Look over there! I see something shiny!"

He pointed to a small pond near the hill. In the pond, there was a duck with a silver ring around its neck. The duck was swimming and quacking happily.

"Wow, that's a pretty duck!" Mia said. "Maybe the ring is a treasure!"

"Let's go and say hello to the duck!" Ben said. "Maybe it will let us touch the ring!"

They slid down the pipe and ran to the pond. They waved to the duck and called out.

"Hello, duck! You are so pretty! Can we see your ring?"

The duck saw them and quacked louder. It swam to the edge of the pond and shook its head.

"No, no, no!" the duck said. "This is my ring! It is very special to me! You can't have it!"

Ben and Mia were surprised. They did not know that ducks could talk.

"Sorry, duck!" Ben said. "We didn't mean to upset you. We just wanted to look at your ring. It is very shiny and beautiful."

"Yes, it is!" the duck said. "My friend gave it to me. He is a fairy. He lives in the pipe. He is very kind and magical. He can make anything he wants with his wand."

"Really?" Mia said. "That's amazing! Can we meet your friend? Maybe he can show us some magic!"

The duck thought for a moment. Then it nodded.

"OK, OK, OK!" the duck said. "But you have to be very nice and polite. And you have to promise not to touch his wand. It is very fragile and powerful. If you break it, he will be very sad and angry."

Ben and Mia agreed. They followed the duck to the pipe. They climbed on it again and looked inside. They saw a small door at the end of the pipe. The duck knocked on the door and said.

"Hello, fairy! It's me, your friend, the duck! I have some visitors for you. They want to see your magic. Can we come in?"

The door opened and a fairy came out. He had wings and a wand. He smiled and said.

"Hello, duck! Hello, visitors! I'm happy to see you. Come in, come in! I have some magic to show you!"

The boy listened closer and realised the whispers were coming from inside the ticket machine. He moved closer and the whispers grew louder.

So Jack and his mom went back to the store and bought the kitten food and a toy mouse. Jack was so happy. He carried the kitten home and gave it a nice warm bed.

Jack and the kitten had so much fun together. They played with the toy mouse and chased each other around the house. Sometimes, Jack put the kitten on his shoulders and ran around the garden.

Suddenly, the telephone rang. Mary was excited and ran to answer it. Daddy said she could answer it, but only if she said hello with her best voice. So Mary said hello in her best voice.

On the other end of the telephone, Grandma said hello. Grandma said she was so proud of Mary for saying hello in such a nice voice. Grandma was so excited to hear Mary's voice that she sent her a special gift to say thank you.

The next day, when it came, Mary was so excited. She rushed to the door to see what Grandma had sent her. Mary was so proud when she saw the special gift. She had never had such a special present before!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was curious about the world and wanted to know and learn more. One day, he asked his parents to explain a pond. His parents said a pond is a big, cold place full of water. He was so excited to go for a visit and see the pond. When they got there, it was even bigger than the little boy thought. He could see lots of animals swimming in the cold water and it was so exciting. He asked his parents what all the animals were. His parents were happy to explain the different animals and the little boy was filled with joy and wonder. He had lots of fun at the pond, always learning more and more.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He had a big television in his room. But he was very selfish, and he wouldn't share it with anyone. He would watch it all day long by himself.

One day, his mom and dad told him he had to share the television. Jack didn't want to, but he knew he had to. So he split the television in two - one for him, and one for anyone else who wanted to watch it.

Jack still watched the television a lot, but he started to learn how to share it with his family. He stopped being so selfish and he remembered what his mom and dad had said about sharing. 

Now Jack and his family get to watch the television together and have a lot of fun. They don't have to split it anymore, because they all know how to share.
